entries.evidence: Followed #77's lead a second time: this run's failed icalls were 0x00000001, 0x00000000 and 0x00216F70; sub_00216F70 did not exist in the tree and dry-ran to a clean 6-byte extent. Seeded (seed_list.json now 1164). RESULT, deterministic 2 of 2: reached 99 -> 101, callsites 382 -> 357, heap_allocs 25 -> 23, failed_icalls 3 -> 5, kernel_calls unchanged at 44. Set diff: 4 gained (sub_001EB200, sub_001EB250, sub_00216F70, sub_00217FD0), 2 lost (sub_0022E0C0, sub_00233490) - and the two lost are NOT the abandoned-failure-path pattern that justified #76's losses, they are from the band #77 had just won. WHY IT IS KEPT ANYWAY: I checked the lifted body rather than trusting the extent, because a 6-byte auto-detected function is exactly the shape of a truncated fragment and the 2026-08-05 regression came from unverified fragments. recomp_seed.c:119077 reads in full `void sub_00216F70(void) { loc_00216F70: eax = MEM32(0x5BC274); esp += 4; return; /* ret */ }` - two instructions, `mov eax, [0x5BC274]` then `ret`, exactly 6 bytes, a COMPLETE getter returning the same global singleton sub_00221F50 reads. It is not truncated. A faithful lift that changes downstream behaviour is REVEALING a bug elsewhere, not causing one: previously the ICALL failed and RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE handed back eax = 0, so the engine was branching on a fake null. Reverting correct code to keep a nicer number would be the wrong trade. The callsites drop is recorded as an open question, not explained away. THE LEAD IS NOW EXHAUSTED: this run's failed icall targets are 0x00000001, 0x00000000, 0x00000010, 0xFFFFFFFF and 0x0000000B - all garbage pointers, no plausible code addresses left, so the cheap #77 method has no more candidates at this wall. THE SYSTEMIC FINDING, which is the real value of this step: esp is ABOVE the top of the stack in BOTH recent crashes. The stack region is 0x00780000-0x00F80000 and grows DOWN, so a valid esp is always below 0x00F80000. Measured esp = 0x00F80120 at sub_0022C2A0 + 0x279, and esp = 0x00F8031C at sub_00204800 + 0x24D - past the top by 0x120 and 0x31C, and getting worse. That is an UNDERFLOW (too many pops), the opposite direction from the 40-byte leak of #70/#71. NOTE triage labels these "heap" because 0x00F80000 is XBOX_HEAP_BASE, which is misleading - it is the stack having run off its top, not a heap pointer. THE TOOL FOR THIS ALREADY EXISTS AND HAS NEVER BEEN RUN: recomp_types.h defines RECOMP_CHECK_ABI, which wraps every direct call to verify ebx/esi/edi are restored (recomp_abi_violation) and to flag esp leaving RECOMP_ESP_LO 0x00700000 .. RECOMP_ESP_HI 0x00F80000, NAMING THE CALLEE (recomp_esp_escape). CMakeLists.txt:28 exposes it as an option. Configured and building now via `cmake -S . -B build_abi -DRECOMP_CHECK_ABI=ON` in a SEPARATE directory so the normal build is untouched. This is an automated detector for the exact bug class that has dominated 2026-08-07 - #38, #52, #69, #71 were all found by hand, one probe pair at a time. CURRENT WALL: write at Xbox VA 0xFFFFFF03 in sub_00204800 + 0x24D (recomp_0015.c ~17954), esi = -1, eax = 0xFFFFFF00, ebx = 0x65637275 which is ASCII "urce" so string data is in a register. Backtrace sub_001A1C97 -> sub_0019F22E -> sub_0019F196 -> sub_001A1C23 -> sub_00011E40 -> sub_00239E50 -> sub_002392E0 -> sub_002155B0 -> sub_0020DA95 -> sub_0020A360 -> sub_00204800.

entries.claim: RECOMP_CHECK_ABI now runs and works - 23 distinct callee-save violations captured to tools_data/abi_violations.txt. But it did NOT fire on esp, which is the important NEGATIVE result: the stack underflow does not happen across any DIRECT call, so it must be an ICALL or a tail-jump chain. The violation list needs triage, not blind trust - several are string-copy code where esi/edi are legitimately consumed
entries.evidence: FIRST EVER RUN of RECOMP_CHECK_ABI on this project - the mode has existed in recomp_types.h and CMakeLists.txt:28 the whole time and nobody had used it. Built into a SEPARATE directory so the normal build is untouched: `cmake -S . -B build_abi -DRECOMP_CHECK_ABI=ON` then `cmake --build build_abi --config Release`, clean apart from four pre-existing C4700 uninitialised-local warnings in recomp_0017.c (mm2, mm3, ebp x2 - worth a separate look). VALIDITY CHECK FIRST: the instrumented binary reports "distinct=101" and "callsites=357", identical to the normal build, and crashes the same way (0xC0000005). So the checking is behaviour-neutral and its observations describe the real run, not a perturbed one. RESULT 1 - 23 distinct callee-save violations, saved to tools_data/abi_violations.txt. Format is "[ABI] sub_X did not restore:  ebx BEFORE->AFTER  esi ...  edi ...". Examples: sub_003432E3 loses all three; sub_00204020 loses esi and edi; sub_0021ACD0 loses all three; sub_002235D0, sub_00209650, sub_001EA600, sub_002096B0, sub_0020E520, sub_002226E0, sub_001EA730, sub_001EA770, sub_002041D0, sub_001EA6B0, sub_00227F90, sub_00236500, sub_00342AA0, sub_001183A0 and a run of sub_00023440/70/80/4C0/4E0/500. DO NOT TREAT THIS AS A BUG LIST - IT NEEDS TRIAGE. Several entries show ASCII in the "after" values: 0x6769203A = ": ig", 0x624F6174 = "taOb", 0x654D6769 = "igMe", 0x65726854 = "Thre", 0x45747865 = "extE", 0x0163656A = "jec". Those are string bytes being moved, i.e. rep movsd / rep stosd style copies where esi and edi are the source and destination pointers and are legitimately consumed. A function whose whole job is a memory copy will trip this check without being wrong. The sub_00023440-sub_00023500 cluster all showing the identical "edi 0044B0A4->00000001" also smells like one CRT-ish helper family rather than six independent bugs. Triage by asking whether the caller actually depends on the register afterwards - that is what made #37/#38/#52/#69 real. RESULT 2, AND THE MORE USEFUL ONE - A NEGATIVE: recomp_esp_escape NEVER FIRED. Zero esp reports in the whole run. The check is `if ((g_esp < 0x00700000 || g_esp > 0x00F80000) && (esp_before >= 0x00700000 && esp_before <= 0x00F80000)) recomp_esp_escape(...)`, so it catches the TRANSITION out of range across a direct call. The crash has esp = 0x00F8031C, which IS out of range (initial esp is 0x00F7FFF0 per the startup banner "Stack: 8192 KB at Xbox VA 0x00780000 (ESP = 0x00F7FFF0)", so the stack has been popped 0x32C bytes more than pushed). Since no direct call was observed carrying esp out of range, THE OVER-POP IS NOT IN A DIRECT CALL. That leaves: an ICALL (RECOMP_ICALL / RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE / RECOMP_ITAIL are NOT wrapped by RECOMP_ABI_CALL and so are unchecked), a tail-jump fragment chain, or arithmetic inside one function. This rules out a large search space for one build. NEXT STEP, and it is cheap: extend the esp range check into RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE and RECOMP_ITAIL, where the target address is already in hand and can be printed - that would name the over-popping indirect callee the same way recomp_esp_escape names a direct one. Given #71 found TWO generic `g_esp += 4` stubs whose real epilogues owed 12 and 36 bytes, an indirect call landing on a stub that pops the wrong amount is exactly the expected shape, and safe_stub still reads 8 every run. State unchanged: 44 kernel calls / 5 failed icalls / 23 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, reached 101, callsites 357, deterministic.

entries.claim: CORRECTION to #79: its central negative - "recomp_esp_escape NEVER FIRED, so the over-pop is not in a direct call" - is WRONG. It did fire. My grep was truncated at 20 lines and the 40+ `[KERNEL] ... esp=` lines crowded the `[ESP]` report out of view. The first and biggest escape IS a direct call: sub_00227F90, delta +180
entries.evidence: HOW I GOT IT WRONG, recorded because the method failure matters more than the fact. To look for esp reports in the first RECOMP_CHECK_ABI run I ran `Select-String -Pattern "esp" | Where-Object { $_.Line -notmatch "^\[ABI\]" } | Select-Object -First 20`. Every one of the first 20 matches was a `[KERNEL] #N: ordinal X esp=0x00F7FFxx` progress line - there are 40+ of them and they appear early in the log. The `[ESP]` report sits after them and was cut off by `-First 20`. I then reported "ZERO esp reports" as a finding and built ledger #79's whole conclusion on it. RECOMP_ABI_CALL was not modified between the two builds, so that report was present in the first run too and I simply did not see it. This is the same class of mistake as the shared probe counter that hid the interesting site three times today: a display limit silently truncating evidence, then a confident conclusion drawn from the truncated view. Do not conclude "X never happens" from a head-limited grep - count the matches first, or grep for the exact tag. WHAT THE FULL RESULT ACTUALLY IS, from the rebuilt binary (coverage identical at distinct=101 / callsites=357, so the instrumentation remains behaviour-neutral and both runs describe the same execution), four escapes in firing order: (1) "[ESP] sub_00227F90 left esp outside the stack: 00F7FF54 -> 00F80008 (delta +180)" - NO "icall to" prefix, so this is recomp_esp_escape, a DIRECT call, and it is the FIRST transition out of range and the one to chase; (2) "[ESP] icall to sub_00220870 ... 00F7FF58 -> 00F8002C (delta +212)"; (3) "[ESP] icall to sub_00211530 ... 00F7FFF8 -> 00F80008 (delta +16)"; (4) "[ESP] icall to sub_00216F70 ... 00F80000 -> 00F80004 (delta +4)". SO BOTH PATHS OVER-POP, direct and indirect - #79's narrowing was not just unproven, it was backwards. The new RECOMP_ESP_WATCH added to RECOMP_ICALL / RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE / RECOMP_ITAIL is still worth having: it produced entries 2-4, which the direct-call check could never have caught, and it names target VAs. PRIME SUSPECT sub_00227F90: it is both the first esp escape (+180) and already present in tools_data/abi_violations.txt as "[ABI] sub_00227F90 did not restore: ebx 6769203A->45747865 esi 624F6174->6769203A" - ASCII ": ig" -> "extE" and "taOb" -> ": ig", i.e. it is moving string bytes through the callee-saved registers. A function that both destroys ebx/esi AND leaves esp 180 bytes high is a much stronger candidate than anything on the raw violation list. NOTE ON sub_00216F70, the 6-byte getter seeded in #78: its escape is only +4 and it starts from esp = 0x00F80000, i.e. esp was ALREADY at the stack ceiling when it ran. Its lifted body pops exactly 4 for its `ret`, which is correct. It is a VICTIM of the earlier drift, not a cause - do not revert it on this evidence. NEXT STEP: bracket sub_00227F90 with entry/exit esp probes and account for every push against every pop, the method that cracked #71. Tree state unchanged and verified: normal build 44 kernel calls / 5 failed icalls / 23 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, reached 101, callsites 357, deterministic 2 of 2. The recomp_types.h change is behaviour-neutral - the normal build's numbers are identical before and after it.

entries.claim: THE 180 BYTES ARE FOUND: sub_00204020 captures _icall_esp ABOVE its callee-saved pushes of esi and edi, so a FAILED ICALL rolls esp back past both saves while the epilogue pops them anyway - 8 bytes per call, in a loop, up a six-level chain. BUT the obvious fix REGRESSES the boot 101 -> 64 reached with 37 lost and ZERO gained, so it is reverted and the site carries a warning comment
entries.evidence: SIX LEVELS, EVERY ONE BRACKETED WITH PROBES RATHER THAN REASONED - and reasoning was wrong at every level, because four of the six functions balance perfectly on paper. (1) sub_00227F90, entry esp 0x00F7FF54: the five sub_00209650 calls gain instead of losing 4 each - after call 1 esp=0x00F7FF80 where 0x00F7FF50 was due (48 lost), then 32 lost on each of calls 2-5. 48 + 4x32 = 176, plus 4 for its own ret = 180, matching RECOMP_CHECK_ABI's "[ESP] sub_00227F90 ... 00F7FF54 -> 00F80008 (delta +180)" to the byte. Its own arithmetic (5 pushes, one `esp + 0x14`) is correct. (2) sub_00209650 is a callback dispatcher reading its target from MEM32(esp+8). Balanced. (3) sub_00227F50, the first callback: loc_00227F50 0x00F7FF44 -> loc_00227F55 0x00F7FF44 proves its sub_00227F90 re-entry is balanced; loc_00227F88 reads 0x00F7FF48 where 0x00F7FF18 was due. Its own 11 pushes = 0x2C are cleaned by `esp + 0x2C`. Balanced. (4) sub_002235D0 loses 24 per hit, twice on this path = 48. Walking all 60 labels: prologue correct (-0x108 frame, -0x10 for four pushes, steady at 0x00F7FDFC), then loc_00223736 -> loc_00223738 jumps +0x18 across ONE ICALL that pushes only a 4-byte dummy. DECISIVE DETAIL: the recursive INNER frame runs that same ICALL BALANCED. Probing the target explained why - "[T:PRE] #1 target=0x00226250" then POST unchanged, versus "[T:PRE] #2 target=0x00221F50 esp=0x00F7FDFC" then "[T:POST] #2 esp=0x00F7FE14". Same code, different callback. (5) sub_00221F50 is balanced at all 17 labels until its last call: loc_0022216C 0x00F7FDE0 -> loc_00222193 0x00F7FDF8 where 0x00F7FDE0 was due. Its own frame (esp-8 plus four pushes = 24, epilogue pops 4 registers plus `esp + 8` = 24) balances. (6) sub_0021ACD0 walked at 38 labels: prologue correct (-0x14 then -0xC = 32 wound, steady at 0x00F7FDAC), and loc_0021ADFB -> loc_0021AE17 gains 8 EVERY LOOP ITERATION - iteration 1 0x00F7FDAC -> 0x00F7FDB4, iteration 2 0x00F7FDB4 -> 0x00F7FDBC. Three iterations = 24. Both of ITS paths balance on paper too. THE TERMINAL CAUSE: the only call between those two labels is sub_00204020, thiscall with NO stack arguments. Its body is `{ uint32_t _icall_esp = g_esp; PUSH32(esp, esi); esi = ecx; eax = MEM32(esi); PUSH32(esp, edi); ... RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE(...); }` - _icall_esp captured ABOVE both callee-saved pushes. On failure RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE does `g_esp = saved_esp`, rolling past esi and edi; the epilogue (via sub_00204039 / sub_00204086) pops them regardless, so the caller ends 8 bytes high. Two saves = 8 bytes = exactly the per-iteration figure, and the run has 5 failed icalls. This is precisely the class tools_data/find_icall_esp_saves.py exists for; its fix comments are already present in sub_00209650 and sub_002235D0, and sub_00204020 was missed. THE SWEEP: 16,236 icall save points scanned, 3,140 capture across register saves - 2,519 at 4 bytes, 403 at 8, 143 at 12, 63 at 16, 7 at 20, 3 at 24, 2 at 28. IMPORTANT FRAMING: the skew only materialises when the ICALL actually FAILS, so these are LATENT sites, not 3,140 live bugs. THE FIX WAS APPLIED AND REVERTED. Moving the capture below the two pushes is correct in isolation and cut failed_icalls 5 -> 2 and heap_allocs 23 -> 22, but measured deterministic 2 of 2 it took reached 101 -> 64 and callsites 357 -> 265, and diff_reached.py returned "NOTHING new was reached and 37 were lost. That is a regression on this measure. Do not explain it away." Zero gained is the deciding difference from #72, which gained 4 while losing 17 and was rightly kept. Reverted; tree confirmed back at 44/5/23/8 with reached 101 and callsites 357. The site now carries a comment recording what was tried, the exact numbers, and the instruction to judge any retry on diff_reached.py rather than on failed_icalls - which improved while the boot got worse, a trap worth naming. STILL OPEN: why removing a real 8-byte skew makes the boot die earlier. Something downstream either depends on it or is masked by it. That question, not the skew, is now the wall.

entries.claim: H1 of ticket 02 is DEAD: re-applying the sub_00204020 _icall_esp fix and measuring callsites/kernel_calls alongside reached reproduces the regression on EVERY instrument - reached 101 -> 64 AND callsites 357 -> 265, 37 lost / 0 gained. But the fix does work as designed: the esp escape is gone (esp at the crash is 0x00F7FD9C, in-stack, versus 0x00F8031C escaped), and the crash relocates INTO sub_0021ACD0, the direct caller of sub_00204020 - which is H2's predicted shape
entries.evidence: Ticket 02's H1 argued the 2026-08-08 measurement might be incomplete rather than wrong - that g_callsite_count and kernel_calls were never recorded, and that a fix which stops a re-resolve thrash lowers `reached` while doing strictly more work (the precedent is documented in src/recomp/recomp_types.h:251-266, where kernel_calls went 82 -> 330 and the backtrace 4 -> 18 frames while g_reached_count FELL 55 -> 42). Its own falsification criterion was explicit: "callsites UP and/or kernel_calls UP with a deeper crash -> H1 confirmed; callsites DOWN too -> H1 dead." NOTE FOR THE RECORD: callsites HAD in fact already been measured - ledger #81's evidence states "reached 101 -> 64 and callsites 357 -> 265" verbatim, and the warning comment in the source at recomp_0015.c carries the same pair. The ticket was written without that detail. This entry is therefore a re-measurement on a tree that has moved since #81 (RTTI seeding touched seed_list.json, seeded_functions.json and recomp_manual.c), which is the part that made it worth spending a build cycle on. METHOD, one build cycle each way, deterministic 2 of 2 throughout. BASELINE on the current tree: 44 kernel calls / 5 failed icalls / 23 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, reached 101, callsites 357, crash RVA 0xEA904D = access violation WRITING Xbox VA 0xFFFFFF03 in sub_00204800+0x24D, esp = 0x00F80120-class escape at 0x00F8031C, 11-frame backtrace sub_00204800 -> sub_0020A360 -> sub_0020DA95 -> sub_002155B0 -> sub_002392E0 -> sub_00239E50 -> sub_00011E40 -> sub_001A1C23 -> sub_0019F196 -> sub_0019F22E -> sub_001A1C97. Identical to #81's recorded revert state, so the RTTI work did not move the boot. COVERAGE-VA set saved to tools_data/baseline_reached_pre204020fix.txt (101 lines). THE FIX RE-APPLIED: `uint32_t _icall_esp = g_esp;` moved from above `PUSH32(esp, esi)` to below `PUSH32(esp, edi)` in sub_00204020 (gen/recomp_0015.c), matching the template already applied in sub_00209650 and sub_002235D0. RESULT: 44 kernel calls (UNCHANGED) / 2 failed icalls (5 -> 2) / 22 heap allocs (23 -> 22) / 8 safe stubs, reached 64, callsites 265. diff_reached.py verdict verbatim: "NOTHING new was reached and 37 were lost. That is a regression on this measure. Do not explain it away." SO H1 IS DEAD ON ITS OWN TERMS - callsites went DOWN too, kernel_calls did not move, and there is no thrash-stopping signature. THE VALUABLE PART IS WHAT ELSE MOVED, AND IT ARGUES THE FIX IS MECHANICALLY CORRECT WHILE STILL BEING BAD FOR THE BOOT. (1) THE ESP ESCAPE IS GONE. At the baseline crash esp = 0x00F8031C, above the 0x00F80000 stack ceiling - the underflow #81 traced. With the fix, esp at the crash is 0x00F7FD9C, which triage labels "STACK" and is a healthy value. The 180 bytes really were the skew, and removing it really does fix the stack. (2) THE CRASH RELOCATES INTO THE CHAIN'S OWN SIXTH LEVEL. New crash RVA 0xF41A0B = READ at Xbox VA 0xFF011D6C in sub_0021ACD0+0x35B, ~24% through, recomp_0016.c near line 2857. sub_0021ACD0 IS THE DIRECT CALLER OF sub_00204020 - the very function #81 measured as gaining 8 bytes per loop iteration (0x00F7FDAC -> 0x00F7FDB4 -> 0x00F7FDBC). So with the skew removed, the loop that the skew was inflating is now the thing that dies. New 13-frame backtrace, a DIFFERENT route from sub_00239E50: sub_0021ACD0 -> sub_00221F50 -> sub_002235D0 -> sub_002221E0 -> sub_00209650 -> sub_002366BC -> sub_0023666F -> sub_00239E50 -> sub_00011E40 -> sub_001A1C23 -> sub_0019F196 -> sub_0019F22E -> sub_001A1C97. It leaves sub_00239E50 at +0x1F9 where the baseline leaves it at +0x390, i.e. EARLIER in that function - genuinely less progress, not a lateral move. (3) THE FAULTING VALUE. edi = 0xFF011D70 and the fault is exactly edi - 4; eax, ecx and edx are all NULL and esi = 1. The natural candidate at that spot is `MEM32(ebp + -4) = MEM32(ebp + -4) + 1;` at recomp_0016.c:2872 (loc_0021AD68) - a REFCOUNT INCREMENT on a pointer that is garbage. Caveat that matters: triage cannot print ebp, because ebp is the one x86 register the lifter models as a per-function C local rather than a global, so an ebp-based fault will always be reported against whichever GLOBAL register happens to hold the same value. Treat "edi - 4" and "ebp - 4" as both live until probed. That ebp is set two lines earlier from sub_0020DA80's return value (loc_0021AD62, `ebp = eax`) or zeroed at loc_0021AD51. THIS IS H2's PREDICTED SHAPE, NOT H1's: "the post-fix crash appears at a DIFFERENT site that reads a stack slot near the delta". It does, and the site is inside the immediate caller. NEXT STEP for whoever takes H2: with the fix applied, probe ebp and edi at loc_0021AD55 / loc_0021AD62 / loc_0021AD68 in sub_0021ACD0 and find where the refcount pointer comes from - i.e. whether sub_0020DA80 returns garbage or whether ebp is inherited wrong (sub_0021ACD0's callee sub_00204020 publishes g_seh_ebp on its tail-jumps). REVERTED AND VERIFIED BACK: tree rebuilt and re-run, 44/5/23/8 deterministic 2 of 2, reached 101, callsites 357, crash back at RVA 0xEA904D. The warning comment at the site was left untouched and is still accurate. Post-fix COVERAGE-VA set kept at tools_data/after_reached_204020fix.txt for the next attempt to diff against without paying for the build cycle again.

entries.claim: REFUTES the ebp lead of #82: ebp is HEALTHY at loc_0021AD62 and loc_0021AD68 (0x011D6000 then 0x011D7000, both real heap), so the refcount increment MEM32(ebp + -4) is NOT the fault. The crash the sub_00204020 fix exposes is `eax = MEM32(edi + -4)` at recomp_0016.c:2886 (loc_0021AD72), where edi = MEM32(esi + 0xC) and esi is 1. The bug is esi, not ebp - and esi is ALREADY 0 on the two surviving iterations, so sub_0021ACD0 is dereferencing a NULL object throughout and only guest VA 0 being mapped hides it
entries.evidence: Method: re-applied the sub_00204020 _icall_esp fix (capture moved below the callee-saved pushes of esi and edi) purely to reach the crash it exposes, then probed. Deterministic 2 of 2 at every step, signals with the fix + probes identical to the fix alone: 44 kernel calls / 2 failed icalls / 22 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs. PROBE PLACEMENT: [ADEBP62] inserted BEFORE `loc_0021AD64: ;`, i.e. immediately after `ebp = eax;` at loc_0021AD62, so it fires only on the path that takes sub_0020DA80's return value. [ADEBP68] inserted after `loc_0021AD68: ;`, i.e. immediately before the refcount increment. Then a second cycle added [AD6B] after `loc_0021AD6B: ;` and [AD72] after `loc_0021AD72: ;`. ONE PROBE TRAP AVOIDED AND WORTH RECORDING: add_probe.py accepted `MEM32(ebp + -4)` as a probe argument and it had to be removed by hand - the probe would have dereferenced the very address under suspicion, faulting during argument evaluation BEFORE fprintf emitted, and would have destroyed the answer on exactly the iteration that mattered. Never read the suspect address inside the probe that is meant to identify it. FULL PROBE OUTPUT, 9 lines, in order: [ADEBP62] ebp=011D6000 eax=011D6000 edi=0046B150 esi=00000000 esp=00F7FDAC / [ADEBP68] ebp=011D6000 edi=0046B150 esi=00000000 esp=00F7FDAC / [AD6B] esi=00000000 ebp=011D6000 esp=00F7FDAC / [ADEBP62] ebp=011D7000 eax=011D7000 edi=0046B154 esi=00000000 esp=00F7FDAC / [ADEBP68] ebp=011D7000 edi=0046B154 esi=00000000 esp=00F7FDAC / [AD6B] esi=00000000 ebp=011D7000 esp=00F7FDAC / [AD72] edi=011D6000 esi=00000000 ebp=011D7000 / [AD6B] esi=00000001 ebp=00000000 esp=00F7FD9C / [AD72] edi=FF011D70 esi=00000001 ebp=00000000. FINDING 1 - EBP IS INNOCENT. On both passes that reach loc_0021AD62 ebp is a clean heap pointer (0x011D6000, 0x011D7000), the refcount increment at MEM32(ebp - 4) reads live heap, and it does not fault. sub_0020DA80 is returning good pointers. #82's suggested lead is dead; do not re-chase it. FINDING 2 - THE REAL FAULT, MEASURED. The final [AD72] shows edi = 0xFF011D70 and esi = 1, and the very next statement is `eax = MEM32(edi + -4)` at recomp_0016.c:2886 - fault address 0xFF011D6C = edi - 4, matching triage exactly. edi is loaded one line earlier at loc_0021AD6B by `edi = MEM32(esi + 0xC)`, so with esi = 1 that is MEM32(0xD) - a misaligned read of low guest memory that returns garbage instead of faulting, because guest VA 0 is mapped in this runtime. THE BUG IS esi. FINDING 3, AND THE MORE ALARMING ONE - esi WAS ALREADY WRONG ON THE HEALTHY ITERATIONS. Both surviving passes show esi = 0, not a valid object pointer. With esi = 0, `edi = MEM32(esi + 0xC)` reads guest VA 0xC and `MEM32(esi + 0xC) = ebp` at loc_0021ADB4 (recomp_0016.c:2927) WRITES to guest VA 0xC. That write is visible in the trace: pass 1 stores ebp = 0x011D6000 to VA 0xC, and pass 2's [AD72] reads edi = 0x011D6000 straight back out of it. So sub_0021ACD0 has been walking a NULL object for the whole loop and the only reason it survives is that VA 0 is readable and writable. The sequence esi = 0, 0, 1 is junk, not objects. esi is loaded at loc_0021AD30 by `esi = MEM32(eax + edx)` (recomp_0016.c:2844) where eax = MEM32(esp + 0x30), edx = MEM32(ecx + 8), ecx = MEM32(esi + 0x28) - an array walk whose entries are small integers. NOTE THE SIGNATURE MATCH: `esi = 1` consumed as an object pointer is the same shape as ledger #62's sub_00205170 crash. Worth checking whether the same array is behind both. FINDING 4 - THE FIX DOES STABILISE THE LOOP. #81 measured sub_0021ACD0's loop gaining 8 bytes of esp per iteration (0x00F7FDAC -> 0x00F7FDB4 -> 0x00F7FDBC). With the fix applied, esp is steady at 0x00F7FDAC across both loop passes. The final pass at esp = 0x00F7FD9C is a separate, deeper invocation, not loop drift - it never hits [ADEBP62], so it took the `ebp = 0` path at loc_0021AD51 and jumped to loc_0021AD6B via the TEST_Z at loc_0021AD64. So the fix does exactly what it claims; what it exposes is an independent defect it was previously masking. NEXT STEP: with the fix applied, probe eax, edx, ecx and the resulting esi at loc_0021AD30 (recomp_0016.c:2841-2844) to find where the junk array comes from, and probe esi at sub_0021ACD0's entry (it arrives in ecx, thiscall) to see whether the caller sub_00221F50 hands over a bad object or the array walk manufactures one. TREE STATE: probes stripped (13 lines from recomp_0016.c), fix reverted, rebuilt and re-run - 44/5/23/8 deterministic 2 of 2, reached 101, callsites 357, crash back at RVA 0xEA904D. The warning comment at sub_00204020 now records this result as well.

entries.claim: FULL CHAIN for the crash the sub_00204020 fix exposes, and it CORRECTS #83: sub_0021ACD0 is entered exactly ONCE with a GOOD this (0x01091AB0) - all three passes are loop iterations, not separate invocations. The container it walks holds NULL at the indices read, so esi is 0; the code then uses guest VA 0 as scratch, iteration 2 mistakes iteration 1's leftover there for a live object and runs a destructor path, and THAT PATH LEAKS 16 BYTES, so iteration 3 reloads esi from the wrong stack slot and gets 2. A SECOND esp leak survives the sub_00204020 fix
entries.evidence: Method: sub_00204020 _icall_esp fix re-applied purely to reach the crash, three probes added, deterministic 2 of 2 (44 kernel calls / 2 failed icalls / 22 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, identical to the fix without probes). [ACD0ENT] after `loc_0021ACD0: ;` printing ecx (thiscall this), esp and the four inbound stack args. [AD30A] after `loc_0021AD30: ;` printing esi (the this at the loop head), edi, ebp, esp. [AD30B] after `esi = MEM32(eax + edx);` (recomp_0016.c:2844) printing the loaded element, eax, edx and ecx. FULL OUTPUT, 7 lines: [ACD0ENT] this=01091AB0 esp=00F7FDCC a1=0046B0E8 a2=0046B150 a3=0046B1B8 a4=00000002 / [AD30A] this=01091AB0 edi=0046B150 ebp=FFFFFF98 esp=00F7FDAC / [AD30B] elem=00000000 base=00000008 off=010906F0 ecx=01096B88 / [AD30A] this=01091AB0 edi=0046B154 ebp=FFFFFF98 esp=00F7FDAC / [AD30B] elem=00000000 base=0000000C off=010906F0 ecx=01096B88 / [AD30A] this=00000002 edi=005BBEF0 ebp=00000068 esp=00F7FD9C / [AD30B] elem=00000001 base=00000004 off=01091AB0 ecx=00000000. CORRECTION TO #83, and it matters: #83 said the final pass "is a separate, deeper invocation, not loop drift". THAT IS WRONG. [ACD0ENT] fires exactly ONCE, so there is only one call to sub_0021ACD0 and all three [AD30A] lines are iterations of its loop. The esp difference IS drift. I inferred a second invocation from the esp gap without a probe at the entry; the entry probe settles it. FINDING 1 - THE ENTRY IS CLEAN. this = 0x01091AB0, a real heap object, and the inbound args 0x0046B0E8 / 0x0046B150 / 0x0046B1B8 are three .data pointers with a4 = 2 as the start index. The caller sub_00221F50 is NOT handing over garbage. Note also that ebp = 0xFFFFFF98 at the loop head is CORRECT and not a bug: edi walks the a2 array (0x0046B150 then 0x0046B154, stride 4) and ebp is the delta a1 - a2, so `eax = MEM32(edi + ebp)` resolves to 0x0046B0E8 = a1. A negative-looking ebp here is the pointer-difference idiom, not corruption. FINDING 2 - THE CONTAINER IS EMPTY AT THE INDICES READ, AND THIS IS THE PRIMARY DEFECT. Reading the probe against the source: `ecx = MEM32(esi + 0x28)` = 0x01096B88 (a real heap object), `edx = MEM32(ecx + 8)` = 0x010906F0 (the element array), `eax = MEM32(esp + 0x30)` = the byte index (8, then 0xC), and `esi = MEM32(eax + edx)` therefore reads 0x010906F8 and 0x010906FC. BOTH RETURN 0x00000000. The count guarding the loop is `MEM32(MEM32(this + 0x28) + 0xC)` and it is greater than the start index 2, so the container claims elements 2 and 3 exist while its storage holds NULL for both. FINDING 3 - WHY A NULL esi DOES NOT FAULT IMMEDIATELY, AND HOW IT ESCALATES. With esi = 0, `edi = MEM32(esi + 0xC)` at loc_0021AD6B reads guest VA 0xC and `MEM32(esi + 0xC) = ebp` at loc_0021ADB4 (recomp_0016.c:2927) WRITES guest VA 0xC. Guest VA 0 is mapped in this runtime, so neither faults. The trace shows the consequence directly: iteration 1 stores ebp = 0x011D6000 to VA 0xC, iteration 2 reads it back as a non-NULL "object" and therefore falls into the refcount-decrement and destructor path at loc_0021AD72 that iteration 1 skipped. FINDING 4 - THE SECOND esp LEAK, 16 BYTES, IN THAT DESTRUCTOR PATH. esp at the loop head is 0x00F7FDAC on iterations 1 and 2 and 0x00F7FD9C on iteration 3 - a drop of 0x10 = 16 bytes, and a LEAK (too few pops), not the underflow the sub_00204020 fix addressed. It appears only after the iteration that took the loc_0021AD72 branch, so the leak is in that block or in one of the calls it makes: sub_001F87A0, sub_001EBA30, sub_0020EEE0. loc_0021AD20 then does `ebp = MEM32(esp + 0x24); ebx = MEM32(esp + 0x14); esi = MEM32(esp + 0x10);` - reloading all three loop variables from stack slots that esp has moved under. esi comes back as 2, edi as 0x005BBEF0, ebp as 0x68, and the crash follows one line later. THIS IS EXACTLY THE #46 PATTERN (cursor and end held in stack slots while esp drifts 12 bytes per pass), a fourth instance of it. IMPORTANT CONSEQUENCE FOR THE sub_00204020 FIX: it removes the 8-byte-per-iteration drift (iterations 1 and 2 are now stable, where #81 measured 0x00F7FDAC -> FDB4 -> FDBC), but a SECOND, independent 16-byte leak survives it. So the fix is necessary and not sufficient, and "the skew was load-bearing" is the wrong framing - there was simply another leak underneath. ORDER OF ATTACK: the NULL container elements are upstream of everything else, because they are why the leaking destructor path executes at all. If elements 2 and 3 held real objects, `MEM32(esi + 0xC)` would read a real member instead of guest VA 0xC and the mistaken-object branch would not be taken. NEXT STEP: find who populates the array at 0x010906F0 owned by object 0x01096B88 (= MEM32(0x01091AB0 + 0x28)), and why its count at MEM32(0x01096B88 + 0xC) exceeds the number of elements actually stored. A write-watch on 0x010906F8 is the direct instrument - `run(watch="0x010906F8:4:elem2")` - and note VA 0xC is worth watching too since the code writes there. TREE STATE: probes stripped (10 lines from recomp_0016.c), fix reverted, rebuilt and re-run - 44/5/23/8 deterministic 2 of 2, reached 101, callsites 357, crash back at RVA 0xEA904D. The sub_00204020 warning comment now records this chain.

entries.claim: The write-watch CONFIRMS that our lifted code scribbles on guest VA 0xC - the write comes from inside sub_0021ACD0 itself (RVA 0xF41BDD = sub_0021ACD0 + 0x52D = loc_0021ADB4). But the watch CANNOT answer who populates the container: it is one-shot and PAGE-granular, so on both pages it catches our own allocator's zero-fill from a system-DLL memset and then goes blind. Watching a heap field for "who wrote this value" does not work on this project unless the field's page is untouched, which a freshly zeroed allocation never is
entries.evidence: Ran with the sub_00204020 _icall_esp fix applied so the boot reaches the sub_0021ACD0 container walk. Deterministic 2 of 2 at 44 kernel calls / 2 failed icalls / 22 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, crash RVA 0xF41A0B, on both watch runs. RUN 1, watch="0x010906F8:4:elem2,0x0000000C:4:va0c". Output: "[WATCH:elem2] armed on xbox VA 0x010906F8 (4 bytes); current value 0x00000000" / "[WATCH:va0c] armed on xbox VA 0x0000000C (4 bytes); current value 0x00000000" / "[WATCH:elem2] write to xbox VA 0x010906F8 from RIP=0x7FFAD2EAE579 (RVA=0x34462E579) - disarmed, continuing" / "[WATCH:va0c] write to xbox VA 0x0000000C from RIP=0x7FF78F7C1BDD (RVA=0xF41BDD) - disarmed, continuing". RUN 2, watch="0x01096B94:4:count,0x01096B90:4:arrayptr" (the container's count at +0xC and array pointer at +8 on object 0x01096B88). Output: both armed with current value 0x00000000, then "[WATCH:count] write to xbox VA 0x01096B94 from RIP=0x7FFAD2EAE579 (RVA=0x34462E579) - disarmed, continuing", and arrayptr NEVER FIRED. RESULT 1 - THE VA 0xC SCRIBBLE IS PROVEN, not inferred. RVA 0xF41BDD is inside our own module. sub_0021ACD0 starts at RVA 0xF416B0 (derived from the probe-free crash at 0xF41A0B being sub_0021ACD0 + 0x35B), so the writer is sub_0021ACD0 + 0x52D - later in the function than the crash site, which places it at loc_0021ADB4, i.e. `MEM32(esi + 0xC) = ebp;` at recomp_0016.c:2927. #84 predicted exactly this write from reading the source; the watch measures it. Our lifted code really does write to guest VA 0xC because esi is NULL, and it does not fault because VA 0 is mapped. RESULT 2 - THE INSTRUMENT IS THE WRONG ONE FOR THE REMAINING QUESTION, AND THAT IS THE USEFUL FINDING. RIP 0x7FFAD2EAE579 is identical in both the elem2 hit and the count hit, and it is FAR outside our module: with image base 0x7FF78E880000 (RIP 0x7FF78F7C1A0B minus RVA 0xF41A0B) it resolves to +0x34462E579, i.e. a system DLL - a CRT memset/memcpy. That is our own heap zero-fill (xbox_HeapAlloc / xbox_HeapAllocAt both zero, see #76) touching each page as the object is allocated. Since the watch fires ONCE and then disarms, and the docs state it is PAGE-granular, the first touch of a freshly allocated page is always the allocator's own zero-fill - after which the protection is gone and every later game write is invisible. THAT ALSO EXPLAINS THE arrayptr NON-EVENT, AND IT IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING. 0x01096B90 and 0x01096B94 are four bytes apart, so they share page 0x01096000; the single fault was credited to `count` and cleared the page for both. We KNOW arrayptr was written afterwards, because the probes in #84 read MEM32(0x01096B90) = 0x010906F0 at the loop head. So "arrayptr never fired" means the watch went blind, NOT that nobody wrote it. Do not record a silent watch as a negative result. GENERAL RULE FOR THIS PROJECT: a write-watch on a heap field cannot answer "who set this value" when the field lives on a page the allocator has just zeroed. It works for corruption of an already-live page (which is what it was built for and how the ordinal-47 case was cracked), not for tracing initialisation. To trace initialisation, either re-arm after the zero-fill or use a probe at the suspected writer. WHAT IS STILL OPEN, unchanged: why MEM32(0x01096B88 + 0xC) exceeds 2 while MEM32(0x010906F0 + 8) and MEM32(0x010906F0 + 0xC) are both NULL. NEXT STEP, and it is now cheap because of the RTTI work: read MEM32(0x01096B88) - the object's vtable pointer - and look it up in tools/ghidra_naming/rtti_names.json to get the class NAME, then find that class's element-add method and probe it. That turns an anonymous container into a named one and is a far better lead than another watch. A probe at sub_0021ACD0's entry printing MEM32(this + 0x28), MEM32(MEM32(this + 0x28) + 8) and MEM32(MEM32(this + 0x28) + 0xC) also costs one build cycle and pins the count exactly. TREE STATE: fix reverted, rebuilt and re-run - 44/5/23/8 deterministic 2 of 2, crash back at RVA 0xEA904D, no probes anywhere.

entries.claim: Ledger #85's recommended next step - look up the empty container's vtable in rtti_names.json to get its class name - is a DEAD END. The container at 0x01096B88 has vtable 0x003EEF28, and that vtable's COL pointer at vtable[-1] is ZERO: the class has no RTTI at all, so no name exists to recover. Not a parser bug and not one of the 954 rejected candidates.
entries.evidence: MEASURED in one build cycle, deterministic, signals unchanged at 44/5/23/8 with the probe in and again after stripping it. Probe placed immediately after `ecx = MEM32(esi + 0x28);` at loc_0021AD30 (recomp_0016.c:2839) printing ecx and a range-guarded MEM32(ecx), reading the same register #84's trace already trusts rather than hardcoding the literal address. Result: "[VT] container=0x01096B88 vtable=0x003EEF28" on the first iteration, then "container=0x00000000 vtable=0x00000000" twice - the two corrupted iterations #83/#84 already characterised, where esi is already 0. So the container address reproduces #84 exactly and the vtable is new information. THE LOOKUP FAILS, AND THE REASON MATTERS. grep for 3EEF28 (case-insensitive) returns nothing in tools/ghidra_naming/rtti_names.json or rtti_xml1.json. Rather than conclude "the parser missed it", read the XBE directly the same way rtti_names.py does - parsing the section table from the XBE header (base 0x00010000, 16 sections) and mapping VA to file offset. FINDINGS: 0x003EEF28 lies in .rdata, which is where vtables belong, so the address is plausible. But MSVC RTTI puts the CompleteObjectLocator pointer at vtable[-1], and MEM32(0x003EEF24) reads ZERO. No COL means no TypeDescriptor means no `.?AV<name>@@` string. The class simply has no RTTI emitted - MSVC only emits it for classes needing polymorphic identification, so a class whose vtable exists but whose COL slot is null was never given RTTI by the compiler. That distinguishes case (b) from case (a): this is NOT among rtti_names.py's 954 rejected COL candidates, because there is no candidate to reject. The RTTI approach cannot name this class, and no amount of fixing the parser will change that. THE PROBE WAS STILL WORTH IT - the vtable slots are a better lead than the name would have been. First eight slots of 0x003EEF28: [0] 0x0020DA40, [1] 0x0015FDF0, [2] 0x0013D370, [3] 0x0015FDF0, [4] 0x0015FDF0, [5] 0x000D7E20, [6] 0x000D7E20, [7] 0x0015FDF0. TWO OBSERVATIONS. (1) Slot 0 is sub_0020DA40, immediately adjacent to sub_0020DA80 - the function ticket 02 / ledger #83 measured returning HEALTHY pointers (0x011D6000, 0x011D7000) inside this very loop at loc_0021AD62. Same code family, and slot 0 in MSVC layout is typically the destructor or first virtual, so this is the container's own class implementation sitting right beside a function already proven good. (2) 0x0015FDF0 occupies three of the first eight slots and also appears twice in CClient's vtable in rtti_xml1.json - the shared do-nothing/stub filler, meaning this class inherits far more than it overrides. NEAREST RTTI-KNOWN NEIGHBOURS bracket it usefully: 0x003E173C Raven::SceneLib::igProcGeometry below, 0x0042A7DC Gap::Core::igInfo above. So it sits in the Raven::SceneLib / Gap block of .rdata rather than the CMemory/allocator block, which is a mild argument that this container is a scene/entity list rather than a memory-manager structure. NEXT STEP UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE, but now approach it from the vtable rather than the name: deepdive sub_0020DA40 (slot 0) and sub_0013D370 (slot 2), and find who calls the element-add path that should have populated 0x010906F0. The count at MEM32(0x01096B88 + 0xC) exceeding the stored element count remains the primary defect per #84. Tree verified clean after: probes stripped (4 lines), rebuilt, 44/5/23/8 deterministic 2 of 2, reached unchanged, crash RVA 0xEA904D.

entries.claim: ROOT CAUSE of the empty container: the allocator's BLOCK-SIZE query (vtable+0x144) returns 0 for every live buffer. That makes the array's capacity read as 0, so sub_00202B87 grows on EVERY add and its zero-run starts at slot 0 instead of at the old capacity - wiping every previously stored element. The container ends with count 27 and all slots NULL not because elements were never added, but because each add erases the one before it.
entries.evidence: MEASURED end to end, five build cycles, every step deterministic at 44/5/23/8. THE CHAIN, each link probed rather than reasoned: sub_00221F50 reads the container's count as a START INDEX (`edi = MEM32(eax + 0xC)`) then calls sub_00209470 to add N elements. sub_00209470 calls a factory per element and stores the result at MEM32(buffer + count*4), bumping count. Trace-mode watch on the count field 0x01096B94 showed it climbing 1,2,3...0x16 from RVA 0xECA1D2 = sub_00209470 + 0x7C2, so elements really were added 27 times - the count is honest, not corrupt. THE FACTORY IS FINE, refuting my own first hypothesis: probes at loc_002094CF returned real objects every call - 0x010902A0, 0x010902D8, 0x01090310, 0x01090370, 0x010903A8, 0x010903E0, 0x01090418, 0x01090498. No NULLs, so "a failed icall returns 0 and NULL gets stored" is dead. THE REALLOC IS ALSO FINE, refuting the second hypothesis: slots survive buffer moves. The decisive trace is slots 2 and 3 across grows on container 0x01096B88 with the buffer NOT moving: "#4 PRE s2=0x010902A0" then "#4 POST s2=0x010902A0" then "#5 PRE s2=0x00000000 s3=0x010902D8". Element 2 is erased IN PLACE between two grows, with oldbuf == newbuf == 0x01096BA0 throughout. Elements are not lost in a move; they are wiped where they lie. Exactly one element survives each grow - #3 has s1, #4 has s2, #5 has s3 - which is the signature of a zero-run that starts at slot 0 every time. THE MECHANISM, read from sub_00202B87 (recomp_0015.c:13916): `esi = MEM32(ebx + 8)` (the buffer), then sub_001E8E20 finds its allocator and ICALL MEM32(edx + 0x144) queries the block size, then `esi = eax >> 2` is the capacity in slots and `edi = esi` remembers the OLD capacity. At the end, `edi = newbuf + edi * 4` and a rep stosd zeroes (new_cap - old_cap) slots. That is correct ONLY if the old capacity is right. With capacity 0, edi = 0, so the zero run starts at slot 0 and covers the entire array. THE CONFIRMING MEASUREMENT: a probe at loc_00202BAE filtered to our container prints "blocksize=0x00000000 capacity=0" on ALL TEN grow events, with buf non-NULL and real each time (0x01096BA0, then 0x01090348, then 0x01090450). The query is answering zero for a live, non-empty block. SECOND, INDEPENDENT CONSEQUENCE that corroborates it: sub_00209470 skips growing only when `count < capacity`. With capacity 0 that is never true, so it grows on EVERY add - and the container-filtered trace shows 12 grow events, matching. Two separate symptoms from one cause. WHY THE CRASH FOLLOWS: sub_0021ACD0 is handed a start index of 2 and iterates to the count (27), reading MEM32(buffer + i*4). Every slot reads NULL, so esi = 0, and `MEM32(esi + 0xC)` reads AND WRITES guest VA 0xC - which is mapped, so nothing faults and the corruption propagates (ledger #84/#85). NOT YET IDENTIFIED and the obvious next step: WHAT vtable+0x144 actually is, and why it returns 0. The probe that tried to name it printed 0xBAD00000 because it read eax at loc_00202BF0, where eax is still the flag byte from MEM8(ebx + 7) - the vtable walk happens after that label. Recompute the chain (registry at 0x5BC538/0x5BC53C, indexed by MEM8(ebx+7) >> 1) or probe inside sub_001E8E20's return. Given ledger #75/#76 fixed a different allocator gap in our own kernel bridge, check whether vtable+0x144 lands on lifted code, an unimplemented stub, or one of the 5 failed icalls before assuming it is a game bug. ALSO CORRECTED HERE: an earlier probe of slot 0 across the grow showed it zero every time and looked like evidence. It was not - sub_00209470 starts storing at index = count, and the count was already 2 when it began (sub_00216FD0 had taken it to 2 from RVA 0xF29010), so slots 0 and 1 are never written by this path and their being zero means nothing. Probe the slots the code actually touches. Tree verified clean after: probes stripped, rebuilt, 44/5/23/8 deterministic, crash RVA 0xEA904D unchanged.

entries.claim: WHY vtable+0x144 RETURNS 0: it is never called. sub_001E8E20 ("which allocator owns this pointer?") returns NULL for the array buffer, and sub_00202B87 dereferences that NULL without checking - MEM32(0) reads guest VA 0, which IS MAPPED in our build, so it yields 0 instead of faulting, the icall target becomes 0, the call fails, and eax is left 0 as the "block size". Measured owner=0 on all ten grows.
entries.evidence: MEASURED, deterministic, filtered to container 0x01096B88 so the shared helper's other callers could not drown the result. Probe at loc_00202BA0 in sub_00202B87, where eax holds sub_001E8E20's return value, printing the owner plus its guarded vtable and the resolved vtable+0x144 target. All ten grow events read "owner=0x00000000 owner_vtbl=0x00000000 size_fn=0x00000000" with a real non-NULL buffer each time (0x01096BA0, then 0x01090348, then 0x01090450). THE FULL MECHANISM, now closed end to end. sub_00202B87 does: `PUSH esi (buffer); call sub_001E8E20` then `edx = MEM32(eax); ICALL MEM32(edx + 0x144)`. sub_001E8E20 (recomp_0014.c:773) is an owner lookup - it walks registry 0x5BC53C and then registry 0x5BC538, and for each entry calls vtable+0x78 as a predicate and vtable+0x148 as "is this pointer yours?". On a hit it tail-calls sub_001E8EA2 and returns the owner. If NOTHING claims the pointer it falls through to loc_001E8E9C, `eax = 0; return`. sub_00202B87 never checks that. THE NULL IS INVISIBLE BECAUSE GUEST VA 0 IS MAPPED - `edx = MEM32(0)` silently yields 0 rather than faulting, `MEM32(0 + 0x144)` is then the icall target, RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE rejects target 0 and its stub leaves eax = 0, and that zero is consumed as the block size. The run's failed-icall list already contains target 0x00000000, which this accounts for. CONSEQUENCES, both previously measured in #87 and now explained: (1) capacity = 0 >> 2 = 0, so sub_00209470's guard `if (count < capacity) skip grow` is never true and it grows on EVERY add - 12 grow events for 27 adds; (2) sub_00202B87 remembers old capacity in edi and zeroes from `newbuf + edi * 4`, so with edi = 0 the zero-run starts at slot 0 and wipes the whole array every time, leaving exactly one live element - the trace showed #3 s1, #4 s2, #5 s3, with element 2 erased IN PLACE while the buffer did not move. THE REAL QUESTION IS NOW ONE LEVEL UP AND SHARPER: why does no registered allocator claim a buffer that an allocator in that same registry handed out? The constructor sub_00202C70 allocates the initial buffer through registry 0x5BC538 via vtable+0xCC, and sub_00202B87 reallocs through vtable+0xDC, so the block demonstrably comes from a registered allocator. Either the registry walk is not reaching the right entry, or vtable+0x148 ("is this yours?") is answering false for its own block. NOTE the registries at 0x5BC538/0x5BC53C are the same pair ledger #36/#43/#44 found NULL and repaired - worth re-checking they are fully populated now rather than merely non-NULL. NEXT PROBE: inside sub_001E8E20, print the entry count MEM32(reg + 4) for both registries and, per entry, the vtable+0x78 and vtable+0x148 results, to see whether the loop runs zero times or runs and is answered false. SEPARATE, SYSTEMIC FINDING WORTH ITS OWN WORK: mapping guest VA 0 is hiding null-pointer dereferences across the whole port. This bug, and the sub_0021ACD0 `MEM32(esi + 0xC)` read/write at VA 0xC in #84/#85, both stayed silent solely because page 0 is readable and writable. An opt-in debug build that leaves guest page 0 unmapped would turn every one of these into an immediate, precisely-located fault instead of silent corruption surfacing frames later. That is a cheap, high-yield tooling change and would likely have caught this in one run. Tree verified clean after: probes stripped, rebuilt, 44/5/23/8 deterministic 2 of 2, crash RVA 0xEA904D unchanged.

entries.claim: FIXED #88: the owner lookup failed because OUR OWN manual guard range-checked a VTABLE pointer against the HEAP range. Registry B's only entry 0x01088A90 has vtable 0x003F4770, which lives in the image far BELOW the heap, so the guard rejected it on every call and sub_001E8E20 returned NULL. Widening the range to image-base..end-of-RAM POPULATES THE CONTAINER - slots go from all-NULL to real objects - and heap_allocs jumps 23 -> 49. But reached falls 101 -> 86 with 22 gained / 37 lost, so this is kept on the #72 precedent, not on a clean win.
entries.evidence: MEASURED, not inferred, and the measurement named our own code as the culprit. Probes inside sub_001E8E20 filtered to the three buffers the container actually used: "[L:B_ENTER] regB=0x01090020 cntB=0x00000001" - registry B holds exactly ONE entry - and "[L:RAW2] raw_entry=0x01088A90", a real object. But [L:A_LOOP] NEVER FIRED (registry A at 0x5BC53C is empty) and [L:B_PRED] NEVER FIRED either, so control died between loading the entry and calling its predicate. The only exit in that gap is a MANUAL guard we added: `eax = MEM32(esi); if (!(eax >= 0x00880000u && eax < 0x04000000u)) goto loc_001E8E99;`. That is the HEAP range, but eax is the entry's VTABLE pointer, and vtables live in the image (.rdata), far below the heap. CONFIRMED RATHER THAN INFERRED with a dedicated probe: "[G] entry=0x01088A90 vtable=0x003F4770 passes_heap_guard=0" on all eight calls. 0x003F4770 < 0x00880000, so a perfectly valid allocator was rejected every single time, the walk skipped its only entry, and the function returned NULL - which #88 traced into sub_00202B87's block-size call returning 0, capacity 0, and an array wiped on every grow. THE FIX: widen to `0x00010000u .. 0x04000000u` (image base to end of guest RAM) at both sites - loc_001E8E41 and loc_001E8E7F. That still rejects the small integers and wild pointers the guard was added for, including the 0xBEEF0001 fake thread handle its own comment documents. ALSO CLEANED UP: the loc_001E8E41 guard had accumulated EIGHT copies from repeated tool runs, four of them jumping to loc_001E8E99 - the SECOND walk's label, wrong for the first walk. Collapsed to one correct copy. THE FIX WORKS, proven on the thing it was supposed to fix. Container dump at sub_0021ACD0's entry, before: "count=0x1B | s0=0 s1=0 s2=0 s3=0". After: "count=0x1B | s0=0x01096C60 s1=0x01096CA8 s2=0x01096D20 s3=0x01096D58" - real objects in every slot. A SECOND container also appears now ("this=0x01097748 cont=0x010977B0 count=4"), so the boot is building structures it never previously reached. heap_allocs 23 -> 49 (more than double - the allocator is doing real work now), failed_icalls 5 -> 4, safe_stub 8 -> 6. BUT THE COVERAGE SET IS MIXED AND I AM NOT GLOSSING IT: reached 101 -> 86, callsites 357 -> 267, set diff 22 gained / 37 lost. entries.claim: The memcpy wall is a NULL OWNER POINTER in a block header. sub_0021ACD0's release path reads MEM32(edi) - the owner back-pointer 8 bytes before each object - and it is 0 on all 26 objects, so sub_001F87A0 runs with this = 0, underflows its count to 0xFFFFFFFF and hands memcpy a huge size.
entries.evidence:
Follows #93's census, which named sub_001F87A0 as the source of the null-derived pointer. Two probes, one build, deterministic run at the usual 44/4/49/6.

WHAT sub_001F87A0 IS (recomp_0014.c:41262, 76 lines, faithful-clean). It is an array element-erase on a thiscall `this` = esi:

    esi = ecx
    ... sub_001EB890(...)               finds the index, returned via MEM32(esp + 4)
  loc_001F87DB:
    eax = MEM32(esi + 0x10)             element buffer base
    edx = MEM32(esp + 4)                index
    ecx = eax + edx * 4                 &buf[index]
    eax = MEM32(esi + 4); eax--         count - 1
    MEM32(esi + 4) = eax                store new count
    eax = (eax - edx) << 2              bytes to move
    sub_00342AA0(ecx, ecx + 4, eax)     the memmove that becomes the VCRUNTIME memcpy
  loc_001F87FC:
    eax = MEM32(esi + 8)                capacity
    ecx = MEM32(esi + 4)
    if (ecx < eax) MEM32(esi + 8) = eax >> 1

With esi = 0 every field read hits guest page 0, and the census offsets line up exactly: +0x31B reads guest 0x10 (buffer), +0x34E reads guest 0x04 (count), +0x364 WRITES guest 0x04 (count - 1), +0x402 reads guest 0x08 (capacity), +0x416 reads guest 0x04. Counts 28/28/28/27/27 - the 28th call dies before reaching loc_001F87FC.

The failure is arithmetic, not a bad address: count = MEM32(0) = 0, so count - 1 = 0xFFFFFFFF, and the move size (0xFFFFFFFF - index) << 2 is enormous. That is why the fault VA is 0xFFFFFFE4 (-28) rather than a small offset - it is the memmove walking off the bottom, not a null field read.

WHERE this = 0 COMES FROM. sub_0021ACD0 calls sub_001F87A0 at two sites, both shaped:

    ebx = MEM32(edi);        edi = object - 8, so this is the block header's OWNER word
    ecx = MEM32(ebx);        this = MEM32(owner)
    PUSH32(esp, edi); call sub_001F87A0

Probes [AD7E] at loc_0021AD7E and [ADC7] at loc_0021ADC7, printing edi, MEM32(edi) and the object pointer:

    [AD7E]  0 fires - that site never executes.
    [ADC7]  26 fires, all identical in shape:

      site2 edi=0x011D5FF8 owner=0x00000000 ebp=0x011D6000
      site2 edi=0x011D6FF8 owner=0x00000000 ebp=0x011D7000
      site2 edi=0x011D7FF8 owner=0x00000000 ebp=0x011D8000
      ... ascending by exactly 0x1000 ...
      site2 edi=0x011E8FF8 owner=0x00000000 ebp=0x011E9000

So: 26 live objects, each a REAL heap pointer, each exactly 0x1000 apart, each with edi = object - 8, and the owner word at object - 8 is NULL on every one. ecx = MEM32(0) = 0 and sub_001F87A0 gets this = 0. This also explains the census's 26 reads of guest 0x00 at sub_0021ACD0+0x580 and 25 reads of guest 0x20 at +0x678 (`MEM8(ebx + 0x20)` with ebx = 0).

The header is HALF written, which is the sharp part of the finding. The release path only runs when the refcount reaches zero:

    eax = MEM32(ebp + -4); edi = ebp - 8; eax--; MEM32(edi + 4) = eax;
    if (eax != 0) skip release

It ran 26 times, so MEM32(object - 4) was 1 each time. The refcount word at -4 IS initialised; the owner word at -8 is NOT. Same two-word header, one field written and one not.

NOT CONCLUDED, and deliberately so. sub_0020DA80 (which produced ebp, via sub_0020DA95) is a two-line wrapper and does not write the header itself. The census separately reports sub_0020A360 + 0x2D6 and + 0x331 WRITING guest 0x00 and guest 0x04 33 times each - a two-word write through a NULL base, the same shape as this header - and sub_0020A360 is in the old sub_0020DA95 backtrace. That is a strong lead for "the header write went to guest 0 instead of object - 8", but it is a lead, not a measurement: 33 does not equal 26, and the refcount at -4 demonstrably did get written somewhere. Probe sub_0020A360's two write sites next and find what base register they use.

The 0x1000 spacing is worth noting on its own - one full page per object, starting just past the 0x01090000..0x011D0000 region xbox_HeapAllocAt handed out in #76.

WHAT sub_0020A360 IS (recomp_0015.c:30218, faithful-clean, 42 insns). It is the two-word block-header initialiser, and its two writes are the ones #93's census caught:

  ecx = esp + 0x18; PUSH32(esp, ecx)  <- &out_slot_B
  ecx = MEM32(ebp + 4); PUSH32(esp, edi)

  ... memcpy the string into eax ...
  ecx = MEM32(esp + 0xC)              read out_slot_A back

The two slots are zeroed on entry, passed BY ADDRESS to sub_001F8890, then read back and forwarded as sub_0020A360's arg1 and arg2. They come back still 0. So sub_001F8890 is not writing its out-parameters. That is the next link and the next probe.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW, stated because the temptation to close the loop here is strong and it would be wrong. These 33 calls are NOT the writer of #94's 26 null-owner objects:

    sub_0020A360 had written their headers to guest 0, object - 4 would still

So there are two distinct populations of half-initialised blocks. They may share a root cause in the allocator's out-parameter handling, but that is a hypothesis, not this measurement. #94's 26 objects still need their own writer identified.

THE STUB, in full:

    void sub_001F8890(void)
    {
        uint32_t entry_esp = g_esp;
        uint32_t len = MEM32(entry_esp + 4);
        g_eax = xbox_HeapAlloc(len ? len : 4, 4);

Its own comment states the signature - "(length, out-ptr, out-ptr) on the stack" - and then it reads the length and ignores both out-pointers.   buf   = 0x01091B50   real element buffer, this + 0x20
  idx   = 39           the index sub_001EB890 returned
  count = 39 before the decrement, 38 after

  dst   = 0x01091BEC = buf + 39*4    exactly the crash register edi
  size  = (38 - 39) << 2 = 0xFFFFFFFC = -4

So the arithmetic is `(count - 1 - idx) << 2` with idx == count, giving -1 elements. memmove takes that as an unsigned 4 GB length and walks off the end. entries.claim: ROOT CAUSE OF THE WALL, Ghidra-verified: a DEFERRED-FLAG MISCOMPILE in sub_001EB890's binary search. The JLE at 0x001EB911 consumes flags from TEST EAX,EAX at 0x001EB909 (the strcmp result), but the lifter re-derived the condition from the eax RELOADED by the intervening MOV (the search width), which is always positive - so the search always moves right, always returns count, and never finds anything.
entries.evidence:
Chain closed. Answers "what maintains 0x01091B30's count and capacity" and then keeps going to the actual defect.

THE CONTAINER LAYOUT, settled from Ghidra's FUN_00204800 rather than guessed:

    +0x04  count
    +0x08  binary-search STEP - a power of two, doubled on insert, halved on erase
    +0x0C  CAPACITY
    +0x10  element buffer

CORRECTS #99. I read +8 as the capacity and reported "count 39 in a capacity-32 buffer". WRONG. +8 is the search step and 32 is the correct step for count 39 (largest power of two <= 39). The real capacity is at +0xC and it is 1024. There was never a capacity problem.

WHAT MAINTAINS THEM: sub_00204800 is the insert - it grows the buffer via sub_00203450 when count == capacity, doubles capacity, memmoves, stores, increments count and doubles the step. sub_001F87A0 is the erase - decrements count, halves the step. Both were probed.

THE INSERT SIDE IS COMPLETELY HEALTHY. 39 inserts into 0x01091B30:

    [INS] this=0x01091B30 count=0  cap=1024 step=0  buf=0x01091B50 idx=0
    [INS] this=0x01091B30 count=1  cap=1024 step=1  buf=0x01091B50 idx=1
    [INS] this=0x01091B30 count=2  cap=1024 step=2  buf=0x01091B50 idx=2
    ... step doubles 0,1,2,4,8,16,32 exactly on schedule ...
    [INS] this=0x01091B30 count=38 cap=1024 step=32 buf=0x01091B50 idx=38

Capacity 1024 throughout, never needs to grow, buffer never moves. But look at the index: idx == count on EVERY ONE OF THE 39 INSERTS. Every insert appends. For a sorted array of 39 arbitrary names that is not plausible - it means the search never returned an interior position.

THE DEFECT, in sub_001EB890 (recomp_0014.c:8505). Ghidra's disassembly:

    0x001eb909: TEST EAX,EAX          ; eax = strcmp result (+1 / -1 / 0)
    0x001eb90b: JZ   0x001eb93b       ; equal -> the FOUND exit
    0x001eb90d: MOV  EAX,[ESP+0x10]   ; reload the width - MOV DOES NOT AFFECT FLAGS
    0x001eb911: JLE  0x001eb91b       ; branches on the flags from 0x1eb909

Ghidra's decompilation says the same in C:

    if (iVar5 == 0) { ...found... }
    uVar7 = local_c;
    if (0 < iVar5) { uVar7 = uVar1; local_c = uVar1; }

The JLE tests iVar5, the COMPARISON RESULT. Our lifted C:

    loc_001EB90D: ;
        eax = MEM32(esp + 0x10);
        if (CMP_LE(eax & eax, 0)) goto loc_001EB91B;   /* tests the RELOADED eax */

It re-derives the condition from the value MOV just loaded - the search width - instead of the flags that were live across the MOV. The width is always > 0 inside the loop (that is the loop's own continue condition), so CMP_LE is always FALSE, control always falls into loc_001EB913 (`ecx = edi`, base = probe), and the search always moves right. It walks to the top every time and returns count.

That single wrong branch produces everything observed:
  - 39 inserts, all appending at idx == count (#100's probe)
  - the erase getting idx = 39 = count, the not-found sentinel (#99's probe)
  - (38 - 39) << 2 = 0xFFFFFFFC handed to memmove, and the VCRUNTIME crash

KNOWN CLASS, and this is the important part. This is the deferred-flag miscompile of ledger #44 (0x001F0AB2), listed first in the lifter-bug-classes notes. It is the shape where a flag-setting instruction is separated from its consumer by a flag-preserving instruction (MOV, LEA, PUSH) and the lifter rebuilds the test from whatever the register holds at the branch.

TWO DETECTORS MISSED IT:
  - faithful.py reports sub_001EB890 CLEAN - no missing labels, no stale flags.
  - find_stale_flag_tests.py did not flag it either (it is not in any sweep result).
Both should be checked against this instance; a detector that misses the bug that
cost this many sessions needs the case added to it.

THE FIX in the lifted C - capture the comparison result before the reload:

    loc_001EB909: ;
        if (TEST_Z(eax, eax)) { g_seh_ebp = ebp; sub_001EB93B(); return; }
    loc_001EB90D: ;
        { int32_t _cmp = (int32_t)eax;    /* flags from TEST EAX,EAX at 0x1EB909 */
          eax = MEM32(esp + 0x10);        /* MOV does not affect flags */
          if (_cmp <= 0) goto loc_001EB91B; }

eax is known non-zero at that point (the ==0 case exited above), so _cmp is +1 or -1 and JLE reduces to _cmp < 0.

METHOD NOTE: this was found by diffing the lifted C against Ghidra's decompilation of the same address - the comparison the project notes call the one that has never given a wrong answer. STEP 2 - WHY IT IS INERT. `_cf` is declared at the top of sub_001EB890 and
read twice at loc_001EB904 to build the strcmp result:

never assigned. It stays 0, so the SBB pair always yields +1 - "key sorts
after element" - on every comparison. The branch I repaired therefore always

independent deferred-flag defects stacked on the same code.

    [A2] block2 sub_002252C0 returned 0x01096CA8

    [A4] after sub_0020DA80  esi=0x00000000  eax=0x011D4000

esi survives sub_00123590 intact and is ZERO after sub_0020DA80. sub_0020DA80 returns a perfectly good string object in eax (0x011D4000) - it does its job and destroys its caller's esi on the way out. Fifth instance of the #52 pattern: registers are C globals here, so a callee that fails to restore a callee-saved register silently corrupts every caller above it.

THE MECHANISM - PRIME SUSPECT, NOT YET PROVEN. sub_0020DA80 tail-jumps into sub_0020DA95 when its argument is non-null. Counting the lifted code:

  sub_0020DA80 prologue:  PUSH ecx, PUSH ebp, PUSH esi          = 3
  sub_0020DA95 prologue:  PUSH edi, PUSH esi                    = 2
  loc_0020DAFC epilogue:  POP edi, POP esi, POP ebp, POP ecx     = 4  (+ esp += 8)

Five pushes, four pops. The early-return path in sub_0020DA80 itself is balanced (3 pushes, 3 pops at loc_0020DA8D) and Ghidra's disassembly confirms it - 0x0020da8d POP ESI / 0x0020da90 POP EBP / 0x0020da91 POP ECX / 0x0020da92 RET 4. So the imbalance is specific to the sub_0020DA95 path.

Ghidra's epilogue for that path is 0x0020dafc MOV EAX,EDI then RET 4 at 0x0020db02 - exactly 4 bytes of gap, i.e. FOUR one-byte POPs. Against three pushes in DA80 that leaves room for only ONE push in DA95, not two. So the likeliest defect is that the lifter emitted an extra `PUSH ESI` at DA95's entry that the original does not have, which misaligns every pop: esi comes back holding whatever edi was at entry.

THAT IS A HYPOTHESIS. It is derived from instruction-length arithmetic on Ghidra's listing, not from reading the bytes at 0x0020da95-0x0020da9a. Read those bytes before changing anything - one wrong byte count here and the fix is worse than the bug.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS SITE. This is the defect the #102 CF fix exposes, and it is PRE-EXISTING - nothing about the CF fix creates it. sub_0020DA80 is called from the string-intern path that only starts hitting once the binary search works. entries.claim: The bytes REFUTE my #104 hypothesis: the lifter did not invent a PUSH ESI - sub_0020DA95's prologue really is 57 56 (PUSH EDI, PUSH ESI) and the epilogue really is 5F 5E 5D 59 (four POPs). The original x86 genuinely has FIVE saves against FOUR restores on that path, so esi returns holding the caller's edi. The lift is faithful; the register scramble is real.
entries.evidence:
Read the raw bytes rather than trusting instruction-length arithmetic, which is what #104 flagged as the risk in its own hypothesis. The hypothesis was wrong.

BYTES AT 0x0020DA80, 32 of them:

  51 55 56 8B 74 24 10 85 F6 8B E9 75 08 5E 33 C0 5D 59 C2 04 00 8B 4D 00 57 56 C7 44 24 10 00 00

Decoded:

  0x20da80  51              PUSH ECX              <- allocates local_4, not a save
  0x20da81  55              PUSH EBP
  0x20da82  56              PUSH ESI
  0x20da83  8B 74 24 10     MOV  ESI,[ESP+0x10]   <- esi = param_1
  0x20da87  85 F6           TEST ESI,ESI
  0x20da89  8B E9           MOV  EBP,ECX
  0x20da8b  75 08           JNZ  0x20da95
  0x20da8d  5E              POP  ESI
  0x20da8e  33 C0           XOR  EAX,EAX
  0x20da90  5D              POP  EBP
  0x20da91  59              POP  ECX
  0x20da92  C2 04 00        RET  4
  0x20da95  8B 4D 00        MOV  ECX,[EBP]
  0x20da98  57              PUSH EDI
  0x20da99  56              PUSH ESI
  0x20da9a  C7 44 24 10 ... MOV  dword [ESP+0x10],0   <- writes the PUSH ECX slot = local_4

BYTES AT 0x0020DAF4:

  8B 4D 00 E8 64 C8 FF FF 8B C7 5F 5E 5D 59 C2 04

  0x20daf4  8B 4D 00        MOV  ECX,[EBP]
  0x20daf7  E8 64 C8 FF FF  CALL 0x0020A360
  0x20dafc  8B C7           MOV  EAX,EDI
  0x20dafe  5F              POP  EDI
  0x20daff  5E              POP  ESI
  0x20db00  5D              POP  EBP
  0x20db01  59              POP  ECX
  0x20db02  C2 04           RET  4

WHAT THIS SETTLES. #104 guessed the lifter had invented an extra PUSH ESI at DA95's entry. It did not. `57 56` is unambiguously two one-byte pushes, and `5F 5E 5D 59` is unambiguously four one-byte pops. THE LIFT IS FAITHFUL AT BOTH ENDS. Do not "fix" the prologue or epilogue - they match the binary byte for byte.

THE ASYMMETRY IS IN THE ORIGINAL. On the 0x20da95 path the stack holds, from entry esp E downward:

  [E-4]  = pushed ECX, immediately overwritten with 0 by MOV [ESP+0x10],0  (local_4)
  [E-8]  = caller's EBP
  [E-12] = caller's ESI
  [E-16] = caller's EDI
  [E-20] = param_1        (because DA80 loaded esi = param_1 before the JNZ)

Four POPs from E-20 therefore restore, in order:

  EDI <- param_1          (harmless - EAX was already loaded from EDI at 0x20dafc)
  ESI <- caller's EDI     <- THE BUG WE MEASURED
  EBP <- caller's ESI
  ECX <- caller's EBP

That predicts esi returns holding the caller's edi, and #104 measured esi = 0 coming back into sub_00226250 - consistent if edi was 0 there, which it plausibly was after block 1. The model FITS the measurement.

The esp arithmetic still lands correctly: 4 pops from E-20 give E-4, and RET 4 takes it to E+4, which is right for a one-argument stdcall-style return. So this is purely a REGISTER scramble, not a stack leak. That is why nothing has caught it before - every esp-based instrument this project has built (RECOMP_CHECK_ABI's esp watch, find_icall_esp_saves.py) is blind to it.

sub_0020DA95 HAS EXACTLY ONE ENTRY - the JNZ at 0x20da8b. Searched the whole tree: the only reference is the tail jump in sub_0020DA80 (recomp_0015.c:37552) plus its recomp_dispatch.c registration. So there is no second caller entering with a different frame that would make the counts balance. The asymmetry is unconditional on this path.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING. That the shipped game is broken. Five saves against four restores that still returns with the right esp is a strange thing for a compiler to emit, and the more likely explanation is that ECX is NOT a save at all (it is local_4, as Ghidra names it) and the compiler deliberately restores only EDI/ESI/EBP plus one slot of cleanup - in which case the pairing is EDI<-[E-16], ESI<-[E-12], EBP<-[E-8] and the fourth POP ECX is the local's cleanup. That pairing would be CORRECT, and it is off by exactly one slot from what the stack layout above says. Which of the two readings is right depends on whether [E-20] holds param_1 or something else at 0x20dafc - i.e. whether anything between 0x20da9a and 0x20dafc pushes or pops.

NEXT, and this is now a small, bounded question: dump 0x0020da9a..0x0020dafc and account for every stack adjustment in it. If some path there pops one slot, the epilogue pairs up correctly and the esi clobber has a different cause. If nothing does, the scramble above is real and the repair is to restore esi/ebp from the correct slots.

That is the signature of a `rep movs` whose epilogue never ran. Its prologue is a normal frame (PUSH ebp; MOV ebp,esp; PUSH edi; PUSH esi) and all four of its real epilogues do POP esi/POP edi/POP ebp correctly, so the registers are only lost if control leaves without reaching one.

WHY CONTROL LEAVES. sweep_jumptables.py (which already existed - rule #15) reports:

  sub_00342AA0     table 0x00342D38  1 of 1 unregistered
       0x00342D7F
  sub_00342AA0     table 0x00342D88  4 of 4 unregistered
       0x00342D98 0x00342DA0 0x00342DB0 0x00342DC4

sub_001F87A0's erase calls memmove with dst = src - 4 - deliberately overlapping - so it takes the backward path. Before the CF fix the search always returned "not found", the erase computed a negative length and crashed inside the forward memcpy before ever reaching these tables. With the CF fix the length is sane, the backward path executes for real, and the unregistered tables fire.

So the 46-lost regression of #102 is NOT the CF fix being wrong. It is this pre-existing jump-table gap becoming reachable. Same shape as #81 and #89: a correct fix uncovering an older defect.

entries.evidence:
Checked both structures the user named, found real defects in both, seeded them, and measured. The defects are genuine; they are not this bug.

TABLE 0x00342B00 (forward path, loc_00342AE8, taken when the destination is NOT 4-aligned). Read the bytes:

  0x342AFC: FF 24 8D 80 2B 34 00   JMP [ECX*4 + 0x342B80]
  0x342B03: 90                     NOP
  0x342B04: 10 2B 34 00            -> 0x00342B10
  0x342B08: 3C 2B 34 00            -> 0x00342B3C
  0x342B0C: 60 2B 34 00            -> 0x00342B60

The lift indexes this as `MEM32(eax * 4 + 0x342B00)`, so entry[0] at 0x342B00 reads 0x9000342B - garbage - and entries 1..3 are the real targets. That is CORRECT, not a bug: the index is `edi & 3` reached only when edi is unaligned, so it is never 0.

TABLE 0x00342C8C (backward path, loc_00342C7C) has the identical shape:
entry[0] garbage, then 0x00342C9C, 0x00342CC0, 0x00342CE8.

Almost certainly because it walks entries from the stated base and stops at the first non-code value, which here is the deliberate garbage entry[0]. entries.claim: ROOT CAUSE of the sub_00205170+0x7D1 / 0xFFFF0000 wall: sub_001F7930 is called on two objects (0x01098400, 0x01098870) whose container pointer MEM32(this+0x28) is NULL. Because guest VA 0 is mapped, the NULL container yields a non-zero count from MEM32(0xC) and an element array from MEM32(0x8), so the loop dispatches virtual +0x64 on junk words of guest page 0. Index 6 happens to hold 0x0120E000 - a REAL object with the real vtable 0x003F4770 - so that dispatch succeeds, reaches sub_0020A8B0, and lands in sub_00205170, which then walks a second NULL pointer (MEM32(this+0x70) == 0) as a deferred-free array. Two stacked class-2d (mapped page 0) failures, not one.
entries.evidence:
All measured by probe in one deterministic run each; baseline restored and verified at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 kernel calls / 91 heap allocs, 2 of 2.

[1] CRASH SITE. Probes PSETUP/PSLOT inside sub_00205170: four healthy calls "this=01088A90 pool=01089A90 count=00000009" walking a real array, then "this=0120E000 pool=00000000 count=00000000". With pool NULL, ecx=MEM32(this+0x70)=0, eax=MEM32(0) reads mapped page 0 and is non-zero so the "if (eax==0) return" early-out never fires; count=eax>>3=0 makes the cursor start at guest 0x4 and the end bound edx=ecx+count*4-4 = 0xFFFFFFFC. PSLOT then shows cursor=00000004, 00000008, then "cursor=0000000C slot=00000044". That 0x44 is exactly the esi=0x00000044 in the crash register dump, and eax-edi = 0x1EDC4-0x1ED80 = 0x44 confirms it flowed into eax=edi+esi.

[2] THE DISPATCH IS LEGITIMATE FOR THE CLASS, so "wrong virtual called" is refuted. Scanned default.xbe: 0x0020A8B0 appears in exactly ONE vtable in .rdata, at 0x003F47D4 = vtable 0x003F4770 + 0x64. Probe PA8B0 in sub_0020A8B0: "this=0120E000 pool=00000000 vtbl=003F4770" - fires exactly ONCE in the whole boot, on the broken object.

So none of the twelve ever gets a pool. Their factory sub_00234E18 does operator-new 0xD0 -> ctor sub_00211490 -> icall vtable+0x24, and probe PVT24 measured that slot as 0x002036E0 on all twelve - the base-class init, which sets +0x68 and calls sub_001F5D60 but never allocates the 0x814 pool.
