  [PPRE] outer=01098870 cont=00000000 arr=00000000 idx=00000005 elem=003DA978 vt=0011DF40
  [PPRE] outer=01098870 cont=00000000 arr=00000000 idx=00000006 elem=0120E000 vt=003F4770
  [PA8B0] this=0120E000 pool=00000000 vtbl=003F4770
arr = MEM32(cont+8) = MEM32(0x8), a word of page 0 that CHANGES mid-walk (010988D8 on the first iteration, then 0). 010988D8 is exactly outer+0x68 - the embedded container's own address - which is consistent with some other NULL-container write storing "this+0x68" through a NULL base into guest VA 8. 0x003DA978 appears verbatim in triage's failed-icall list for this run, so the junk dispatches are the source of several of the 278.

[5] TOOLING LIMITATION FOUND, and it nearly produced a false finding. A trace-mode write watch (RECOMP_WATCH_TRACE, never disarms) on 0x0120E070 reported NOTHING for the whole boot - not even the guaranteed xbox_HeapAlloc zero-fill of heap page #77 (0x0120E000..0x0120F000). Watching offset 0 of the same page instead caught all three writes: "#1 = 0x00000000 from RVA=0x2E62DE75B" (our heap memset), "#2 = 0x003EEAE8 from RVA=0xE4C758" (sub_001F7CD0+0x98, base ctor), "#3 = 0x003F4770 from RVA=0xF020F1" (sub_00211490+0x121, derived ctor). A control watch on 0x01088B00 (+0xB00 in its page) DID work, so it is not simply "non-zero offsets never work" - it is unreliable. RULE: on this build, do not treat a silent trace watch at a non-zero page offset as a negative; confirm with a probe. The "+0x70 is never written" conclusion here was re-established by probe [3], not by the watch.

[6] A SECOND SELF-CORRECTION worth keeping: PENTRY read MEM32(this) at sub_00211280's entry as 0x003F4770 even for the healthy manager, which looked like it contradicted sub_00211280 living at 0x003F48E8 in a different table. It does not - the image scan in [2] shows 0x00211280 occurs at exactly one VA and 0x0020A8B0 at exactly one, so 0x01088A90 is a DERIVED instance whose base ctor had already stored 0x003F4770 and whose derived ctor had not yet overwritten it. Reading a vtable during construction tells you which ctor is running, not which class the object ends up as.

CONCLUSION AND NEXT STEP: the twelve poolless objects are a SECONDARY hazard - 0x0120E000 was never legitimately in that container, it was scavenged out of page 0. Fix the primary defect: find who is supposed to set MEM32(this+0x28) = this+0x68 on 0x01098400 and 0x01098870 and why it did not run. sub_00205170 also has no NULL-pool guard and cannot get one honestly, because on real hardware MEM32(0) would fault; the honest instrument is the RECOMP_TRAP_PAGE_ZERO census build, which would have caught both derefs immediately.

entries.claim: ANSWERS #114's open question, and REFUTES its "this+0x68" framing. Nothing is supposed to set MEM32(this+0x28) = this+0x68 - 0x68 is just the allocation stride of this 0x64-byte class, so "container == owner+0x68" was the bump allocator handing out the next block, not a structural relationship. The real store is MEM32(esi+0x28) = sub_00222600(0) inside the factory sub_00222708, and it SUCCEEDS on every object that goes through it. The two NULL-container outers 0x01098400 and 0x01098870 are never constructed at all: they are raw 0x68-stride slots returned by the ALT path of sub_002226E0, which is taken once the guard byte at MEM32(0x5BC508) flips 0 -> 1 (written by sub_002366BC+0xB1, itself in the crash backtrace).
entries.evidence:
All by probe, each in a deterministic run; tree stripped and re-verified at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 / 278 / 91 / 8, deterministic 2 of 2.

[1] THE CLASS AND THE STORE. Probe POUTER at sub_001F7930's entry: all nine calls carry vtable 0x003F5D88, one class. Six healthy (cont = a real container, and MEM32(outer+0x68) = 0x003EEF28, the container class vtable), three broken: outer=00000004 vtbl=00000000, outer=01098400 cont=00000000, outer=01098870 cont=00000000.
Three sites write vtable 0x3F5D88: sub_00216EE0 (plain ctor, which explicitly does MEM32(esi+0x28) = 0), sub_0022229A, and sub_00222708. sub_00222708 is the real factory: allocate 0x64 via sub_001F7E00, base ctor sub_001F7CD0, sub_00216EE0, then eax = sub_00222600(0) and MEM32(esi + 0x28) = eax.

[2] THE FACTORY NEVER FAILS. Probe PSTORE on that store fired 7 times, container non-NULL every time, guard byte 0 every time: obj=01091AB0 cont=01096B88, 01096BB8/01096C20, 01097498/01096BA0, 01097518/01097580, 01097728/01097790, 010977C0/01097828, 01097858/010978C0. Neither 01098400 nor 01098870 is in that list. So "sub_00222600 returned NULL" is REFUTED.

[3] THE TWO OUTERS ARE NEVER CONSTRUCTED. Probe PBASE inside sub_00216EE0 fired on exactly 8 objects - the 7 above plus one STACK address, 00F7FD98 - and on neither of the two. Probe PCOPY in sub_0022229A fired ZERO times, so that path is dead this boot. Yet POUTER read MEM32(0x01098400) as a valid 0x003F5D88. So their vtable word is not written by any constructor that ran.

[4] WHERE THEY COME FROM. Probes PC1/PC2 on both call sites of sub_001F7930: all nine calls come from sub_002235D0 (loc_0022379A, ecx = esi), none from sub_00209610. In sub_002235D0, esi = MEM32(ebx) at loc_00223698, cached from sub_002226E0's return.
sub_002226E0 has the same shape as sub_00222600: eax = MEM32(0x5BC508); if (MEM8(eax) == 0) tail-jump to the real factory sub_00222708, else take an alt path through sub_00209650(0x2221E0) and sub_0020E520 on MEM32(0x5BC274).
Probe PALT on the alt path's return, verbatim:
  eax=00000000 guardb=01
  eax=010982C8 guardb=01
  eax=01098330 guardb=01
  eax=01098398 guardb=01
  eax=01098400 guardb=01   <- immediately followed by [PC2] this=01098400
  eax=010985B0 guardb=01
  eax=01098870 guardb=01   <- immediately followed by [PC2] this=01098870
The returns are spaced exactly 0x68 apart. That stride is also why the healthy objects showed cont == outer+0x68 - consecutive blocks of the same 0x64-byte class, nothing structural. #114's "embedded sub-object at +0x68" reading is withdrawn.

[5] THE SWITCH. Trace watch on the guard, at page offset 0 so it is in the reliable regime: "[WATCH:guard] armed on xbox VA 0x01086000; current value 0x00000000", then #1 = 0 from RVA=0x3012DE75B (heap zero-fill, system DLL), #2 = 0 from RVA=0xF1D7E7 = sub_002154F0+0xB7, #3 = 1 from RVA=0x17C6561 = sub_002366BC+0xB1. sub_002366BC is already in the crash backtrace at +0x14B, so the flip is a legitimate state transition, not corruption.

[6] THE ALT PATH IS FULLY LIFTED - no stub explanation. sub_002221E0, sub_002225B0, sub_0020E520 and sub_00209650 are all real defined functions in gen/, none in recomp_stubs_unresolved.c. sub_002221E0 is a descriptor thunk: it pushes (0, 0x5BC274, 0x2264D0, 0x1A4340, 0x1F19C0, 0x3F9734, 0x64, 0x219A10, 0x221F50, 0, 0x46B2C4) and calls sub_002235D0 - so sub_002235D0 is a generic parameterised "register/create this type" routine, 0x64 is the object size and 0x219A10 the per-type constructor callback.

NEXT: sub_00219A10 is that callback and it constructs into a STACK buffer (esp -= 0x64; ecx = esp + 4; call sub_00216EE0), which is exactly the single stack construction PBASE caught at 00F7FD98. Determine whether the pool slots the alt path hands out are ever meant to be constructed in place, and by what - the slots at 0x010982C8..0x01098870 demonstrably never see sub_00216EE0. Start at sub_0020E520 on registry 0x5BC274 and at sub_002235D0's use of the 0x219A10 callback.

entries.claim: REFUTES my own #115 next-step: sub_00219A10 is NOT a per-instance constructor. sub_002235D0 is a generic TYPE-DESCRIPTOR REGISTRATION routine taking 11 args, and it calls the 0x219A10 callback exactly ONCE per registration, with no `this` prepared, storing its return value into MEM32(descriptor + 0x5C). The measured return is a VTABLE POINTER every time, so 0x219A10 is a "get this type's vtable" helper - it constructs a throwaway instance on the stack and reads the vtable word back out at the offset MEM32(MEM32(0x5BC508) + 0x394). Nothing in sub_002235D0 constructs the descriptor slots themselves; the defect stays in sub_002226E0's alt path, which returns raw storage where a constructed descriptor is required.
entries.evidence:
Read plus one probe run, deterministic; tree stripped and re-verified at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 / 278 / 91 / 8, deterministic 2 of 2.

[1] ARGUMENT MAP. sub_002221E0 pushes 11 args and cleans 0x2C. In sub_002235D0, `esp -= 0x108` plus four callee-saved pushes puts arg_n at esp + 0x11C + 4n. Every slot is accounted for, and the map is self-consistent with the values sub_002221E0 pushes:
  0x11C arg0  = 0          -> MEM8(esi+0x1A); GATES the 0x219A10 call (`if non-zero goto loc_0022372B`, skipping it)
  0x120 arg1  = 0x5BC274   -> ebx, the get-or-create singleton cell; MEM32(ebx) is the descriptor
  0x124 arg2  = 0x2264D0   -> icall at loc_002236DC, result into ebp
  0x128 arg3  = 0x1A4340   -> icall at loc_002236E3, result passed to sub_00216FD0 on the descriptor
  0x12C arg4  = 0x1F19C0   -> MEM32(esi + 0x54)
  0x130 arg5  = 0x3F9734   -> edi, the type NAME (the strlen + rep movsd block copies it)
  0x134 arg6  = 0x64       -> MEM32(esi + 0x48), the instance SIZE
  0x138 arg7  = 0x219A10   -> icall at loc_00223721, return into MEM32(esi + 0x5C)
  0x13C arg8  = 0x221F50   -> icall at loc_00223736 if non-zero
  0x140 arg9  = 0
  0x144 arg10 = 0x46B2C4
Then loc_0022379A calls sub_001F7930 on the descriptor. So the object sub_001F7930 walks is a TYPE DESCRIPTOR, not an allocator instance.

[2] THE CALLBACK RETURNS A VTABLE. Probe PCB on `MEM32(esi + 0x5C) = eax`, all nine registrations in the boot:
  desc=01096BB8 ret=003EEAE8 size=00000008 cont28=01096C20
  desc=01091AB0 ret=003F5D88 size=00000064 cont28=01096B88
  desc=01097518 ret=003EEED0 size=00000010 cont28=01097580
  desc=01097728 ret=003F7EA0 size=00000044 cont28=01097790
  desc=01097498 ret=003EEF28 size=00000010 cont28=01096BA0
  desc=01098398 ret=003E0CC4 size=00000014 cont28=00000000
  desc=01098400 ret=003F7C90 size=00000034 cont28=00000000
  desc=010985B0 ret=003F7DB0 size=00000050 cont28=00000000
  desc=01098870 ret=003F79C0 size=00000034 cont28=00000000
Every return value is a .rdata vtable, and the size field differs per type (8, 0x64, 0x10, 0x44, 0x10, 0x14, 0x34, 0x50, 0x34), so sub_002235D0 registers MANY types and sub_002221E0 is only one of its descriptor thunks. This also matches sub_00219A10's body exactly: `esp -= 0x64; ecx = esp + 4; call sub_00216EE0` builds a temporary, then `ecx = MEM32(MEM32(0x5BC508) + 0x394); esi = MEM32(esp + ecx + 4)` reads one word back out of it and returns that. Reading the vtable out of a throwaway instance is what a metaclass does when it needs a type's vtable without an instance. The stack construction at 00F7FD98 that #115 recorded is this, and nothing more.

[3] SELF-CONSISTENCY WORTH NOTING. The registration for size 0x64 returns vtable 0x003F5D88 - the very class all nine descriptors belong to. So descriptor 01091AB0 is the descriptor FOR the descriptor class; the metaclass registers itself. That is why the raw alt-path slots read 0x003F5D88 in their first word despite never running sub_00216EE0: they are descriptor-class storage that the alt path fills in piecemeal (+0x48 size, +0x5C vtable) without ever constructing.

[4] CONCLUSION. The four descriptors with cont28 == 0 are exactly the raw 0x68-stride slots #115 caught coming out of sub_002226E0's alt path. sub_002235D0 does its job on them - it writes name, size and the callback fields - but it never creates the +0x28 member container, because that is the factory sub_00222708's job via sub_00222600, and the alt path bypasses the factory entirely.

NEXT, and now narrow: sub_0020E520 called on registry MEM32(0x5BC274), and sub_00209650(0x2221E0). One of those is meant to hand back a CONSTRUCTED descriptor once the guard byte at MEM32(0x5BC508) is 1. Determine which, and why it returns raw storage. Do NOT go back to sub_00219A10 or to the twelve poolless allocator objects - both are settled dead ends.

entries.claim: THE LOOP IS CLOSED. sub_0020E520/sub_0020E547 is the generic "create an instance of type T" path: it picks an allocator, allocates MEM32(desc+0x48) + MEM32(desc+0x20) bytes, and calls sub_002096B0, which installs the vtable from desc+0x5C, sets refcount 1, and registers with the owning allocator - but runs NO constructor. A type only gets a real constructor if its descriptor supplies a creation override at MEM32(desc+0x3C), and that field is measured ZERO on all 15 calls, so the override path never runs and every descriptor born this way has +0x28 == NULL. The page-0 poisoning of #114 is then self-inflicted by sub_00216FD0, the inheritance step: it appends the parent's members through the child's NULL container, doing MEM32(esi+0xC) = count and MEM32(MEM32(esi+8) + i*4) = member with esi = 0 - which writes exactly the guest 0x8 and 0xC words that sub_001F7930 later reads back as a fake array pointer and fake count.
entries.evidence:
Probes PE520 and PE547 in one deterministic run; tree stripped and re-verified at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 / 278 / 91 / 8, deterministic 2 of 2.

[1] THE PATH. sub_002226E0's alt path calls sub_0020E520 with ecx = MEM32(0x5BC274) (the descriptor) and forwards the caller's argument. sub_0020E520 walks an override chain at MEM32(esi+0x3C) - `node = call(node); while (node->0x3C)` - and when it is empty falls to loc_0020E53B, where `MEM8(esi+0x1A) != 1` tail-jumps to sub_0020E547. sub_0020E547 picks an allocator (desc+0x60 by name via sub_001E9B80, else the default sub_001F5C20), then allocates `MEM32(desc+0x48) + MEM32(desc+0x20)` through allocator vtable+0xCC and calls sub_002096B0(instance, desc).

[2] sub_002096B0 IS NOT A CONSTRUCTOR. It does: ecx = MEM32(MEM32(0x5BC508) + 0x394); MEM32(esi + ecx) = MEM32(desc + 0x5C) - installing the vtable that the 0x219A10 callback produced in #116 - then MEM32(esi+4) = 1, then icall vtable+0x50, then sub_001E8E20 to find the owning allocator and icall its vtable+0x160, storing a byte at +7. Slot +0x50 is a two-instruction getter, not a ctor: for the descriptor class it is sub_00216F70, and the sibling vtable 0x003F4770 has sub_00211480 in the same slot, both `eax = MEM32(global); ret`. So the instance is blessed and registered, never constructed. This is also why the raw slots read a valid vtable at +0 while probe PBASE proved sub_00216EE0 never ran on them.

[3] THE OVERRIDE IS ALWAYS ABSENT. Probe PE520 at sub_0020E520's entry, all 15 calls, chain3C is 00000000 on every single one:
  desc=010977C0 chain3C=0 flag1A=01 size48=00000038 off20=0 cont28=01097828
  desc=01097728 chain3C=0 flag1A=00 size48=00000044 off20=0 cont28=01097790
  desc=01091AB0 chain3C=0 flag1A=00 size48=00000064 off20=0 cont28=01096B88   (x7)
  desc=01097498 chain3C=0 flag1A=00 size48=00000010 off20=0 cont28=01096BA0
  desc=01098400 chain3C=0 flag1A=00 size48=00000034 off20=0 cont28=00000000   (x4)
sub_00216EE0 explicitly zeroes MEM32(esi + 0x3C) along with +0x30/0x34/0x38/0x40/0x44, so the field starts at 0 and nothing observed ever fills it.

[4] THE SLOTS ARE DESCRIPTORS, AND ONE IS THEN USED AS ONE. Probe PE547 at loc_0020E582, immediately after the allocation:
  desc=01091AB0 reqsize=00000064 -> block=01098260, 010982C8, 01098330, 01098398, 01098400, 010985B0, 01098870
  desc=01098400 reqsize=00000034 -> block=01098508, 01098540, 01098578, 01098468
  desc=01097728 reqsize=00000044 -> block=010981B8, 01098720
  desc=01097498 reqsize=00000010 -> block=00000000   (one allocation genuinely FAILED)
The size-0x64 blocks are exactly the values probe PALT reported in #115, so 0x01098400 and 0x01098870 are new descriptor instances minted through the descriptor-class descriptor 0x01091AB0. And 0x01098400, itself container-less, is then used as the descriptor for four further allocations - a half-built descriptor in live service.
CORRECTION to #115: off20 is 0 on every call, so the 0x68 stride is the allocator rounding 0x64 up, not a header offset. My "0x64 + 4" reading is withdrawn.

[5] WHO POISONS GUEST 0x8 AND 0xC - #114's missing writer. sub_00216FD0(child = ecx, parent = arg) is the inheritance step called from sub_002235D0 at loc_002236EC. It copies the parent's +0x5C/+0x58/+0x20/+0x48 into the child, then loops over the parent's members and appends each to the CHILD's container:
    esi = MEM32(esi + 0x28);                       /* child's container - NULL here */
    ebx = MEM32(esi + 8);  ecx = MEM32(esi + 0xC);
    ...
    MEM32(MEM32(esi + 8) + eax * 4) = ebp;  MEM32(esi + 0xC) = ebx;
With esi = 0 that reads and writes guest 0x8 and 0xC directly. Those are precisely the two words #114 measured sub_001F7930 reading back as the fake element array and fake count, and it explains why MEM32(0x8) CHANGED mid-walk. Same class-2d silence: guest page 0 is mapped, so none of it faults.

[6] SIDE OBSERVATION - a dead manual guard, #91 class. In sub_0020E520 at loc_0020E53B the original unguarded line `if (CMP_NE(MEM8(esi + 0x1A), 1)) { sub_0020E547(); return; }` still sits ABOVE the manual heap-range guard that was meant to replace it, so the guard is unreachable. Harmless here because the original does the right thing for a valid esi, but it is the same insert-after-instead-of-replace defect as #91 and should be collapsed. sub_0020E520 also carries FOUR duplicated copies of the same "esi from ecx" guard, the #89 accumulation problem again.

NEXT: find what is supposed to write MEM32(descriptor + 0x3C). It is the single field that separates a properly constructed descriptor from the raw ones. Secondarily, sub_00216FD0 should not append through a NULL container - but that is a symptom, not the cause.

entries.claim: NOTHING writes MEM32(descriptor + 0x3C) for this type, and #117's next-step framing was wrong: +0x3C is a type-REDIRECTION chain for abstract types (paired with the abstract flag at +0x1A), not a construction override, so its absence is CORRECT. The generic create path's own construction hook does exist - sub_002096B0 tail-jumps to sub_002096FD, which icalls vtable+0x24 and vtable+0x1C, the same two virtuals the bootstrap factory sub_00222708 runs - but for the descriptor class those slots are do-nothing stubs (0x0013D370 and 0x0015FDF0) in the REAL game vtable, read from the XBE. The per-field initialiser sub_001EA5A0 also runs correctly with valid inputs and all 25 of its member hooks resolve, so none of the three candidate mechanisms creates the +0x28 member container. The asymmetry between the bootstrap and self-hosted paths is real and its resolution is NOT yet found.
entries.evidence:
Static search, XBE disassembly and two probe runs; tree stripped and re-verified at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 / 278 / 91 / 8, deterministic 2 of 2.

[1] NO WRITER EXISTS. 909 writes to +0x3C tree-wide, 834 non-zero, but almost all are esp-relative stack locals. Restricting to non-esp writes in the 0x001E0000-0x00240000 band leaves 88. Only 8 references to registry 0x5BC274 exist in the whole tree and NONE writes +0x3C. Our type's setup thunk is sub_00221F50 (arg8 of sub_002221E0, icalled by sub_002235D0 at loc_00223736); its only 0x3C references are MEM8(ebp + 0x3C) on MEMBER objects, not on the descriptor. sub_002235D0 itself never references +0x28 or +0x3C at all - verified by listing every call and every 0x28 reference in its 373 lines.

[2] WHAT +0x3C ACTUALLY IS. The idiom exists for other types: sub_002263F0 does `eax = MEM32(0x5BC190); MEM32(eax + 0x3C) = 0x2263C0;` after adding members, and ~15 similar sites store a nearby code address. In sub_0020E520 the field is consumed as `eax = MEM32(esi+0x3C); if (eax) { call eax; esi = eax; repeat }` - call it, take the RESULT as a new descriptor, loop. That is abstract-to-concrete type redirection, gated alongside `if (MEM8(esi + 0x1A) != 1)` (the abstract flag, which is arg0 of sub_002235D0). A directly instantiable type correctly has 0 here. Probe PE520 measured chain3C = 0 on all 15 calls and flag1A = 1 on exactly one descriptor (010977C0), consistent with that reading.

[3] THE CONSTRUCTION HOOK DOES EXIST, AND IS STUBBED FOR THIS CLASS. sub_002096B0 ends `tail jmp sub_002096FD`, which I had not read. sub_002096FD calls sub_001EA5A0, sub_001EA600, sub_001EA6B0, then icalls vtable+0x24 and vtable+0x1C - the SAME two virtuals sub_00222708 runs right after `MEM32(esi + 0x28) = sub_00222600(0)`. So the generic path is structurally capable of initialising. But reading the real vtable out of default.xbe, descriptor class 0x003F5D88 has +0x24 = 0x0013D370 and +0x1C = 0x0015FDF0, both shared do-nothing stubs. Not a lifting artefact - that is the shipped vtable.
Also confirmed by disassembly that +0x50 is a getter, not a ctor: 0x00216F70 is `mov eax, [0x5BC274]; ret` and its sibling 0x00211480 is `mov eax, [0x5BC498]; ret`. GetTypeDescriptor. Ledger #78's old note about sub_00216F70 being a genuine two-instruction getter is CONFIRMED, not stale.

[4] THE PER-FIELD INITIALISER RUNS CORRECTLY. sub_001EA5A0 gets the instance's descriptor via vtable+0x50, then walks that type's member list from the BASE type's count (MEM32(0x5BC554) - the registry that sub_002264D0, a sibling descriptor thunk, registers) up to its own, calling member->vtable+0x7C on the new instance. Probe PINITF, for every new descriptor:
  inst=01098260/010982C8/01098330/01098398/01098400/010985B0/01098870
  desc=003F5D88 desccont=01096B88 basedesc=01096BB8 basecont=01096C20 thiscount=0000001B basecount=00000002
Valid inputs; 0x1B - 2 = 25 members iterated, exactly the 0x19 that sub_00221F50 adds.
Probe PHOOK on the hook target: all 25 resolve, to only two real functions - 0x0015FDF0 (the shared no-op) and 0x001EB200. NO failed icall among them. So "a missing member-init hook is the bug" is REFUTED, and none of these hooks builds a container.

[5] THE CASCADE, MEASURED. PINITF also caught instances whose descriptor IS the broken 0x01098400: `desc=003F7C90 desccont=00000000 thiscount=00000016 / 00000016 / 00000017 / 0000002E`. With desccont NULL, `ebx = MEM32(edi + 0xC)` reads guest 0xC, so the member count comes out of page 0 and CHANGES between calls, and the loop then dispatches +0x7C on page-0 junk - PHOOK caught one such: `mvt=000E8000 hook=84846850`. So one container-less descriptor poisons every instance of its type. Another contributor to the 278 failed icalls.

CONCLUSION AND NEXT. Three candidate mechanisms are now eliminated: +0x3C redirection (correctly absent), the vtable+0x24/+0x1C init virtuals (genuinely stubs in the shipped vtable), and the member +0x7C hooks (all resolve, none constructs). The container is created ONLY by the bootstrap factory sub_00222708 via sub_00222600. So the strongest remaining hypothesis is TIMING: the guard byte at MEM32(0x5BC508), set 0 -> 1 by sub_002366BC+0xB1 (#115), flips too early in our boot, so descriptors that the real game would still build through the bootstrap factory get built through the self-hosted path instead. Investigate what sub_002366BC is supposed to have completed before +0xB1, and whether anything it depends on is inert in our port. Do NOT re-chase +0x3C, sub_00219A10, sub_002096B0's vtable+0x50, or the member hooks.

entries.claim: sub_002366BC is the bulk TYPE-REGISTRATION DRIVER and the guard flip at +0xB1 is CORRECT BY DESIGN: it registers the descriptor class itself via sub_00209650(0x2221E0), then sets MEM8(ebp) = 1 to switch the metaclass to self-hosting, then drives ~23 more type thunks. So "the guard flips too early" is REFUTED - the metaclass is fully built before the flip. Separately, faithful.py found a REAL deferred-flag miscompile in the same function at 0x002367CA (bug class 1, which ledger #56 recorded as swept clean - that claim was stale because this site lives in recomp_seed.c, outside the gen/ sweep). Fixed and KEPT, but it is currently UNEXERCISED: a probe proves loc_002367C1 is never reached, because the boot crashes earlier inside the registration sequence it drives.
entries.evidence:
Read, XBE disassembly, faithful.py and two probe runs; tree rebuilt and verified at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 / 278 / 91 / 8, deterministic 2 of 2, with the fix in place.

[1] WHAT sub_002366BC DOES. It is a driver that calls sub_00209650(thunk) about 24 times, one per type-descriptor thunk, in this order:
  sub_00209650(0x2221E0)      <- the DESCRIPTOR CLASS itself, registered while the guard is still 0, so sub_002226E0 tail-jumps to the real factory sub_00222708 and the descriptor gets its +0x28 container. This is the object probe POUTER measured as 0x01091AB0 with cont28 = 0x01096B88.

entries.claim: The boot dies during the FIRST post-flip registration. sub_002366BC drives ~23 type thunks after the guard flip but only the first, sub_00220870, ever runs - the remaining 22 (0x2361A0, 0x231820, 0x236280, ...) never execute at all. By the seventh (0x01098870) that word had been overwritten to 0, so the junk walk landed on a real object and faulted. Chasing "which registration crashes" is therefore a dead end - only the missing +0x28 container matters.

entries.claim: ANSWERED, and it was a class-2b defect, not a NULL pool base. CORRECTS #121: sub_001186A0's pool base is not NULL, it is `NULL + 0x16C` - the OWNING OBJECT is null and the trees are embedded in it. Traced up: sub_0011E980 receives a GOOD this (0x005024D0, a static object) and has it destroyed by the single call in between, sub_0011E0F0, which does `push esi; xor esi,esi` and relies on a `pop esi` that lives in a later fragment. One branch of that chain reaches sub_0011E13C, which did not exist - it was a generic `g_esp += 4` stub that skipped `pop edi; pop esi` entirely. Seeded it. kernel_calls 274 -> 338, failed_icalls 278 -> 273, heap_allocs 91 -> 92, and the crash leaves the page-0 junk walk for the real construction path.

  0011E13C  dec eax
  0011E13D  mov [ecx + eax*4 + 0x164], edx
  0011E144  inc edx

  0011E148  jl  0x11e110
  0011E14A  pop edi
  0011E14B  pop esi

So `edx = MEM32(ecx)` on 0xFFFFFFFC is the faulting read.

Across 13 calls: icont=0x01097790 (icount=25, stable, healthy) 3x; icont=0x01096B88 (icount=27 once, then icount=0 six times); icont=0x00000000 (NULL container, the #117/#118 defect) 3x, the last fatal with icount=0x18000001. This rules out object/address reuse (a destroyed-and-reallocated object would show a different vtable or array pointer) - it is a surgical zero of exactly the count word on a live, otherwise-untouched object. STEP 3: probed inside sub_001EA5A0's own dispatch loop (loc_001EA5E3 entry and loc_001EA5EF exit) unconditionally, capturing the container id and MEM32(0x01096B94) at every one of the 27 field-dispatch iterations for container 0x01096B88 - the global word reads 27 at every single iteration, never dropping mid-loop, and the loop completes cleanly (esi 2->27). STEP 4: read the raw stderr.txt around the loop boundary (grep for the loop's last iteration then the next probe hit). Between them sits exactly one anomaly: `[ICALL] Failed to resolve VA 0x00000064 (total calls: 23000)` with a 16-entry \"recent ICALL targets\" ring buffer that decodes (little-endian, per-dword ASCII) to fragments of RTTI type-name strings (\"...UnsignedShortArrayMetaField...\", \"...VirtualFuncMetaField...\", \"Manager...\") - i.e. a vtable dispatch chain that walked off a real vtable into a type-name string table and called through several consecutive \"pointers\" that are actually string bytes, ending on the small integer 0x64. The failure's native call stack, resolved against build/xmen_legends_recomp.map: sub_00209750+0x77 <- sub_002281E0+0x2AA <- sub_00220A00+0x215 <- sub_002096FD+0x4A2 <- sub_00238309+0x3DB <- sub_00236930+0x589 <- sub_00239F40+0xD29 <- sub_00011FF0+0 (entry thunk). sub_00209750 dispatches FIVE vtable icalls on its `this` (vtable+0x48 conditionally, then +4, +0x2C, +0x1C, +0x50 unconditionally) and vtable slot +0x50 is the SAME slot sub_001EA5A0 itself calls at entry to fetch a descriptor - so this is the same descriptor-fetch mechanism, just on a DIFFERENT (corrupted) `this`. sub_002096FD and sub_00236930/sub_00239F40 are the exact functions #119-#123 already identified as the type-registration driver family (sub_002366BC's dispatcher and its neighbours) - this is that same cascade moving on to register the NEXT type after finishing 0x01096B88's class, and walking a bad pointer while doing it.

REAL EFFECT MEASURED, not just theoretical: stderr's own `[COVERAGE]` summary shows callsites 421 -> 418 (reached stays 147, the indirect-dispatch metric, unaffected as expected since #73 established it only counts RECOMP_ICALL - this fix only removes DIRECT RECOMP_ABI_CALL sites). entries.claim: The member zero-fill hook sub_001EB200 is NOT the writer that zeroes descriptor container 0x01096B88's count - REFUTED by direct measurement of all 48 of its destinations. Separately CONFIRMED against Ghidra ground truth: +0x28 is built ONLY in sub_002226E0's pre-flip inline body, and both that factory AND the container builder sub_00222600 delegate to the generic path sub_0020E520 once the guard flips. Also found a 14th sub_001EA5A0 call at this=010981B8 that #123's inner probe never saw, and bracketed the count flip to the window between instance 0x01098260 and instance 0x01099050 with NO member-hook activity in between.

The FUN_001f7d30 / FUN_00204100 second entry into sub_001EA5A0 is NOT the count writer - it never executes at all in this boot (probe fired zero times), so ledger #127's "open lead" is dead. ALSO CORRECTS #127: its claim of "a 14th sub_001EA5A0 call at 0x010981B8 that #123 never saw" is WRONG - there are 13 calls, exactly as #123 reported; #123 printed only the tail of its list, so 0x010981B8 was already in its set and was simply not displayed.
entries.evidence:
METHOD: two probes in one build - [PF7D] at sub_001F7D30's entry printing this, desc, the dynamic vtable offset MEM32(MEM32(0x5BC508)+0x394) and the live count MEM32(0x1096B94); and [PIEA] re-placed at sub_001EA5A0's entry to correlate. Probes stripped afterwards, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 338 / failed_icalls 273 / heap_allocs 92 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0.

[1] THE LEAD IS DEAD. [PF7D] fired ZERO times. sub_001F7D30 is never entered during the boot, so neither of its two calls to sub_001EA5A0 ever happens, and it cannot be the writer that zeroes 0x01096B94. Ghidra confirms its only caller is FUN_00204100, so that whole branch is inert here. Every one of the 13 sub_001EA5A0 calls comes from FUN_002096b0, i.e. the path #123 already probed. Do NOT re-chase sub_001F7D30 or sub_00204100 for this question.

[2] SELF-CORRECTION OF #127. [PIEA] again produced exactly 13 lines:
  010981B8 cnt=1B, 01098260 cnt=1B, 01099050 cnt=0, 010990B8 cnt=0, 01099100 cnt=0,
  01099148 cnt=0, 010991B0 cnt=0, 01099248 cnt=0, 010992B0 cnt=0, 01099368 cnt=0,
  01099468 cnt=0, 011D0008 cnt=0, 00000008 cnt=0
That is 13, and ledger #123 also reported 13 calls. #123's evidence block is headed "ALL 13 CALLS, tail shown" and explicitly displays only the tail, beginning at 01098260 - so 0x010981B8 was always inside its 13 and was merely not printed. #127's statement that this was "a 14th call that #123's inner probe never saw" is a MISCOUNT on my part, caused by comparing my full list against #123's displayed subset rather than against its stated count. The two probes agree; there is no discrepancy and no extra call. Everything else in #127 stands - the PZERO refutation, the Ghidra +0x28 finding, and the bracketing of the flip between 01098260 and 01099050 are all unaffected, since none of them depended on the call count.

[3] LESSON WORTH KEEPING: a prior entry's DISPLAYED evidence is not its full evidence. #123 said 13 and showed 12; I read the shown rows as the whole set. Compare against the stated count, or re-measure, before announcing a new observation. Same family as the head-limited-grep trap recorded at ledger #79.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN: the count writer is still unidentified. It runs between the initialisation of instance 0x01098260 and instance 0x01099050, it is not a member zero-fill hook (#127), not sub_00209470 or sub_00202B87 (#124), and not sub_001F7D30 (this entry). The one unexplored signal is #127's inconclusive watch hit showing a write from a system DLL, i.e. a native memset/memcpy in our own runtime rather than lifted guest code - which would make this a PORT defect. That is now the strongest remaining hypothesis by elimination, and it has not been tested.

entries.claim: THE COUNT WRITER IS FOUND, and it is not corruption: the container 0x01096B88 is itself run through per-member DEFAULT INITIALISATION while already populated. sub_001E9E60 (a memcpy hook, vtable+0x68) copies member 0x010976F0's 4-byte default over inst+0xC with inst = 0x01096B88 - i.e. the container's own count field is reset to its default of 0. This also CORRECTS #123's framing that the count collapse and the missing +0x28 container were two separate defects: they are the same root cause, because a post-flip descriptor with a NULL +0x28 ends up sharing the metaclass's container. Also refines #127: the system-DLL RIP was real but meant only that the lifter emits guest rep movsd as native memcpy - it is lifted GUEST code, NOT a port-runtime defect.
entries.evidence:
METHOD: a three-stage bisect, each stage one build+run. All probes stripped afterwards; rebuilt and verified deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 338 / failed_icalls 273 / heap_allocs 92 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0, tree clean.

[1] STAGE ONE - which call in sub_002096FD. Six probes (PA/PB/PC/PD/PE/PG) at every label of sub_002096FD printing MEM32(0x1096B94). The flip is inside sub_001EA6B0, during the initialisation of instance 0x01098260:
  [PA] entry this=010981B8 cnt=1B ... [PG] exit cnt=1B      <- first instance, count survives
  [PA] entry this=01098260 cnt=1B
  [PB] postEA5A0  cnt=0000001B
  [PC] postEA600  cnt=0000001B
  [PD] postEA6B0  cnt=00000000    <- flipped inside sub_001EA6B0
  [PE] post1C     cnt=00000000
Every later instance enters with cnt already 0.

[2] STAGE TWO - which member. sub_001EA6B0 is the same member-walk shape as sub_001EA5A0 but dispatches vtable+0x68 / +0x70 / +0x6C per member according to a kind tag at member+0x24, gated by an icall on member vtable +0xE8. Probe [PM] after each dispatch printed member, member vtable, kind and the count. The count holds at 0x1B through member 0x01097698 (kind=03, mvt=003F7DB0) and reads 0 immediately after member 0x010976F0 (kind=00, mvt=003F7C90). kind=00 selects vtable+0x68, and MEM32(0x003F7C90 + 0x68) read out of default.xbe via Ghidra is 60 9E 1E 00 = 0x001E9E60.

[3] WHAT sub_001E9E60 IS. Ghidra and the lifted C agree instruction-for-instruction - it is the per-member DEFAULT-VALUE COPY:
    uVar1  = *(ushort *)(in_ECX + 0x14);              /* length  */
    puVar3 = *(undefined4 **)(in_ECX + 0x20);         /* source: member's stored default */
    puVar4 = (undefined4 *)(*(int *)(in_ECX + 8) + param_1);  /* dest: instance + member offset */
    rep movsd / rep movsb
The lifted C emits both loops as native memcpy() calls. THAT EXPLAINS #127's WATCH HIT: the write really did execute inside a system DLL, but only because the lifter lowers guest rep movsd to CRT memcpy. So #127's "this may be a PORT defect rather than game behaviour" is REFUTED - this is ordinary lifted guest code, and the RIP being outside our module proves nothing about origin. Any future watch hit landing in a system DLL must be read the same way.

[4] STAGE THREE - the destination, measured. Probe [PCPY] at sub_001E9E60's entry printed member, the instance argument, the member offset and the length for all 55 calls. Exactly one call covers the count word, and it is unambiguous:
  [PCPY] m=010976F0 inst=01096B88 off=0000000C len=0004   ->  dest = 01096B94..01096B98
THE INSTANCE IS THE CONTAINER ITSELF. 0x01096B88 is not a bystander being overwritten by a stray pointer - it is being passed to the constructor AS the object under construction, and member 0x010976F0 legitimately lives at offset +0xC, which is the container's count. The hook does exactly what it is supposed to do: write that member's default value, 0. Nothing is corrupt, mis-sized or mis-aimed; the wrong OBJECT is being initialised.

[5] WHY THIS UNIFIES TWO OPEN THREADS. #123 recorded the count collapse and the missing +0x28 container as separate defects and that is now wrong. Post-flip descriptors have a NULL +0x28 (#125/#127, and confirmed in Ghidra: FUN_002226e0 stores piVar1[10] = FUN_00222600(0) only in its pre-flip inline body). With no container of its own, the construction path for descriptor 0x01098260 reaches the metaclass's shared container 0x01096B88 and runs default-init across it, wiping the 27 members that the pre-flip bootstrap had put there. So the "second, cleanest lead" of #123 is a SYMPTOM of the +0x28 gap, not an independent bug. Fixing +0x28 should remove the count collapse for free; they must not be worked as two tickets.

[6] SCOPE NOTE, not glossed: 55 memcpy calls happen and only ONE lands on the container. The other 54 are ordinary member defaults written into genuine instances. So this is a single mis-targeted construction, not a systemic mis-aim - consistent with exactly one descriptor (0x01098260) being the first post-flip type whose construction dereferences the shared container.

STILL OPEN: why the construction of 0x01098260 selects 0x01096B88 as the object to default-initialise. The likely mechanism is the NULL +0x28 falling back to the metaclass container, but the fallback site itself has not been probed and must be before any fix is attempted.

entries.claim: THE FALLBACK IS NOT A FALLBACK - it is register corruption from a NESTED NULL-object recursion. sub_002096FD enters with this=0x01098260 and calls sub_001EA6B0 with this=0x01096B88, because sub_001EA600 (called between them) returns with esi destroyed. Cause measured exactly: at member 0x01096FA0 (iteration 0x0B) the +0x74 hook recurses into sub_001EA600 with this=0 and a NULL container, and that nested call leaves esp 0x14 (20 bytes) lower, so the outer epilogue's four POPs read the wrong stack slots and restore esi = 0x01096B88. This CORRECTS ledger #129 part (5): the container is not selected by a designed NULL-+0x28 fallback.
entries.evidence:
METHOD: four more probe builds after #129, each stripped afterwards. Final state rebuilt and verified deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 338 / failed_icalls 273 / heap_allocs 92 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0, tree clean and probe-free.

[1] THE CORRUPTION, CAUGHT DIRECTLY. Probes at sub_002096FD's entry and at sub_001EA6B0's entry, printing this:
  [PFD]  096FD this=010981B8   [PEA6] EA6B0 this=010981B8    <- match
  [PFD]  096FD this=01098260   [PEA6] EA6B0 this=01096B88    <- MISMATCH
  [PFD]  096FD this=01099050   [PEA6] EA6B0 this=01099050    <- match
  ... all remaining pairs match.
sub_002096FD holds this in esi and uses `ecx = esi` for all three calls (sub_001EA5A0, sub_001EA600, sub_001EA6B0). Between the second and third, esi changed from 0x01098260 to 0x01096B88. So sub_001EA600 did not preserve the caller's esi on exactly one call.

[2] sub_001EA600 IS BALANCED ON ITS FACE, so the fault is esp, not a missing pop. Its prologue pushes ebx, ebp, esi, edi and its epilogue pops edi, esi, ebp, ebx. Probes at entry and at the epilogue label loc_001EA63B measured esp:
  this=010981B8  in=00F7FC50  out=00F7FC40   delta 0x10   <- correct, = 4 pushes
  this=01098260  in=00F7FC98  out=00F7FC74   delta 0x24   <- 0x14 too much
  this=01099050  in=00F7FC6C  out=00F7FC5C   delta 0x10
  ... every other call delta 0x10.
20 bytes vanish on the bad call, so the four POPs read 20 bytes off and restore garbage. That is the documented "a stack leak is never local" pattern - the damage lands in the CALLER's registers.

[3] RULED OUT the runtime as the cause. RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE (recomp_types.h:674) does restore g_esp = saved_esp on every failure path, so failed icalls do NOT leak arguments. Worth recording because with 273 failed icalls a leak there would have been systemic. NOTE A REAL HAZARD SPOTTED IN PASSING, not the cause here: in sub_001EA600's entry block the lifter captures `_icall_esp = g_esp` BEFORE the four callee-save pushes, so if that +0x50 icall ever failed it would restore esp above the saved registers. It does not fail here, but the pattern is wrong and may bite elsewhere.

[4] LOCATED IN THE LOOP, and the shape is a NESTED CALL. A probe at the loop tail printing iteration, esp, edi and the member pointer:
  it=02..0B   esp=00F7FC88  edi=01098260  mem=01096D20,01096D58,...,01096FA0
  it=00       esp=00F7FC74  edi=00000000  mem=00000000     <- iteration counter RESTARTS
  it=01..     esp=00F7FC74  edi=00000000  mem=00000000/00000006
The counter restarting at 00 with a different esp is a nested sub_001EA600 entered from inside iteration 0x0B. The nested call has this = 0 and its container is NULL, so it walks page 0 (mem reads 0 and 6) instead of a member array. So the +0x74 hook of member 0x01096FA0 is where a NULL sub-object enters the chain, and the nested junk walk is what leaves esp 20 bytes low.

[5] THE FULL CHAIN, every link measured:
  member 0x01096FA0's +0x74 hook -> nested sub_001EA600 with this=0, NULL container
  -> nested loop walks page 0, esp ends 0x14 low
  -> outer sub_001EA600 epilogue POPs from wrong slots, esi = 0x01096B88
  -> sub_002096FD calls sub_001EA6B0 with this = the CONTAINER
  -> sub_001EA6B0 default-initialises it, sub_001E9E60 memcpy's member 010976F0's default over +0xC
  -> count 0x1B -> 0, so every later descriptor initialises zero members (#123)

[6] CORRECTION TO #129. Its part (5) claimed the container is reached because a post-flip descriptor's NULL +0x28 makes construction "fall back" to the metaclass's shared container. That is WRONG - there is no fallback path. The container is reached purely because esi is corrupted by the stack leak. The +0x28 gap is still real and still unfixed (#125/#127), and a NULL object is still what triggers the nested walk, so the two remain related - but they are NOT the single root cause #129 asserted, and a +0x28 fix alone is NOT guaranteed to remove the count collapse. Treat #129's "fixing +0x28 should fix both for free" as unproven.

[7] SECOND PROCESS LESSON IN ONE SESSION, same family as #128. I first read 30 lines of the loop trace, saw esp stable, and concluded the leak was in the post-loop vtable+0x4 icall. The fuller trace showed the loop was where it happens. #128 was the same mistake against a prior entry's displayed evidence; this one was against my own truncated output. HEAD-LIMIT YOUR GREPS AT YOUR PERIL - confirm the tail before concluding a region is clean.

NEXT: identify what member 0x01096FA0 is and why its +0x74 hook produces a this of 0. That is the real defect; the esp leak and the count wipe are both downstream of it. Do NOT patch the memcpy, the POPs, or the count.

entries.claim: THE +0x28 CONTAINER *IS* BUILT BY THE POST-FLIP PATH - the build just FAILS. Member 0x01096FD8 describes the field at offset 0x28 and its +0x74 hook sub_0020E960 calls FUN_0020e520(typedesc=0x01097498) to create the container, then stores the result into the field. Measured: it returns NULL, exactly once in the boot, and the NULL is stored. This OVERTURNS #125/#127/#129's "nothing in the self-hosted path builds a container", and CORRECTS #130's attribution to member 0x01096FA0 (an off-by-one - my probe printed AFTER the icall, so the real culprit is the NEXT iteration, 0x0C).
entries.evidence:
METHOD: two probe builds after #130, both stripped. Final tree clean and probe-free, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 338 / failed_icalls 273 / heap_allocs 92 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0.

[1] THE MEMBER LOOP, WITH TARGETS AND FIELD VALUES. A probe at loc_001EA621 computing the member, its +0x74 target, its field offset and the current field value, for the sub_001EA600 call on instance 0x01098260:
  it=02 m=01096D20 tgt=0015FDF0 off=00000008 fld=00000000
  it=03 m=01096D58 tgt=0015FDF0 off=0000000C fld=00000000
  ... every iteration 02..0B has tgt=0015FDF0, the known DO-NOTHING stub ...
  it=0B m=01096FA0 tgt=0015FDF0 off=00000024 fld=00000000
  it=0C m=01096FD8 tgt=0020E960 off=00000028 fld=00000000   <- the only real hook
Offset 0x28 is the container field. So the type system DOES carry a member that owns +0x28 and DOES give it a real constructor hook.

[2] CORRECTION TO #130. #130 named member 0x01096FA0 as the source of the nested NULL recursion. That is an OFF-BY-ONE and it is wrong. #130's probe sat at loc_001EA62D, i.e. AFTER the icall returned, so the last line printed before the nested block was the PREVIOUS iteration. 0x01096FA0's hook is 0x0015FDF0, a no-op that cannot recurse. The real culprit is iteration 0x0C, member 0x01096FD8. Everything else in #130 - the esi mismatch, the 0x24-vs-0x10 esp delta, the nested walk, the runtime being ruled out - stands unchanged; only the member identity was wrong.

[3] WHAT THE HOOK IS. sub_0020E960 (Ghidra) is the per-member SUB-OBJECT CONSTRUCTOR:
    if (*(char *)(member + 0x34) != 0) {                    /* auto-construct flag */
        name = *(char **)(member + 0x40);
        if (name == 0 || *name == 0)  piVar3 = <default allocator from 0x5BC538/0x5BC53C>;
        else { piVar3 = FUN_001e9b80(name); if (!piVar3) piVar3 = FUN_001eabe0(param_1); }
        piVar3 = FUN_0020e520(*(void **)(member + 0x38), piVar3);   /* CREATE the sub-object */
        FUN_00209ec0(member, param_1, (int)piVar3);                 /* STORE it into the field */
        ...refcount decrement, free_object_instance if it drops to 0...
    }
So the container is supposed to be created by the generic creator FUN_0020e520 using the type descriptor stored at member+0x38, and then written into the instance by FUN_00209ec0.

[4] THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT. A probe at loc_0020E9BA, immediately after the FUN_0020e520 call, where esi = eax = the created object. It fires exactly ONCE in the entire boot:
  [PMK] made=00000000 memb=01096FD8 typedesc=01097498 inst=01098260
FUN_0020e520 RETURNED NULL. FUN_00209ec0 then stored that NULL into instance 0x01098260's +0x28. That is the whole "+0x28 is NULL" phenomenon: not an absent code path, a FAILING one.

[5] THE TYPE IS THE CONTAINER TYPE, cross-checked. Descriptor 0x01097498 appears in ledger #116's measured table as `01097498 ret=003EEED0/003EEF28 size=0x10`, and the pre-flip container builder FUN_00222600 allocates its container with FUN_001f7e00(0x10, 0, param_1) - the same 0x10 size. So 0x01097498 is the container type, and the failing creation is unambiguously the container's.

[6] OVERTURNS THREE ENTRIES. #125 concluded "the self-hosted/post-flip path has no call to sub_00222600 and no direct write to +0x28 anywhere in sub_002235D0's body", #127 repeated it from Ghidra, and #129 built on it. All three were looking in the wrong place: the container is not built by the registration routine at all, it is built LATER, during instance construction, by the member hook. The searches were correct about sub_002235D0 and simply did not cover sub_0020E960. This is why the NULL was never explained despite four entries of effort.

[7] AND IT EXPLAINS #130's STACK LEAK. FUN_0020e520 does not bail when its allocation fails - it proceeds to bless and construct the NULL, which is the nested sub_001EA600 with this=0 and a NULL container that #130 measured walking page 0 and leaving esp 0x14 low. One failure, three visible symptoms: NULL +0x28, the esp leak, and the wiped count.

THE SINGLE REMAINING QUESTION: why does FUN_0020e520 return NULL for descriptor 0x01097498? Per #117 the path is FUN_0020e520 -> sub_0020E547, which picks an allocator (desc+0x60 by name via sub_001E9B80, else default sub_001F5C20) and allocates MEM32(desc+0x48) + MEM32(desc+0x20) through allocator vtable+0xCC. Probe that allocation for desc=0x01097498: the size fields, the chosen allocator, and the vtable+0xCC result. Do NOT patch +0x28 by hand - the builder exists and must be made to succeed.

entries.claim: THE TWELVE POOLLESS ALLOCATORS ARE THE ROOT CAUSE, NOT A RED HERRING - ledger #114's "do not chase the twelve" is REFUTED. Every allocation in the boot that goes through allocator 0x01088A90 succeeds (11 of 11); every allocation that goes through 0x01218000, one of the twelve pool-less allocators built by sub_00234E18, produces garbage: NULL for the 0x10-byte container (which is the entire missing +0x28), plus 0x011D0008 and 0x00000008 - and 0x00000008 is the guest-VA-8 "instance" that #123 measured crashing the boot. Also ruled out: descriptor 0x01097498 is NOT abstract (+0x1A = 0), so the abstract early-return is not the NULL path.
entries.evidence:
METHOD: three probes in two builds - [PABS] at loc_0020E53B (descriptor and its abstract flag), [PALLOC] at loc_0020E582 (descriptor, allocation result, desc+0x20 offset, desc+0x48 size), [PALR] at loc_0020E56D (descriptor, chosen allocator, its vtable, and the resolved vtable+0xCC target). Probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 338 / failed_icalls 273 / heap_allocs 92 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0, tree clean.

[1] THE ABSTRACT EXIT IS RULED OUT. FUN_0020e520 has two ways to yield nothing: the abstract check `if (MEM8(this + 0x1A) == 1) return 0`, and a zero allocation in sub_0020E547. Measured: `[PABS] E53B desc=01097498 abstract=00`. Not abstract, so it proceeds into the allocator path. The NULL comes from the allocation.

[2] THE ALLOCATION ITSELF, and it is the only failure in the boot. 14 allocations total, one returns zero:
  [PALLOC] E582 desc=01097498 alloc=00000000 off=00000000 size=00000010
size 0x10 confirms the container type a third independent way (after #116's table and FUN_00222600's FUN_001f7e00(0x10,...)), and desc+0x20 is 0 so there is no offset masking the result. The allocator's vtable+0xCC returned NULL for a 16-byte request.

[3] THE FULL CORRELATED TABLE - allocator choice against result. This is the finding:
  allocr=01088A90 -> 010981B8 (size 0x44), 01098260 (0x64), 01099050 (0x64), 010990B8 (0x44),
                     01099100 (0x44), 01099148 (0x64), 010991B0 (0x64), 01099248 (0x64),
                     010992B0 (0x64), 01099368 (0x64), 01099468 (0x34)      -- 11 of 11 SUCCEED
  allocr=01218000 -> 00000000  (desc 01097498, size 0x10)
  allocr=01218000 -> 011D0008  (desc 01099148, size 0x00)
  allocr=01218000 -> 00000008  (desc 01099148, size 0x00)                   -- 3 of 3 GARBAGE
Every object in this boot is allocated by one of exactly two allocators. One works perfectly. The other has never returned a usable pointer. All three of its results are the pathological "instances" prior entries have been chasing.

[4] 0x01218000 IS ONE OF THE TWELVE. Ledger #114 established that sub_00234E18 builds twelve base-class allocators at 0x0120D000 ... 0x01218000, one page apart (heap allocs #76-#87), that their init vtable+0x24 = sub_002036E0 never allocates the pool, and that the only writer of +0x70 is sub_00211280 which fires EXACTLY ONCE all boot, on 0x01088A90. That is precisely the split measured here: the one allocator that got a pool works, and 0x01218000 - the LAST of the twelve - has no pool and returns nothing.

[5] #114's CONCLUSION IS REFUTED. It wrote: "The twelve poolless objects are a RED HERRING ... Fix the NULL container first; do not chase the twelve." That is exactly backwards. The twelve are not downstream of the NULL container - they CAUSE it. Its reasoning was that 0x0120E000 had been scavenged out of page 0 rather than legitimately held in the container, which was true as far as it went, but it led to dismissing the allocators entirely and the dismissal has cost entries #117 through #131.

[6] IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE FATAL INSTANCE DIRECTLY. #123 measured the crash with inst=0x00000008 - guest VA 8 used as an object with no vtable - and could not say where it came from. It comes from here: allocator 0x01218000 returning 8 for a size-0 request. The other bad result, 0x011D0008, is #123's other vtable-less instance. Both are now sourced.

[7] A SECONDARY OBSERVATION worth its own thread: the two size-0 allocations use desc=0x01099148, a descriptor whose instance size is 0x00000000. A descriptor with zero size is itself a product of the count-wipe cascade (descriptors initialised with zero members), so there is a feedback loop - the broken allocator corrupts descriptors, and corrupted descriptors then ask the broken allocator for zero-byte objects.

NEXT: why the twelve never get a pool. sub_002036E0 is their vtable+0x24 init and does not allocate one; sub_00211280 is the only +0x70 writer and fires once, on 0x01088A90 only. Determine what the original does for the other eleven - whether sub_00211280 should run per allocator, whether sub_002036E0 is mis-lifted, or whether an earlier registration step that assigns pools is being skipped. Do NOT hand-patch +0x28, the container builder, or the allocator's return - all three are downstream of a pool that was never created.

entries.claim: The twelve allocators ARE fully constructed - derived ctor sub_00211490 runs on all twelve and base init sub_002036E0 runs on all twelve - but the pool writer sub_00211280 (vtable+0x178) runs ZERO times for them and exactly once for 0x01088A90, which is a DIFFERENT class that goes through neither of those two functions. At the allocation site the difference is measured directly: the working allocator has +0x70 = 0x01089A90 and id +0xAC = 1, all twelve have +0x70 = 0x00000000 and id = 4, with an identical dispatch target sub_00211530. So #114's "+0x70 is never written for the twelve" was CORRECT; only its conclusion that the twelve were a red herring was wrong.
entries.evidence:
METHOD: four probes across three builds, all stripped afterwards. Final tree clean and probe-free, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 338 / failed_icalls 273 / heap_allocs 92 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0.

[1] CALL COUNTS, the clean split:
  [PCTOR] sub_00211490 (derived ctor)  -> 12 calls: 0120D000, 0120E000, 0120F000, 01210000,
          01211000, 01212000, 01213000, 01214000, 01215000, 01216000, 01217000, 01218000
  [PINIT] sub_002036E0 (base init)     -> 12 calls, the same twelve, every one with +0x70 already 0

[2] SO "THE TWELVE ARE UNCONSTRUCTED" IS WRONG. They are fully constructed: the derived constructor runs on every one of them. What they never receive is the pool. sub_002036E0 is tiny and provably cannot supply one - `MEM8(ecx + 0x68) = MEM8(0x46A284); call sub_001F5D60;` and nothing else.

[3] THE DIFFERENCE AT THE ALLOCATION SITE, measured. sub_001EC5E0 (vtable+0xCC, the allocate entry, lives in recomp_seed.c) is a thin forwarder: it reads MEM16(this + 0xAC) as an id and tail-dispatches vtable+0x1AC. Probe over all 138 calls:

  this=0120E000  f70=00000000  fAC=0004  tgt1AC=00211530     <- and identically for
  this=0120F000 ... 01218000   f70=00000000  fAC=0004           every one of the twelve
Same dispatch target in every case, so the allocator code is shared and correct. TWO fields differ: the pool pointer at +0x70 (a real buffer vs NULL) and the arena id at +0xAC (1 vs 4).

[4] CORRECTS A GUESS I MADE MID-INVESTIGATION. On seeing sub_001EC5E0 forward this[0x2b] I suggested the differing field might be +0xAC "and not +0x70, meaning #114's focus on +0x70 may be a red herring too". The measurement shows BOTH differ and the NULL pool is the substantive one. #114's +0x70 finding stands; recording this so the guess is not mistaken later for a result.

[5] WHERE THE CLASS COMES FROM. FUN_00234df0 (which contains 0x00234E18) is the allocator-class factory and carries the same guard as every other factory: post-flip it returns FUN_0020e520(DAT_005bc498, param_1); pre-flip it does _malloc(0xd0), FUN_00211490(buf), then icalls vtable+0x24 and vtable+0x1C. So the twelve are built by the pre-flip branch, get their derived ctor, and their vtable+0x24 resolves to sub_002036E0 which does not allocate a pool.

[6] THE REMAINING QUESTION IS NARROW. sub_00211280 has exactly ONE reference in the whole image and it is a DATA reference from 0x003f48e8 - i.e. it is purely a virtual, slot +0x178 of vtable 0x003F4770, never called directly. Something dispatches +0x178 once, on 0x01088A90. Find that dispatcher and determine whether the twelve should reach it too, or whether the twelve are instead meant to inherit an already-created pool (the id 4 vs 1 at +0xAC suggests they are meant to name a shared arena rather than own one). Either answer is a real fix; guessing between them is not.

CAUTION FOR THE NEXT STEP: do not write a pool pointer into +0x70 by hand. Two independent readings are still open - "the twelve should each be given a pool" and "the twelve should resolve an existing arena by id" - and the +0xAC id difference is evidence for the second.

entries.claim: A1 ANSWERED: sub_00211280 is the pool OPEN method, dispatched as vtable+0x178 from sub_00216210, the engine's memory-system bootstrap - an Alchemy/Intrinsic pool factory that selects an implementation by NAME ("igArenaMemoryPool" / "igMallocMemoryPool") and loops 47 slots, storing each at slot*0x90+0x14. By design only slots 0 and 4-7 create and open their own pool; slots 1-3 and 8-0x2E ALIAS slot 0's object. The twelve pool-less allocators do NOT come from that loop at all - they are created by the type-system factory and register themselves through their own base init sub_002036E0 -> sub_001F5D60, which never opens a pool. So they may be legitimately pool-less prototypes, and the real defect may be in ALLOCATOR SELECTION rather than in pool creation.
entries.evidence:
METHOD: two probe builds after #133, both stripped. Final tree clean and probe-free, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 338 / failed_icalls 273 / heap_allocs 92 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0.

[1] THE DISPATCHER, recovered from the icall ring buffer. A probe inside sub_00211280 dumping g_icall_trace (recomp_types.h, 16 entries, written by every RECOMP_ICALL/RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE):
  [PTR178] this=01088A90 t1=00211280 t2=001E9380 t3=00216210 t4=FE0000B8 t5=FE0000BC t6=00355730
A literal grep for "+ 0x178" could never have found this - the four icall sites at that offset are all in unrelated sub_000Bxxxx code, so the dispatch is a computed slot. The ring buffer was the right instrument.

[2] WHAT sub_00211280 ACTUALLY IS - the pool OPEN method, and it writes BOTH fields #133 measured:
    in_ECX[1] = 1;                                        /* refcount */
    iVar4 = (**(code **)(*DAT_005bb9ac + 8))(0x814);      /* allocate 0x814 bytes */
    in_ECX[0x1c] = iVar4;                                 /* 0x1c*4 = +0x70, THE POOL */
    for (iVar4 = 0x205; iVar4 != 0; iVar4--) *puVar6++ = 0;   /* zero all 0x814 bytes */
    *(undefined2 *)(in_ECX + 0x2b) = 1;                   /* 0x2b*4 = +0xAC */
So it allocates and zeroes a 2068-byte pool. This is an "open", not a constructor.

[3] BUT +0xAC IS NOT ONLY SET HERE - correcting myself mid-investigation. I first concluded from [2] that the id is "literally set to 1, so the 4 is garbage and reading (2) is dead". That is WRONG. FUN_001f5d60, the registrar, ends every path with (**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x164))(uVar4 + iVar1 * 2) - the id is a REGISTRATION SLOT id, computed as flag + slot*2. The twelve reading 4 is a legitimate registration id (slot 2), not uninitialised memory. Only +0x70 is uniquely sub_00211280's.

[4] sub_00216210 IS THE MEMORY-SYSTEM BOOTSTRAP, and it is configuration-driven:
  - registers in_ECX into DAT_005bb704[DAT_005bc544], capped at 4 entries - the same array sub_001E9380 searches;
  - reads the string DAT_005bc51c and strcmp's it against "igArenaMemoryPool" (0x12 bytes) and "igMallocMemoryPool" (0x13 bytes), constructing malloc(0xd0) with vtable PTR_LAB_003f4770 or malloc(0xa0) with vtable PTR_LAB_003f4df8 accordingly. This is the Alchemy/Intrinsic engine's named pool factory.
  - loops iStack_20 from 0 to 0x2E, storing each pool at *(iStack_20 * 0x90 + 0x14 + in_ECX) - exactly the stride and offset sub_001E9380 reads back as its slot table.

[5] THE DESIGN IS SHARING, NOT PER-OBJECT POOLS. Inside the loop:
    case 0: (**(code **)(*piVar2 + 0x178))();     /* open */
    case 4/5/6/7: (**(code **)(*piVar2 + 0x178))();
    default: goto switchD_002164c6_caseD_1;       /* no open at all */
  and for the non-owning slots:
    else if ((iStack_20 < 4) || (7 < iStack_20)) { piVar2 = *(int **)(in_ECX + 0x14); }  /* ALIAS slot 0 */
So five slots own and open a pool; forty-two alias slot 0's object. THIS CORRECTS MY OWN A2 CALL EARLIER IN THIS SESSION: I declared "reading (1) is correct, each allocator gets its own pool - reading (2) is dead". Neither reading was right. The real design is a third thing - a few owners plus many aliases of one shared object.

[6] AND THE TWELVE ARE NOT IN THAT LOOP. Probe [PREG] at FUN_001f5d60's entry fired 12 times, on exactly 0120D000..01218000, every one with vt=003F4770 and pool70=00000000 - and 0x01088A90 is NOT among them. Ghidra shows FUN_001f5d60 has THREE callers: FUN_002036e0 (0x002036e9), 0x00216562 and 0x002123bf. sub_002036E0 is the twelve's own base init, which #133 measured firing on all twelve. So the twelve register themselves through their base init and never pass through sub_00216210's slot loop; 0x01088A90 is the one that came from the loop and got its pool opened.

[7] THE FORK THIS OPENS, and I am not guessing between the halves:
  (a) The twelve are legitimately pool-less - registered prototypes/templates that the engine never intends to allocate from - and the real defect is in ALLOCATOR SELECTION: sub_0020E547 picks desc+0x60 by name via sub_001E9B80, else the default sub_001F5C20, and something makes it hand back 0x01218000 instead of the opened pool 0x01088A90.
  (b) The twelve are meant to be opened too, by a path we are not executing.
Evidence currently favours (a): the bootstrap's own design registers only a handful of owners and aliases the rest, and nothing in the type-system factory path ever calls +0x178.

NEXT: probe sub_0020E547's allocator selection for desc=0x01097498 - specifically whether desc+0x60 holds a name, what sub_001E9B80 returns for it, and what the default sub_001F5C20 returns - and compare against 0x01088A90. Do NOT open pools on the twelve until (a) vs (b) is settled by that measurement.

entries.claim: FORK SETTLED - it is (a), ALLOCATOR SELECTION, and the defect is the owner lookup sub_001E8E20 MIS-ATTRIBUTING ownership. Instance 0x01098260 was allocated by the good pool 0x01088A90 (measured in #132), yet sub_001E8E20 reports 0x01218000 - a pool-less prototype - as its owner. That wrong owner's vtable+0x160 stamps id 0x18 into the instance at +7, and sub_0020E960 later indexes registry A with 0x18>>1 to pick 0x01218000 for the container allocation, which fails. The twelve are NOT meant to be opened; nothing should be selecting them at all.
entries.evidence:
METHOD: one build, three probes (M1 of the approved plan), all stripped afterwards. Tree clean and probe-free, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 338 / failed_icalls 273 / heap_allocs 92 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0.

[1] THE SELECTION CHAIN, confirmed in both Ghidra and the lifted C. FUN_002096b0 stamps every new object with an allocator id at +7:
    piVar3 = FUN_001e8e20((int)this - *(int *)(iVar2 + 0x20));   /* who owns this memory? */
    if (piVar3 == 0) { *((int)this + 7) = 0; }
    else { uVar1 = (**(code **)(*piVar3 + 0x160))(); *((int)this + 7) = uVar1; }
and sub_0020E960 later uses the OWNING INSTANCE's id to choose the sub-object's allocator:
    piVar3 = DAT_005bc53c;
    if ((*(byte *)(param_1 + 7) & 1) == 0) piVar3 = DAT_005bc538;
    piVar3 = *(int **)(*piVar3 + ((uint)*(byte *)(param_1 + 7) >> 1) * 4);
So bit 0 of the id picks the registry and the rest is the slot index - matching FUN_001f5d60's registration id of flag + slot*2 exactly.

[2] THE MEASUREMENT, and it is unambiguous:
  [POWN]  inst=01098260 owner=01218000
  [PIDST] inst=01098260 stampid=00000018
  [PSEL]  inst=01098260 id=18 allocr=01218000 regA=01090020 regB=01090008
  [PSEL]  inst=01099468 id=18 allocr=01218000
  [PSEL]  inst=011D0008 id=18 allocr=01218000
id 0x18 = 24: bit 0 is 0 so registry A (DAT_005bc538 = 0x01090020), index 24>>1 = 12, which resolves to 0x01218000.

[3] THE CONTRADICTION THAT NAMES THE BUG. Ledger #132's correlated table measured, for this very object, `allocr=01088A90 -> alloc=01098260 (size 0x64)`. So instance 0x01098260's memory came from the GOOD pool 0x01088A90, and sub_001E8E20 nonetheless reports 0x01218000 as its owner. The owner lookup is simply wrong. Every instance after the first inherits the same wrong stamp - PIDST shows 010981B8 getting id 0 and then 01098260, 01099050, 010990B8, 01099100, 01099148 and the rest all getting 0x18.

[4] SO THE FORK FROM #134 IS SETTLED AS (a). The twelve are legitimately pool-less registered prototypes; nothing is supposed to allocate from them. They were never meant to be opened, and #133's caution against hand-writing a pool into +0x70 was correct - doing so would have papered over a mis-attributing lookup and left the real defect in place.

[5] THIS LANDS BACK ON #88/#89's FUNCTION. sub_001E8E20 is the same "which allocator owns this pointer?" lookup those entries fought with: #88 found it returning NULL because it dereferenced a null registry entry, and #89 fixed that by widening a manual heap-range guard from the heap range to image-base..end-of-RAM. A guard that was widened to stop false NEGATIVES is a plausible cause of false POSITIVES - it may now match an allocator whose range does not really contain the pointer. That is a hypothesis, not a result: it has NOT been verified and must be checked against Ghidra before any edit.

NEXT: read sub_001E8E20's lifted body against Ghidra, with attention to #89's manual guard, and probe what it walks for pointer 0x01098260 - which candidates it considers, what range test each applies, and why 0x01218000 wins over 0x01088A90. Do NOT widen or narrow the guard by guess; establish the original's ownership test first.

entries.claim: A REAL FIX LANDED, and diff_reached returns "strictly more code ran - unambiguous progress" (7 gained, 0 lost), only the second such verdict this project has produced after #77. sub_001FBA90 - vtable+0x148 of allocator class 0x003F4770, the "does this allocator own this pointer?" predicate - was a class-1 deferred-flag miscompile: the lifter emitted `neg eax` without assigning _cf, so the following `sbb eax,eax` always read _cf = 0 and the function returned 1 UNCONDITIONALLY. Every allocator claimed every pointer, so sub_001E8E20's ownership walk returned whichever it scanned first. reached 147 -> 154, callsites 418 -> 434, heap_allocs 92 -> 826. HONEST CAVEAT: kernel_calls reads 4000 but that is the LOGGING CAP and the tail is a two-ordinal spin with descending esp - do NOT read it as 338 -> 4000 progress.
entries.evidence:
METHOD: probes at all four decision points of sub_001E8E20's two registry walks, then a one-line lifter fix, then build + 2 runs + diff_reached. Probes stripped before the fix run. Tree clean; manual_edits extract/verify now reports 1064/1064 placing cleanly, so the fix survives regeneration.

[1] THE MEASUREMENT THAT NAMED IT. Probing sub_001E8E20's walk for the query on pointer 0x01098260:
  [PA78]  A active cand=01088A90 ptr=01098260 r=3F4701
  [PA148] A owns   cand=01088A90 ptr=01098260 r=01
  [PA78]  A active cand=01218000 ptr=01098260 r=3F4701
  [PA148] A owns   cand=01218000 ptr=01098260 r=01
BOTH allocators answer "I own it" for the same pointer, which is impossible if the predicate works. Also: the registry B walk fired ZERO times (PB78/PB148 counts 0), so the good allocator is only ever found via registry A, and since the walk runs BACKWARDS from the current count, allocators registered later are scanned first - which is why a pool-less prototype won as more of the twelve registered.

[2] THE DEFECT, in recomp_seed.c at loc_001FBAD7. Original x86:
    001FBAD7  sub eax, esi     ; eax = eax - esi
    001FBAD9  neg eax          ; CF = (operand != 0)
    001FBADB  sbb eax, eax     ; eax = -CF
    001FBADD  inc eax          ; eax = (original eax == esi)
Lifted C as generated:
    eax = eax - esi;
    eax = (uint32_t)(-(int32_t)eax);
    eax = _cf ? 0xFFFFFFFF : 0;   /* sbb self (CF extend) */
    eax++;
`neg` is the instruction that PRODUCES the carry the `sbb` consumes, and it was lifted as a plain negate with no _cf assignment. _cf is initialised to 0 at function entry and written nowhere else in the function, so the sbb always yielded 0 and inc made it 1. Ghidra confirms the intent: `return (uint)(iVar1 == in_ECX);`.

[3] THE FIX, one line plus a comment recording the original instruction order:
    _cf = (eax != 0);
inserted before the negate. Equal -> difference 0 -> _cf 0 -> eax 0 -> inc -> 1. Unequal -> _cf 1 -> eax 0xFFFFFFFF -> inc -> 0. Matches the idiom exactly.

[4] MEASURED, deterministic 2 of 2 both before and after:
  reached        147 -> 154
  callsites      418 -> 434
  heap_allocs     92 -> 826
  failed_icalls  273 -> 274
  distinct kernel functions   17 -> 17  (all-time best held)
diff_reached.py: 7 ONLY-AFTER (sub_001EC600, sub_00209F50, sub_00209F80, sub_0020A8B0, sub_0020E410, sub_002172B0, sub_00218070), ZERO only-before, verdict "strictly more code ran. Unambiguous progress." That is the second time this project has produced that verdict; #77 was the first.

[5] THE CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE GLOSSED. kernel_calls reads 4000, which is the LOGGING CAP (ledger #33), not a measurement. The tail of the log is ordinals 184 and 217 alternating with steadily DESCENDING esp (0x00F4D348 down to 0x00F4D260), i.e. a deepening recursion pinned at the cap. Reporting this as "338 -> 4000" would repeat exactly the mistake that got ledger #30 wrongly reverted. The trustworthy signals here are the set diff and heap_allocs.

I wrote that from #70's text without checking whether it had since been fixed. It had.
