They are simply whatever those four callbacks happened to leave in esi. Two of the four leave small integers and two leave other heap pointers - the latter are equally wrong and equally silent, and would corrupt a different object.

[4] IT IS SYSTEMIC AND EACH SITE NEEDS ITS OWN ANALYSIS. A first look shows the four are not identical: sub_0021B890 does push esi in its prologue (so its loss is deeper, likely a callee or an _icall_esp rollback of the #145 kind), whereas sub_002002B0 never pushes esi at all and opens with `esp -= 0x10`, so either the original genuinely does not touch esi and something it calls does, or the prologue is mis-lifted. Do not assume one fix covers all four.

[5] WHY THIS SURFACED NOW: sub_0021B890 and sub_0021BB80 are both in the eleven functions #142 newly reached. The defect was unreachable before that fix.

[6] THIS IS THE SAME FAMILY AS #130, #142 and #145 - callee-saved registers not surviving a call - which is now the dominant bug class of this session with four distinct instances. The generator-level suspect remains translator.py's _fixup_icall_esp_save (#145 point 8).

NEXT: take the four callbacks one at a time, cheapest first. For each, probe esi at entry and at every return path, and diff the lifted prologue/epilogue against the disassembly. sub_002002B0 is the one that produces the fatal 4 and is the natural first target. Do NOT guard sub_002235D0's use of esi - it is correct to expect a callee to preserve it.

entries.claim: CORRECTS #149: its per-callback attribution is UNSOUND and must not be acted on. #149 paired PRE/POST probes around sub_002235D0's callback icall by log order and named four callbacks as esi-clobberers. Re-probing with esp as a frame discriminator shows the calls NEST, so log order does not pair frames. sub_002002B0 in particular CANNOT clobber esi: it is 17 lines of lifted C, contains no calls at all, and never assigns esi. Two of #149's four pairs are provably cross-frame - their POST esp reappears as a LATER PRE esp. What IS solid is different and simpler: on 7 of 11 calls esp is identical PRE to POST and esi is preserved, and on the other 4 esp DIFFERS across the call.
entries.evidence:
METHOD: re-ran #149's measurement with esp added to both probes. Probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 226 / failed_icalls 272 / heap_allocs 95 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001FBA90+0x76, tree probe-free, manual_edits 1066/1066.

[1] THE DISPROOF BY READING, which should have come first. sub_002002B0 is seventeen lines of lifted C in full: `esp -= 0x10; eax = 0; MEM32(esp+8) = eax; MEM32(esp+0xC) = eax; eax = MEM32(0x5BC508); ecx = MEM32(eax+0x394); MEM32(esp+4) = 1; MEM32(esp) = 0x3EEF28; eax = MEM32(esp+ecx); esp += 0x10; return;`. It makes NO calls and never assigns esi. In a model where registers are globals, it cannot clobber esi. #149 named it as the source of the fatal 4 anyway.

[2] THE MEASUREMENT WITH esp ADDED:
  PRE esp=00F7FCB4 esi=01096BB8 cb=001EA570 -> POST esp=00F7FCB4 esi=01096BB8
  PRE esp=00F7FE00 esi=01091AB0 cb=00219A10 -> POST esp=00F7FE00 esi=01091AB0
  PRE esp=00F7FC9C esi=01097518 cb=002002E0 -> POST esp=00F7FC9C esi=01097518 (deferred; nested)
  PRE esp=00F7F89C / 00F7F9E8 / 00F7FB34 / 00F7FCC4  -> all POST with MATCHING esp and preserved esi
  PRE esp=00F7FDE8 esi=01097498 cb=002002B0 -> POST esp=00F7FDDC esi=00000004      esp -0xC
  PRE esp=00F7FA14 esi=01098638 cb=001F3370 -> POST esp=00F7F880 esi=01098728      esp -0x194
  PRE esp=00F7F880 esi=010988F8 cb=0021BB80 -> POST esp=00F7F6DC esi=01098A68      esp -0x1A4
  PRE esp=00F7F6DC esi=01098D08 cb=0021B890 -> POST esp=00F7F6C8 esi=00000017      esp -0x14
Note that 00F7F880 appears as both a POST and a later PRE, and so does 00F7F6DC. Those two "pairs" are cross-frame artefacts of nesting, not clobbers.

[3] SO WHAT SURVIVES. Seven of eleven calls have identical esp and preserved esi - the mechanism works. Four have esp DIFFERING across the call. Two of those four are explained by nesting alone. The remaining two, at -0xC and -0x14, look like genuine esp leaks, but the callback identity itself is now suspect: cb is read as MEM32(esp + 0x138), so if esp is already shifted at the PRE probe, the value printed as "cb" is read from the wrong stack slot. I am NOT naming a culprit function on this evidence.

[4] METHOD, and this is the eighth correction of the session. The repeated failure mode all day has been building a story on top of a sound measurement: #128 and #146 (partial view of a small result set), #131 (probe after an icall reporting the previous iteration), #140/#141 (reasoning about a structure without checking its pointer was non-null), #147 (temporal adjacency read as argument identity), and now #149 (log order read as frame pairing in the presence of recursion). THE RULE THAT COVERS ALL OF THEM: before pairing or attributing anything, establish that the two observations belong to the same frame, the same iteration and the same object - and prefer a cheap static disproof (reading the seventeen-line function) over an expensive dynamic inference.

NEXT: treat the esp behaviour as the primary signal rather than esi. Instrument the callback dispatch with a monotonic sequence number and an explicit depth counter so PRE/POST pairing is unambiguous under recursion, and only then ask which target, if any, fails to restore esp. Do not act on #149's list.

entries.claim: Wall 42 is caused by sub_001EA600 capturing _icall_esp before its four callee-save pushes: a failed vtable+0x50 ICALL rolls g_esp back past them, so the epilogue returns a stale esi to sub_002096FD, which re-initialises the previous instance and double-releases its fields
entries.evidence: Measured end to end in single builds. (1) Pairing createInstance's returned instance against the initialiser's `this`: 17 created, 17 initialised, sixteen pairs correct and one wrong - 01098938 created and never initialised, 01098A40 initialised twice. Log shows them adjacent: "createInstance -> 01098938" then "[INIT] 01098A40". (2) Bracketing esi through the init sequence in sub_002096FD: correct at entry (01098938), still correct after sub_001EA5A0, STALE after sub_001EA600 (01098A40). That names sub_001EA600 as the clobber. (3) sub_001EA600's generated code captures `uint32_t _icall_esp = g_esp` BEFORE PUSH32 of ebx/ebp/esi/edi and then ICALLs through vtable+0x50 - textually ledger #145's defect, at the site #130 flagged as latent. (4) Applying #145's fix - move the capture to after the register saves, immediately before the call - MOVES THE WALL: crash goes from sub_001EB890+0x1D5 (fault 0x8B0146F4) to sub_001EA6B0+0x2FB (fault 0xD3010000), deterministic 2 of 2 at 514 kernel calls / 94 heap allocs. Callsites go 445 -> 435, which is consistent with the double-initialisation having executed extra paths on the wrong object. (5) The fix is recorded surgically in manual_edits.json (1069 -> 1071 entries, verify reports 1071/1071 placeable) - manual_edits.py extract was NOT used, per the documented data-loss gotcha, and an accidental run of it was reverted. Everything examined on the pool side during this investigation - the destroy gate, capacity, binary-search seed, the -1 marker, the auto-release flag - behaves exactly as specified; three pool-side hypotheses were raised and refuted before the real cause was found upstream.

entries.claim: The esi clobber producing the 0x41 garbage `this` is sub_001EA8E0, and the _icall_esp-before-callee-save-pushes defect is systemic: 284 prologue captures across the tree sit before register saves
entries.evidence: (1) NAMED BY AN EXISTING TOOL, not by hand. RECOMP_CHECK_ABI already checks callee-saved registers across both direct calls and indirect ones (RECOMP_ICALL_WATCH is wired into all three icall macros). A build_abi run reports "sub_001EA8E0 did not restore: esi 01098CE8->00000041" - the exact garbage value that had been propagating through sub_0021E0D0 into sub_00221070 and faulting at 0xFF000008. Two sessions of manual bracketing were unnecessary; the checker answers this class of question in one run. (2) sub_001EA8E0 carried the same ledger #145 defect as sub_001EA600: _icall_esp captured before four callee-save pushes, then an ICALL through vtable+0x50. Applying the same fix moved the wall - crash went from a READ at 0xFF000008 to a WRITE at 0x8B18817A. (3) THE DEFECT IS SYSTEMIC. A new tool, tools_data/find_icall_esp.py, scans gen/*.c for the pattern. Restricted to PROLOGUE captures - which is where every confirmed instance lives, and where pushes can only be the register saves the epilogue pops - it finds 284 sites where the capture precedes callee-saved pushes ONLY, plus 379 that mix saves with argument pushes and are left for a human because moving a capture past a real argument push would break the rollback. (4) Applying all 284 moved the wall again: crash to sub_001E8800+0x182 (fault 0x8CF8005D), callsites back to 460, deterministic 2 of 2 at 530 kernel calls, and ABI violations fell 41 -> 37. (5) The 284 are NOT recorded in manual_edits.json; re-running find_icall_esp.py --apply after a regeneration is more robust than 284 store entries, and the tool is idempotent because it only matches the unfixed shape. The hand fix to sub_001EA8E0 IS in the store (1083/1083 placeable). A backup of gen/ was taken before the sweep.

entries.claim: The field array is not "sized but never populated" - _metaFields at meta+0x28 is NULL on look-up-path descriptors, and mapped page 0 turns the NULL read into a plausible count. Giving those descriptors a real EMPTY container is a REGRESSION
entries.evidence: DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED, FIX REFUTED - two separate results. (1) THE DIAGNOSIS. Probing the field walk prints meta, _metaFields, count and array together: healthy descriptors read "mf=01097790 count=25 arr=01098088", while the broken one reads "mf=00000000 count=26 arr=010985B8". _metaFields is NULL; the count of 26 and the array pointer are MEM32(0xC) and MEM32(8) read off mapped guest page zero. So the container was never sized-but-empty - it was never there, and page zero is what disguised that as plausible data. That explains why six field walks, a three-level linear search and a two-level binary search all faulted on garbage elements. (2) WHO ASSIGNS IT. A watch on a healthy descriptor's meta+0x28 names sub_00222708+0x3F3, which calls sub_00222600 to build the container. A watch on the broken one shows only the allocator zeroing the block. sub_002226E0 branches on the registry ready-flag at [0x5BC508]: not ready goes to sub_00222708 (constructs AND builds _metaFields), ready goes to the look-up path, which instantiates a blank descriptor via sub_0020E520 and never assigns +0x28. The descriptor class's construct vfunc is an empty function, so nothing fills it later. (3) THE FIX WAS TRIED AND IS A REGRESSION. Calling sub_00222600 in the look-up path when +0x28 is NULL - the same call the create path makes, applied only to genuinely NULL fields - gives kernel calls 578 -> 2210, which looks like a 4x advance and is not: distinct kernel ordinals stay at 17 and two ordinals account for 1086 calls each, so it is a spin. Callsites fall 481 -> 443 and reached VAs 165 -> 159, and the crash regresses to sub_001FBA90+0x76 fault 0xF6000013, the August-era wall. Reverted; baseline restored exactly at 481/578/165. (4) WHAT THAT MEANS. The boot's current depth partly DEPENDS on the walks iterating page-zero garbage with the range guards filtering it, rather than on correct data. Making the data truthfully empty moves the boot backwards. So the real fix is to POPULATE the fields, not to empty them - which needs registration to actually run for look-up-path descriptors, i.e. the BLOCKER_005BB700 registry-count defect. An empty container is truthful and still wrong for this boot.

entries.claim: The subsystem registry count staying at 1 is NOT a lifting gap and is probably not the root defect: the registrar runs, every indirect call in the subsystem init resolves, and one registration is all this code path performs
entries.evidence: BLOCKER_005BB700 records that "0x005BB700 is NULL because SubsystemRegistry_Register never runs... nothing calls it". That is no longer true and the conclusion drawn from it does not hold. (1) THE REGISTRAR RUNS. A probe at sub_00216210's entry fires exactly once: "register obj=01087000 count_before=0", so the count goes 0 -> 1 and the table gets one entry. It is lifted (gen/recomp_0015.c) and present in the generated dispatch table (recomp_dispatch.c:15906). (2) ITS CALLER IS LEGITIMATE. recomp_where puts it at sub_00236500+0x360, the same function documented as flipping the type-registry ready flag - i.e. exactly where a subsystem would register itself during module init. (3) NO CALL IS MISSING. Every indirect call in sub_00236500 was instrumented with its target and resolution: 001E9380 (x3), 00216210, 001EC770 and 001EC5E0 - all four distinct targets RESOLVE. sub_001EC5E0 resolves through the MANUAL table rather than the generated one, which is why a first pass that only queried recomp_lookup() reported it as unresolved; testing recomp_lookup_manual() as well corrected that before it became a finding. (4) SO THE COUNT IS 1 BECAUSE ONE SUBSYSTEM HAS REGISTERED SO FAR, not because a registration was lost. The consumers sub_001E9380 and sub_001E9500 open with "if (count <= 1) skip" and search the table for an entry OTHER than the current subsystem; with one subsystem that search is correctly empty. Further subsystems would register from their own inits, which happen later in the boot than the current crash. (5) IMPLICATION: the dead ">= 2 fallback" is a CONSEQUENCE of boot depth, not a cause of it. Raising the count artificially would mean writing a fabricated pointer into table[1], which is inventing data to satisfy a check - exactly what the project's guard rule forbids. The root defect for the wall 42-53 family therefore remains the NULL _metaFields on look-up-path descriptors (ledger #153), and that is not fixed by the registry count.

entries.claim: registerFields (sub_00216FD0) runs for ALL 15 metaobjects including the broken ones - it registers their fields into a NULL _metaFields, writing through page zero. Creating the container at registration works mechanically but re-exposes the older sub_001FBA90 wall
entries.evidence: (1) WHAT REGISTERS THE FIELDS. Watching a healthy container's count at +0xC shows 26 increments, all from sub_00216FD0+0x741 - the SAME function and offset TYPE_DESCRIPTOR.md records as writing the instance size (FFFFFFFF -> 00000010). So sub_00216FD0 is the per-field registration worker: it appends the field to _metaFields and accumulates the size in one pass, under sub_002235D0. (2) IT RUNS FOR THE BROKEN DESCRIPTORS TOO. A probe at its entry printing `this` and `this->_metaFields` fires 15 times: the first SEVEN have real containers (01096C20, 01096B88, 01097580, 010978C0, 01097828, 01097790, 01096BA0) and the last EIGHT read 00000000. So registration is not skipped for look-up-path descriptors - it runs and writes their fields through a NULL pointer into mapped guest page zero. That is the source of the phantom "count = 26 with a residue array" that every field walk was reading, and it explains all ten guards added this session. (3) THE FIX WORKS MECHANICALLY. Creating the container at the top of sub_00216FD0 when _metaFields is genuinely NULL - the same sub_00222600 call the create path sub_00222708 makes - gives every one of the 13 metaobjects a real container: 01098260->01096DC8, 010984C0->01098528, 01098568->01096D08, 010986A0->01098708, 010987A0->01098808, 010989A8->01098A10, verified by a probe placed AFTER the fix (an earlier probe placed before it read 0 and was misleading). (4) BUT IT IS BLOCKED DOWNSTREAM. With real containers the field walks do real work - the kernel-call pair 277/294 goes from ~289 iterations to 1086 - and the boot then diverges EARLIER and dies at sub_001FBA90+0x76 with fault 0xF6000013, which is the August wall from ledger #145/#149, with sub_002041D0 in the chain. Callsites fall 481 -> 443 and reached VAs 165 -> 159. Two different placements of the fix (sub_002226E0's tail and sub_00216FD0's head) give the same outcome, so this is a property of the fix, not of where it sits. (5) THE NEXT OBSTACLE IS NAMED. An ABI-checker run with the fix in place reports "sub_0021E970 did not restore: esi 010989A8->00000017" - 0x17 being the exact small-integer `this` ledger #143-#149 chased. That function saves ecx/ebx/ebp/esi/edi properly and has no _icall_esp defect, so its epilogue is being misaligned by something deeper. (6) REVERTED to preserve the measured baseline (481/578/165), per the #119 precedent that changes which do not demonstrate progress are not kept. The patch is small and recorded here: at loc_00216FD0, if this is in the heap range and MEM32(this+0x28)==0, PUSH 0 / call sub_00222600 / esp += 4 / MEM32(this+0x28) = eax, preserving ecx across the call.

entries.claim: sub_0021E970's missing esi restore is caused by 0x0021EABF being an unresolved stub, not by a misaligned epilogue
entries.evidence: whatis 0x0021EABF disassembles to `mov ebp, edx; jmp 0x0021E9C2` - a two-instruction island, 7 bytes, identical in shape to sub_0021EAC6 (`mov ebp, edx; jmp 0x0021EA41`) which the generator DID detect and which is seeded in recomp_0026.c. recomp_stubs_unresolved.c:1876 defined sub_0021EABF as { g_esp += 4; /* not detected */ }. sub_0021E970 pushes ecx/ebx/ebp/esi/edi at 0x0021E970 and pops them at loc_0021EAB9, but the je at loc_0021E9B1 exits through sub_0021EABF, which returns immediately - so the epilogue never runs, the five saves stay on the stack, and the caller gets back esi still holding MEM32(esi+0xC), this loop's element count. That is the reported 'esi 010989A8 -> 00000017' (0x17 = 23). FIXED by inlining the island: goto loc_0021E9BF on match, plus a guard there supplying the mov ebp,edx (the loop leaves edx == esi on completion and edx >= esi when skipped, so edx < esi identifies the match path with no extra state). Two manual_edits records; 1095/1095 placeable. Not measurable on the current boot - sub_0021E970 is not reached - so the evidence is static, from the XBE bytes, not from a run.

entries.claim: Only 5 of the 2125 unresolved stubs are actually entered on a boot, so the class is small and fixable rather than a 2061-site latent risk
entries.evidence: A static scan found 2061 of the 2125 stubs in recomp_stubs_unresolved.c reachable by a lifter tail call (sub_XXXX(); return;) across 2661 sites - every one a potential return-without-epilogue. Instrumenting every stub body with a log-once counter and booting gave exactly 5 hits: 0x001183EC, 0x001995AD, 0x0020B8C6, 0x00340F24, 0x0034436E. All five are mid-function continuations; 0x0020B8C6 is 'mov ebx, edx; jmp 0x0020B88D', the same island shape as 0x0021EABF. Three of the five sit inside functions the ABI checker already names (sub_001183A0, sub_001994F0, sub_00344344), so the STUBHIT list and the ABI violation list are the same defect seen from two sides. Probe removed afterwards; strip_probes clean.

entries.claim: Seeding is the right repair for every unresolved stub
entries.evidence: Seeding all five live stubs measured 578 -> 48 kernel calls, 165 -> 125 reached. Bisected with a new tool (tools_data/neuter_seed.py, which stubs one seeded body in place so a candidate costs one rebuild instead of a five-minute re-seed). Result: sub_001183EC and sub_0034436E are GOOD (578 -> 582 kernel, 165 -> 174 reached, 445 -> 501 call sites, deterministic over two runs). sub_001995AD is BAD (578 -> 244): the seeder derives extent by scanning to a ret and gave it 0x001995AD-0x00199862, 693 bytes, but its enclosing function sub_001994F0 is only 41 bytes (0x001994F0-0x00199519), so the seed spans several unrelated functions. sub_0020B8C6/sub_0020B88D are BAD as seeds (578 -> 48): a seeded continuation carries the epilogue POPs without the prologue PUSHes, which is only correct while the parent frame is still live. The rule: seed a continuation only when its extent stays inside one function; inline an island instead.

entries.claim: The correct inline fix for sub_0020B850's 0x0020B8C6 island can land now
entries.evidence: The fix is faithful - 0x0020B8C6 disassembles to 'mov ebx, edx; jmp 0x0020B88D' and the inline form mirrors the one that fixed sub_0021E970 - but applying it measured 582 -> 48 kernel calls and 174 -> 125 reached. The broken stub was load-bearing: it returned early from sub_0020B850 and skipped the icall at 0x0020B893, sub_002093F0 and the release at 0x0020B8AC. With the island inlined, that work runs and the boot dies in a repeating 0x001EC220 -> 0x001FBA90 -> 0x001EC770 ICALL cycle ending in a failed resolve of VA 0 and a read of guest 0x0000FFFF with esi = -1. sub_001FBA90 is the August wall the plan of record already names, so this fix opens the door onto that wall rather than clearing it. REVERTED and held here; re-apply after sub_001FBA90 is fixed. The exact patch: in recomp_0015.c sub_0020B850, insert 'if (CMP_EQ(MEM32(ecx + edx * 4), eax)) goto loc_0020B88A;' before the generated je at loc_0020B880, and replace 'ebx = ebx | 0xFFFFFFFFu;' at loc_0020B88A with 'if (CMP_L(edx, esi)) { ebx = edx; } else { ebx = ebx | 0xFFFFFFFFu; }'.

entries.claim: The lifter emits sbb reg,reg without ever assigning _cf, so every neg/sbb/inc predicate in the tree is a compile-time constant
entries.evidence: 354 functions read _cf; 353 never assign it anywhere, and the generator (tools/recomp/lifter.py:1154, translator.py:372) only ever emits the declaration 'int _cf = 0'. So 'eax = _cf ? 0xFFFFFFFF : 0' always takes the zero branch and 'neg r; sbb r,r; inc r' - the standard 'was r zero?' idiom - collapses to the constant 1. Of the 404 reads, 269 sit on the line immediately after a neg in the same basic block, where the carry is knowable with certainty (CF = operand != 0, taken before the negation); the other 135 take their carry from a cmp/test or from another block and are left alone. Independently corroborated: ledger #136 found and hand-fixed this exact defect at sub_001FBA90 months ago, for the same reason, and the new tool correctly skips that site. New tool tools_data/fix_sbb_carry.py, with --apply, --revert (keyed on its own marker) and a --self-test.

entries.claim: Fixing sub_001FBA90 lets the sub_0020B850 island fix land
entries.evidence: It does not. With sub_001FBA90's carry flag correct - by ledger #136's hand edit or by fix_sbb_carry.py, measured identical either way - applying the island fix still gives 48 kernel calls, 125 reached, 323 call sites, exactly as it did before. The boot dies reading guest 0xFFFFFFFF in sub_001F7930+0x1C8, walking a field array whose element is garbage, under sub_002235D0 and sub_00239E50. So sub_001FBA90 was the wall behind the FIELD-CONTAINER fix (ledger #155 step 2), not behind the island - the plan of record had the ordering wrong. What blocks the island is still the unpopulated field array, one layer below the container.

entries.claim: The root defect is that _metaFields is NULL at registration (ledger #155)
entries.evidence: No longer true in the current tree. A probe at sub_00216FD0's entry, printing this, this->_metaFields, its array at +8 and its count at +0xC, fires for 14 metaobjects and every one already has a real container AND a real array pointer, count 0 as expected at the start of registration. Ledger #155's fix - allocate the container when the slot is empty - is now a measured no-op: with and without it the run is byte-identical at 230/96/477/170. So step 2 of the plan of record is obsolete and the fix was removed rather than kept as dead code. The defect moved one layer down: 6 of the 14 have a _metaFields that does NOT point at their own embedded container (this+0x68, the pattern the other 8 follow) but at another object's memory - e.g. this=01097498 has fields=01096BA0, which is object 01091AB0's field ARRAY - while their own container sits unused at this+0x68. That aliasing, not a null pointer, is what leaves the arrays unpopulated.

entries.claim: seed_missing_functions.py --apply silently discards the manual edits in recomp_seed.c, and manual_edits.py apply can duplicate a region of a file it repairs
entries.evidence: Two separate tool defects, both found by losing work to them today. (1) Regenerating recomp_seed.c dropped all 4 manual-edit records targeting that file, including ledger #136's carry-flag fix at sub_001FBA90. manual_edits.py VERIFY still reported 1095/1095 'would place', because 'would place' means placeable, not present - so the loss was invisible and the 582-kernel-call baseline recorded in progress entry 191 was measured on a tree missing those 4 edits. Running manual_edits.py apply afterwards is mandatory, not optional. (2) That apply then wrote two copies of sub_001EA600, sub_001EA640 and sub_001EA6B0 into recomp_0014.c - 309 duplicated lines, with the first copy a hybrid carrying sub_001EA5E0-family labels (loc_001EA5EF) inside sub_001EA6B0's body. Duplicate definitions in one translation unit do not compile, so this is caught at build time rather than silently, but it destroys the original. Detected by counting 'void sub_XXXX(void)' headers per file, and repaired by keeping the copy whose every loc_ label lies inside the function's own address range - a check worth making standard. Finally: no snapshot had been taken since 7 August, so the pre-regeneration recomp_seed.c is unrecoverable. snapshot.py exists precisely for this and was not used.

entries.claim: Six of the fourteen metaobjects have a _metaFields aliasing another object's field array
entries.evidence: REFUTED by ledger #115, which already settled the framing months earlier and which a ledger check surfaced before any build was spent on it. The pattern 'container == owner + 0x68' holds for 8 of the 14 not because the container is an embedded sub-object but because 0x68 is the ALLOCATION STRIDE of this 0x64-byte class - consecutive blocks from the bump allocator. The other 6 simply had their containers allocated at a different time, so the coincidence does not hold for them. Nothing is aliased and nothing is supposed to set MEM32(this+0x28) = this+0x68; the real store is MEM32(esi+0x28) = sub_00222600(0) inside factory sub_00222708, and #115 measured it succeeding on every object that goes through it. My reading in #162 repeated #114's withdrawn 'embedded sub-object at +0x68' error. The probe evidence behind #162 stands - all 14 do have real containers and real arrays - only the aliasing interpretation of it is wrong.

entries.claim: The field arrays are never populated because sub_00208645 - the append itself - is an unresolved stub, and skipping it also leaks the 16 bytes ledger #84 measured
entries.evidence: Traced by probe, not inference. (1) The search in sub_0021E970 SUCCEEDS: [SEARCH] want=01097C00 cont=01098B80 arr=01098D70 n=00000017, and [ELEM] found it at index 0x0D of 23. So the container is not empty and the first call is clean - [CALL1] idx=0000000D obj=01098FA8. (2) The SECOND call is not: [CALL2] idx=FFFFFFFF obj=00000000, and [AT414] showed outer=01098FA8, which is the OBJECT from pass 1, where the manager 01098D08 belongs. edi had been clobbered between the two calls. (3) Bracketing the first call: [PRE] edi=01098D08 esp=00F7F6C4 esi=01098FA8 ebp=0000000D / [POST] edi=01098FA8 esp=00F7F6B4 esi=00000000. esp is 0x10 LOWER after a call that should leave it unchanged - a 16-byte leak - and edi comes back holding esi's saved value, the signature of an epilogue popping from the wrong depth. walk_chain.py reported the tail-call chain BALANCED for edi, so it was stack depth, not a missing pop. (4) Localised with seven esp probes down the chain: E6 (before sub_00208600) = 00F7F6AC, E7 (after) = 00F7F69C. sub_00208600 is the leaker. (5) Its recompiled extent is only 0x00208600-0x0020860F; the real function runs to its 'ret 8' at 0x00208642, and the 'jl 0x208645' branch target sub_00208645 is defined in recomp_stubs_unresolved.c as { g_esp += 4; }. The original at 0x00208645 is: mov edx,[edi+8] / mov eax,[esp+0x10] / pop edi / mov [edx+esi*4],eax / pop esi / ret 8 - the ARRAY STORE, plus 8 bytes of register restore and an 8-byte argument purge. 8 + 8 = the 16 missing bytes exactly, and skipping the store is why the field array never grows. This is the same 16-byte leak ledger #84 measured and could not place. FIXED by seeding 0x00208645 (15 bytes, extent inside sub_00208600, so a seed and not an inline per ledger #158). MEASURED, deterministic 2 of 2: heap 96 -> 136, reached VAs 170 -> 196, call sites 477 -> 551, kernel calls unchanged at 230. Both reached and call sites are new bests. Wall moves to sub_0020E547+0x1C3 reading 0xFFFE00CC.

entries.claim: manual_edits.py apply duplicates the same three functions on every run, so a regeneration needs a fixed repair sequence
entries.evidence: Reproduced deterministically: two separate apply runs this session each wrote a second copy of sub_001EA600, sub_001EA640 and sub_001EA6B0 into recomp_0014.c. Repairing it by hand twice triggered rule #4, so tools_data/dedupe_functions.py now does it: it scores each copy by how many of its loc_ labels fall outside the address range in its own Original: header, keeps a copy that scores zero, and refuses when no copy is clean. The hybrid sub_001EA6B0 scores 5 - it carries loc_001EA5EF, which belongs to sub_001EA5E0. Has a --self-test. THE SEQUENCE after any seed_missing_functions.py --apply, because each step exposes the next: (1) neuter_seed.py to re-disable known-bad seeds, which the regeneration resurrects; (2) manual_edits.py apply, because the seeder discards recomp_seed.c's hand edits and verify cannot tell present from placeable; (3) dedupe_functions.py --apply; (4) stub_overridden.py --apply, because the seeder does not remove the recomp_stubs_unresolved.c body it supersedes and the link fails with LNK2005; (5) strip_probes.py; (6) snapshot.py. Also found: the seeder drops any function neuter_seed.py has renamed to <sym>__seeded, since the carry-forward scan does not recognise the renamed body - which silently removed sub_001995AD, sub_0020B8C6 and sub_0020B88D this run. That is the desired outcome for those three bad seeds, but it is luck, not design, and their moved-to records had to be deleted and their plain stubs restored by hand.

entries.claim: Full-project audit 2026-09-03: current progress is real and reproducible, and four unresolved stubs are entered on every run
entries.evidence: PRESERVED FIRST: both mirrored repos confirmed pushed, the two with no remote bundled to recomp-snapshots/repo-bundles/, pre-audit snapshot taken. VERIFIED REAL: rebuilt from source and ran twice - 230 kernel / 136 heap / 292 failed icalls / 196 reached / 551 call sites, identical both runs. 196 and 551 exceed every figure anywhere in the 193-entry history, whose previous highs are 170 and 481. All 1093 recorded manual edits are physically present, tested by exact block text rather than by the tool's own report, with zero groups short. Seeds intact at 1656 of 1656 with bodies and no duplicate definitions. NOT A LOST HIGH-WATER MARK: the 2026-08-09 figures of 4000 kernel calls and 826 heap allocations are a runaway - entry #143 documents the change that ended them as removing the page-zero junk dispatch - so today's numbers are not a regression against them. FOUR STUBS ENTERED EVERY RUN, from a fresh census of all 2122: 0x001995AD (ledger #158, seeding refuted, no fix path), 0x0020B8C6 (ledger #159, inline fix written and held), 0x00340F24 (seeder refuses it, no terminating ret found), and 0x0006702C which is NEW and was not in the earlier census because the paths had not opened yet. 0x0006702C's shape is the same class as today's win: dec eax / mov [ecx+eax*4+0x644], edx / inc edx / cmp edx, 0x64 / jl 0x67000 / pop edi - an array store, a hundred-iteration loop, and a register restore. NINE OPEN ITEMS written up as an isolatable worklist in docs/REGRESSIONS.md, the two most consequential being that progress.py neither records nor gates on 'reached', the signal signals.py calls the only one with any resolution, and that manual_edits.py verify reports placeable as though it were present - which is how four edits were silently lost earlier today. Tree restored after the census and re-verified identical at 230/136/292/196/551.

entries.claim: 0x0006702C is a single dec eax whose absence empties a 100-entry table and leaks 12 bytes of stack, but restoring it regresses every signal
entries.evidence: IDENTIFIED. 0x0006702C is ONE BYTE - opcode 0x48, dec eax - falling straight into 0x0006702D. Its enclosing function is 0x00066FE0-0x0006703C: push esi / xor esi,esi / push edi / zero three fields at ecx+0x7D8, +0x7DC, +0x7E0 / xor edx,edx / jmp 0x67000, then a loop that fills a 100-entry table at MEM32(ecx + eax*4 + 0x644) with sequential values. WHY ONE BYTE MATTERED. The jl at 0x0006701D is the NORMAL path, taken on 99 of the 100 iterations; the fall-through at loc_0006701F is only the wrap case that resets the index to 0x63. Because sub_0006702C is an unresolved stub whose whole body is g_esp += 4, taking it returned from the entire function on the first iteration - so the table was never filled, and the caller was left 12 bytes deep because the two prologue pushes and the return address that loc_0006703A in sub_0006702D pops were never popped. sub_0006702D itself is already seeded and complete: the store, the loop back to sub_00067000, and the epilogue. Only the decrement was missing. THE FIX IS ONE LINE and needs no seeding, because sub_0006702D already exists - in sub_00067000, replace the generated jl with: if (CMP_L(eax, 0x64)) { eax--; g_seh_ebp = ebp; sub_0006702D(); return; } MEASURED AND REVERTED, deterministic 2 of 2 both ways. With the fix: kernel calls 230 -> 60, heap 136 -> 91, reached 196 -> 175, call sites 551 -> 489, failed icalls 292 -> 513, indirect dispatches 44941 -> 128. Every tracked signal moved the wrong way, so rule #1 applies and it is reverted. The boot then dies somewhere entirely different - sub_0020F860+0x274F reading 0xFC015AD8, under sub_00211530 and sub_001EC600 - rather than at the previous wall. THIRD instance of a faithful fix that a broken stub was load-bearing for, after ledger #159 and the field-container fix in #162. The pattern is now established enough to expect: an empty table read as empty is survivable, and a table filled with real indices sends execution down paths that have their own defects. Baseline restored and re-verified at 230/136/292/196/551.

entries.claim: R3, R4 and R6 all reduce to one defect: sub_001F7930 is called with this = NULL, and mapped page zero fabricates a field array from it
entries.evidence: FOLLOWED THE FAULT TO ITS CAUSE. With R3 applied the boot dies at sub_001F7930+0x1E5 reading 0xFE000064, a KERNEL THUNK address. Two probes at the field walk - one on the outer object and container, one on each element and its vtable - show the transition exactly. Healthy: outer=01099148 cont=010991B0 arr=01099238, elements 01097DA0/01097DD8/01099428 with real vtables 003F7AB0 and 003F7F90. Then: outer=00000000 cont=00000000 arr=01098F88. The outer is NULL, so MEM32(0+0x28) reads page zero as 0 and MEM32(0+8) yields the stale word 01098F88, which becomes the array base. The walk then fabricates elements 0,0,0,0,0,00000681,003F7AB0 and finally elem=00000001 vt=FE000000, and MEM32(1) read as a vtable gives a kernel thunk, so the dispatch at +0x64 faults at 0xFE000064. Nothing is corrupt - page zero is simply being read as an object. ATTRIBUTION, measured. R3 alone and R3+R4 are byte-identical at 48/96/4/169/437, so R3 accounts for the whole change; R4 contributes nothing on this boot. R4 ALONE is 248/87/435/143/433 - kernel calls UP from 230 but reached DOWN from 196 and call sites down from 551, so it is a regression on the signal signals.py gates first. Both reverted; baseline restored and re-verified twice at 230/136/292/196/551. R6 IS MISCLASSIFIED and must not be seeded. 0x00340F24 is __report_gsfailure: push 8 / push 0x430848 / call 0x3432A8 / call 0x345B7F / or [ebp-4],-1 / push 3 / call 0x3428C6 / int3. It is reached from 0x00340F5D, the failure arm of __security_check_cookie at 0x00340F54 (cmp ecx, MEM32(0x47A050) / jne / ret). So the stack cookie check is FAILING and the stub is swallowing the abort. The cookie global IS written, by two stores in recomp_0025.c, so the open question is whether that initialiser runs before the checks do. Seeding this would make the process abort by design and is the wrong action. THE COMMON CAUSE. Ledger #115 recorded that every call to sub_001F7930 comes from sub_002235D0 with ecx = esi cached from sub_002226E0's return, and that the ALT path of sub_002226E0 - taken once the guard byte at MEM32(0x5BC508) flips 0 to 1 - returned eax=00000000 as its FIRST result. That NULL is this NULL. sub_002226E0's alt path, through sub_00209650(0x2221E0) and sub_0020E520 on MEM32(0x5BC274), is the single next target, and it is what R3 has been blocked on all along.

entries.claim: seed_missing_functions.py overshoots a continuation's extent because it scans to a ret without stopping at the next known function start
entries.evidence: CORRECTS THE REASONING IN LEDGER #158, though not its conclusion. #158 rejected seeding 0x001995AD partly on the grounds that its enclosing function sub_001994F0 is only 41 bytes. That is the RECOMPILER's extent, not the truth: MSVC pads with int3, and the real function runs 0x001994F0-0x00199862, 882 bytes. The recompiler truncated it at the first ret at 0x00199516. The genuine gap is 0x001995AD-0x0019961A, 109 bytes, because sub_00199519 ends exactly at 0x001995AD and the next known function starts at 0x0019961A. The seeder gave it 693 bytes reaching 0x00199862, sailing through the end of the gap and into a neighbour, because function_extent walks to the last ret no forward branch jumps past - correct for a whole function, wrong for a continuation. FIXED: the extent is now bounded by the next known function start. The bound set is kept SEPARATE from the 'starts' set, which filters which addresses get seeded, because adding to that would silently change what the tool seeds; and it unions in seed_list.json, since previously seeded continuations are real function starts that functions.json does not contain - without them the bound overshot straight into one. Verified: the same command now reports 0x001995AD-0x0019961A, 109 bytes. #158's CONCLUSION still stands on new evidence: seeded with the correct 109-byte extent, sub_001995AD still measures 248/87/435/143/433 against a 230/136/292/196/551 baseline - kernel up, reached and call sites down. It is harmful for the load-bearing reason, not the extent reason.

entries.claim: The NULL this is a correctly-refused abstract type whose NULL gets CACHED at 0x5BC218, and it does not come from sub_002226E0's alt path
entries.evidence: FULL CHAIN, every step by probe. (1) sub_0020E520 returns NULL only ONCE per boot, from a real object: NULLRET this=010977C0 flag1A=01 vt=003F5D88. That return is FAITHFUL - the original at 0x0020E53B is cmp byte [esi+0x1A],1 / jne 0x20E547 / xor eax,eax / ret 4, an explicit refusal to instantiate. (2) THE FLAG IS SET DELIBERATELY. Probing both writers of +0x1A: the constructor sub_00216EE0 writes 00, then the registrar sub_002235D0 overwrites with 01 - W16EE0 obj=010977C0 wrote=00 then W235D0 obj=010977C0 wrote=01. Its source is MEM8(esp + 0x11C), a stack argument to sub_002235D0, i.e. a registration parameter. It writes 01 for 010977C0 and 01097858 and 00 for 01091AB0, 01096BB8, 01097518 and 01097728, so this is a per-type declaration, not corruption. The type is abstract. (3) NO CHAIN WALK IS INVOLVED. CH0 shows enter this=010977C0 fwd=00000000, so the +0x3C forwarder loop never runs; esi at the NULL equals ecx at entry. (4) CORRECTS LEDGER #115's ATTRIBUTION. recomp_where on the NULL resolves the caller as sub_00213740+0x2D4, NOT sub_002226E0's alt path. sub_00213740 passes ecx = MEM32(0x5BC214). #115's claim that the alt path supplies this NULL is stale for the current tree. (5) THE CALLER HANDLES IT, AND THAT IS THE PROBLEM. The original at 0x00213787 is: call 0x20E520 / test eax,eax / mov [0x5BC218],eax / je 0x2137EC. So it checks the NULL correctly - and CACHES it. sub_00213740 is a lazy singleton getter, and every later reader of 0x5BC218 gets NULL. That is the NULL that reaches sub_001F7930 as its 'this', where mapped page zero then fabricates a field array from MEM32(0+8) and the walk invents elements until one dispatches through 0xFE000000. (6) THE OPEN QUESTION IS NARROW: why does MEM32(0x5BC214) hold an ABSTRACT type. Nothing in the tree writes it - grep for MEM32(0x5BC214) = finds zero writers - yet it holds heap object 010977C0 at runtime, so it is written through a computed address, or by code reachable only via a data pointer and therefore never translated. That last class has produced the active wall three times before. Baseline unchanged and re-verified twice at 230/136/292/196/551.

entries.claim: The current wall is sub_002219A0 pushing the small integer 2 where an allocator pointer belongs, and the guard meant to catch it is dead code
entries.evidence: TRACED IN THREE PROBES. (1) A probe at loc_0020E56D printing the allocator and its vtable shows 83 healthy calls - alloc=01088A90 vt=003F4770 - then one fatal call with alloc=00000002 vt=FFFE0000. MEM32(2) reads mapped page zero as 0xFFFE0000, and MEM32(0xFFFE0000 + 0xCC) is the reported fault address 0xFFFE00CC. Small integer where a pointer belongs is ledger #149's signature. (2) WHICH PATH SUPPLIES IT. Probes on both candidate producers - the return of sub_001E9B80 at loc_0020E561 and the return of sub_001F5C20 - fired ZERO times on the fatal call, so neither produces it. The value arrives on the direct path: eax = MEM32(esp + 8), the ARGUMENT. (3) THE GUARD IS DEAD CODE. sub_0020E547 reads the argument and the GENERATED line tests it first: if (TEST_NZ(eax, eax)) goto loc_0020E56D. The manual plausible-pointer guard sits immediately AFTER that line with the same condition plus a heap-range test, so for any non-zero eax the generated line has already jumped and the guard never executes. Its own comment says 'keep the plausible-pointer guard too' for exactly this eax=-1 case; it has never been in force. Insert-only placement is what did it - the guard needed to precede the line it constrains, not follow it. (4) THE CALLER. recomp_where on the argument resolves call #84 of 84 as sub_002219A0+0x839, under sub_00209470 and sub_0021DE80. So sub_002219A0 pushes 2 where an allocator pointer belongs. That is the single next target. NOT FIXED - the dead guard is a diagnostic bypass and enabling it would change behaviour without addressing the cause, so it is recorded rather than switched on. Baseline unchanged, re-verified twice at 230/136/292/196/551.

entries.claim: sub_00209650 returns with esp 16 bytes TOO HIGH, and that over-pop is what turns a valid allocator pointer into the integer 2 at the current wall
entries.evidence: TRACED UPWARDS IN FOUR PROBES, each one eliminating a candidate. (1) At the wall, sub_0020E547 sees alloc=00000002 on call 84 of 84 after 83 healthy alloc=01088A90. (2) The 2 is not produced inside that function - probes on the returns of sub_001E9B80 and sub_001F5C20 fired ZERO times on the fatal call - so it arrives as the argument, from sub_002219A0+0x839 per recomp_where. (3) sub_002219A0 does not originate it either: it FORWARDS, doing push 0x221900 / call 0x209650 / mov ecx,[esp+8] / add esp,4 / push ecx. And the value pushed to it is sound - a probe on the producing virtual call [obj+0x58] in sub_00209470 fired 92 times and returned 01088A90 EVERY time, never 2. So the pointer is correct when pushed and wrong when read. (4) THE STACK IS THE CULPRIT. Bracketing sub_002219A0's call to sub_00209650 across two nested invocations: inner A1 pre esp=00F7F98C -> A2 post esp=00F7F988, which is pre-4 and correct for this cdecl call. Outer A1 pre esp=00F7F9D8 -> A2 post esp=00F7F9E4, which is pre+12, i.e. 16 bytes HIGHER than it should be. sub_00209650 over-pops 16 bytes on the outer invocation, so MEM32(esp + 8) reads a slot past the argument and picks up 2. This is an OVER-pop, the opposite sign to the leaks in ledger #84 and #145, and it is consistent with the ABI checker already reporting sub_00209650 did not restore ebx/esi/edi. The 16 bytes and the nesting both matter: the outer call contains the inner sub_002219A0 invocation, so the damage happens somewhere in that deeper chain rather than in sub_00209650's own prologue. NEXT: bracket esp inside sub_00209650 across its own callees to find which one over-pops. Also swept for the ledger #172 dead-guard class across the whole tree: exactly ONE instance, the one already found in sub_0020E547, so every other manual guard is live and the ten diagnostic bypasses are real. Baseline unchanged, re-verified twice at 230/136/292/196/551.

entries.claim: The kernel-call count has been the misleading signal: the 226 to 434 jump came with ZERO extra dispatches, while today's lower 230 carries twice the work of anything before it
entries.evidence: SCANNED ALL 49 DISTINCT WALLS ACROSS 198 ENTRIES. (1) SEVEN WALLS WERE REVISITED after being left - VCRUNTIME140.dll three times across 106 entries, sub_002235D0+0xC0 three times across 54, sub_00205170+0x7D1 twice across 15, and four more that oscillated within two entries during a bisect and are noise rather than regressions. (2) FIFTEEN WALLS WERE LEFT BY A BYPASS OR AN UNCLEAR CHANGE rather than a repair, by classifying the entry that moved off each one: sub_001A0B0C, sub_001F7930+0x1FC, sub_00221F50+0x2E2, sub_001F7560+0x2F8, sub_0013AE50+0xB10, sub_0013B0E0+0x2CE, sub_001186A0+0xC7, sub_0013AE50+0x3C1, sub_0034139A+0x25A, sub_00204800+0x24D and five unclear. Those are passed in the counter and not in the code. (3) ELEVEN WALLS ARE NOT PROVEN BROKEN TODAY - they sat deeper than the 230 kernel calls the current build reaches, so whether their repairs still hold is untested: sub_00202B87+0x35E at depth 1426, sub_001EBA9E+0x1A4 at 582, sub_00209414+0x3FA, sub_00221070+0x647 and sub_001E8800+0x182 at 530, sub_001EA600+0x2C3, sub_001EB890+0x1D5 and sub_001EA6B0+0x2FB at 514, sub_002096B0+0xD5 at 434, sub_001EA5A0+0x341 at 338, sub_00205170+0x7D1 at 274. Thirty-five others sit shallower than 230 and ARE passed every run. (4) THE MISLEADING NUMBER, and this is the finding that matters. Aug 9: 226 kernel, 154 reached, 22313 dispatches. Aug 29 after seeding 512 pointers: 434 kernel, 159 reached, 22313 dispatches - the kernel count nearly DOUBLED while the dispatch count did not move by one and reached rose by five. A count rising with no more work happening is a count measuring something else. Sep 2: 578 kernel, 165 reached, 24681 dispatches. Today: 230 kernel, 196 reached, 551 call sites, 44941 dispatches - the kernel count is the lowest since August and the work is DOUBLE anything ever recorded. The mechanism is proven separately: entry #148's own words are that the wall moves off sub_001FBA90, and that is exactly where ledger #136's carry-flag fix lives - a fix a seeding run silently discards. With it absent the predicate answers yes to everything and the boot skips work while counting kernel calls; with it present the boot is at 230 both on Aug 9 and today. CONCLUSION: reached, call sites and dispatches have risen monotonically all along and are trustworthy; kernel_calls inflated between Aug 29 and Sep 2 and should not be read as depth.

entries.claim: The 16-byte over-pop is inside sub_002235D0 and is PATH-DEPENDENT: the same thunk is balanced on one invocation and over-pops on the next
entries.evidence: NARROWED FROM SIX FUNCTIONS TO ONE PATH, all by probe. (1) Bracketing sub_00209650 entry to exit showed its short-path invocations balanced at -4 and one long-path invocation exiting 16 bytes high. (2) Bracketing each step of the long path put the damage BEFORE any of it ran - esp was already wrong at loc_0020965B - so it happened in the indirect call at 0x00209651. (3) Probing that call's target and its stack effect names the culprit precisely, three dispatches from the same site: target 0021BD20 esp 00F7F9D0 -> 00F7F9CC correct, target 00221900 esp 00F7F9D0 -> 00F7F9DC sixteen bytes high, target 00222230 esp 00F7F980 -> 00F7F97C correct. (4) sub_00221900 is a plain 11-argument registration thunk and both its original and its recompiled form are balanced - 11 pushes, call, esp += 0x2C, ret - so the damage is below it. Bracketing inside it settles that AND shows the defect is path-dependent: invocation one entered at 00F7F9C8 and returned from sub_002235D0 at 00F7F9AC where 00F7F99C was due, 16 bytes high; invocation two entered at 00F7F97C and returned at 00F7F950, exactly right. Same function, same thunk, one balanced and one not. So sub_002235D0 over-pops 16 bytes on ONE of its paths. INSTRUMENT GAP, and it explains why this survived so long. RECOMP_CHECK_ABI has an esp check, but recomp_esp_escape only fires when esp leaves the SIMULATED STACK entirely - a range test against 0x00780000-0x00F80000, not a delta test. A 16-byte imbalance stays far inside that window and never trips it, so the ABI build reports 16 register violations and zero esp ones while this defect is live. A per-call delta check would have named sub_002235D0 immediately. Baseline unchanged, re-verified twice at 230/136/292/196/551.

entries.claim: Built and verified the esp delta-check instrument that ledger #175 called for; it confirms the +16 finding automatically and surfaces 167 total imbalances tree-wide
entries.evidence: RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE already receives saved_esp, the value its own failure path treats as correct - so a successful call is held to the identical invariant, checked once across all 19,239 call sites in this tree: not one is followed by a caller-side esp += N cleanup, so full callee cleanup is assumed everywhere and the invariant is exact. Added RECOMP_ICALL_ESP_DELTA (compiles to (void)0 outside RECOMP_CHECK_ABI) plus recomp_esp_delta_va, reported once per distinct target VA like its range-check sibling. FIRST ATTEMPT WAS WRONG and is worth recording: I nested a fresh #ifdef/#else/#endif inside the ALREADY-OPEN one that guards recomp_esp_escape_va/recomp_abi_violation_va/RECOMP_ICALL_WATCH, which closed that outer block early and stranded RECOMP_ICALL_WATCH's real body outside any #ifdef - the non-ABI build then saw an undeclared RECOMP_ICALL_ESP_DELTA and failed at LINK time (LNK2001), not compile time, because a bare macro that fails to expand is silently treated as a function call. Caught before commit by building the plain configuration, which is exactly the check this addition itself argues for elsewhere. Fixed by inserting the declaration and macro INSIDE the existing ifdef, and the no-op INSIDE the existing else, touching zero other structure. VERIFIED. Normal build: deterministic 2 of 2 at 230/136/292/196/551, byte-identical to baseline - the instrument is compile-time inert without RECOMP_CHECK_ABI as designed. ABI build: reports sub_00221900 delta +16 exactly, esp 00F7F9CC (expected) -> 00F7F9DC (got) - matching the hand-probed finding in ledger #175 exactly (00F7F9D0 -> 00F7F9DC there, same call, different vantage point before vs after the dummy retaddr push). 167 total ESP-DELTA reports tree-wide, not yet triaged - this is a major new surface, not a single fix, and is left for a dedicated pass rather than attempted here.

entries.claim: Of the 167 esp imbalances the ABI build reports, only 10 are over-pops; the other 157 are uncleaned cdecl arguments and are not defects.
entries.evidence: Ledger #176 recorded "167 distinct esp imbalances tree-wide, a major new surface left for a dedicated triage pass". Bucketing every [ESP-DELTA] line in src/game/abi_stderr.txt by sign shows the surface is far smaller than that number suggests. The histogram over all 167: 109 at -4, 27 at -12, 17 at -8, 1 at -16, 1 at -52, 1 at -68, 1 at -288, then 7 at +4, 1 at +12, 2 at +16. RECOMP_ICALL_ESP_DELTA captures _icall_esp before the argument pushes and compares it against g_esp after the call returns, so a cdecl callee, which never pops the caller's arguments, legitimately returns with esp below the captured value by exactly the argument bytes. That accounts for the whole negative tail, and the dominant -4 bucket is simply one-argument calls. A positive delta has no such benign reading: no calling convention leaves esp above where the caller stood before it pushed anything, so esp came back too high and the stack was over-popped. The triage surface is therefore the 10 positive lines, not 167. They are, in file order: sub_FE0000B8 +4, sub_001EC480 +4, sub_001FE770 +4, sub_001FE850 +4, sub_001E90F0 +12, sub_0035ADA0 +4, sub_FE000000 +4, sub_00213160 +4, sub_00221070 +16, sub_00221900 +16.

entries.claim: sub_002235D0 is statically stack-balanced on every path, so the 16-byte over-pop enters it from a callee rather than from a missing push or pop of its own.
entries.evidence: Ledger #175 narrowed the wall to sub_002235D0 over-popping 16 bytes on one of its paths. Reading the whole function in recomp_0016.c:21362-21723 rules out the simplest explanation, that some path reaches the epilogue without having taken the prologue's pushes. The frame is set up at line 21370 with esp = esp - 0x108, before any branch. The four callee-saved pushes of ebx, ebp, esi and edi sit at lines 21397-21400 under loc_002235FD, and every early branch out of the entry block (loc_002235DF, loc_002235E4, loc_002235ED, loc_002235EF, loc_002235F1, loc_002235FB) converges on loc_002235FD, so no path can skip them. There is exactly one epilogue and one ret, at lines 21717-21723: four pops in reverse order, then esp = esp + 0x108, then esp += 4 for the return address. Pushes and pops match, and the two 0x108 adjustments match. faithful on the function reports no findings from its three checks. A static check of its direct RECOMP_ABI_CALL callees for the convention-mismatch shape, a stdcall callee whose esp += N epilogue pops more than the call site pushed, also returns zero for this function; that checker under-counts arguments written through MEM32(esp + N) after a frame adjust rather than through PUSH32, so it is biased toward false positives and its tree-wide count of 1253 is not trustworthy, but the bias means a zero result here is a genuine negative. The over-pop therefore originates below sub_002235D0, either in a deeper callee or in an ICALL_SAFE failure path that unwinds to the wrong depth.

entries.claim: A second 16-byte over-pop exists at sub_00221070, and both +16 sites coincide with ebx, esi and edi holding stack garbage.
entries.evidence: Ledger #176 named sub_00221900 as the sole +16 site the new RECOMP_ICALL_ESP_DELTA instrument reported. There are two. src/game/abi_stderr.txt:10819 reads "[ESP-DELTA] icall to sub_00221070 returned with esp at the wrong depth: expected 00F7F880, got 00F7F890 (delta +16)", thirty lines before the recorded sub_00221900 line at 10849, and the two are the only positive-16 entries in the file. The line immediately preceding the sub_00221900 delta is "[ABI-ICALL] sub_00221900 did not restore: ebx 010986B8->624F6174 esi 010986A0->00000000 edi 010988C0->01097858". Three of the four callee-saved registers come back holding values that are not their originals, and 624F6174 is the ASCII bytes taOb, which is stack or heap text rather than any pointer. Sixteen bytes is exactly four dwords, and ebx, esi and edi are three of the four registers a matching prologue and epilogue would push and pop, so the register damage and the esp displacement are one event and not two. ebp is reported intact only because the lifter gives sub_002235D0 a local uint32_t ebp seeded from g_seh_ebp at recomp_0016.c:21364-21366, so its push and pop move that local and never touch the global the ABI checker compares. Any account of the over-pop has to explain the register clobber at the same time.

entries.claim: RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE's failure path double-unwinds arguments at the ~900 call sites that also carry caller-side cleanup, and 126 of those sites clean up exactly 16 bytes. This is the mechanism of the current wall's 16-byte over-pop.
entries.evidence:
recomp_types.h:664-667 justifies the RECOMP_ICALL_ESP_DELTA invariant with the claim "Checked across all 19,239 RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE call sites in this tree: not one is followed by a caller-side esp += N cleanup, so every site already assumes full callee cleanup and this invariant is exact, not approximate." That claim is false, and the reason it was believed is a search-string mismatch: the lifter emits cleanup as "esp = esp + N;", never as "esp += N;", so a search for the latter finds nothing. Counting the former within six lines of each of the 17,189 RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE sites in gen/recomp_00*.c returns roughly 900 sites with cleanup, the largest buckets being 272 at 8 bytes, 185 at 4, 184 at 0xC and 126 at 0x10, which is 16.

The failure paths at recomp_types.h:750, 754 and 760 all restore with g_esp = (saved_esp), and saved_esp is captured before the site's argument pushes, so the macro unwinds the arguments itself. Where the site also has caller cleanup, that cleanup then runs a second time over the same bytes and esp finishes N bytes high. The success path is unaffected, because a cdecl callee pops only the return address and leaves esp exactly N below saved_esp for the caller's cleanup to correct; that is also why the delta check reports a negative N on those sites, which is ledger #177's benign negative tail rather than a defect.

A concrete instance at recomp_0016.c:52493-52502: _icall_esp is captured at 52493, four arguments are pushed at 52494-52497 for 16 bytes, the dummy return address and the call follow at 52498, and loc_00231EB3 at 52501-52502 does esp = esp + 0x10. Success leaves _icall_esp; failure leaves _icall_esp + 16. The plain RECOMP_ICALL macro does not have this defect, because its failure paths at recomp_types.h:717 and 723 pop only the dummy return address with g_esp += 4, which is the cdecl behaviour these sites expect; the two macros simply disagree.

This accounts for every observed property of the wall. It is path-dependent on whether the indirect target resolves, which is why ledger #175 bracketed the same function balanced on one invocation and 16 high on the next. It is exactly 16 at the 0x10 sites. It leaves esp above the callee-saved slots, so the epilogue's pops read the wrong dwords, which is the ebx/esi/edi garbage recorded in ledger #179. And it is invisible to faithful, because the defect is in the macro and call-site convention rather than in the lifted instruction stream.

The repair follows the shape of an existing tool. At the sites that carry caller cleanup, the capture of _icall_esp belongs below the argument pushes rather than above them, so that a failed call leaves the arguments in place for the caller's own cleanup to remove exactly once. tools_data/find_icall_esp_saves.py --fix already performs precisely this move for callee-saved register pushes, per the manual-fix comments it leaves at recomp_0016.c:21401-21430. Not yet applied or built, so this entry is diagnosis only.

entries.claim: The double-unwind defect in ledger #180 has not been shown to fire in the run that produced the current wall; its attribution to this wall is unproven and the entry should be read as a defect class, not as the wall's cause.
entries.evidence:
Ledger #180 established, and this entry does not disturb, that RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE's failure paths double-unwind arguments at roughly 900 call sites carrying caller-side cleanup, 126 of them at exactly 16 bytes, with a worked instance at recomp_0016.c:52493-52502. What #180 additionally asserted, that this is the mechanism of the current wall, does not survive checking and is refuted here.

Three checks, all negative. First, the failure path that records its own source location is recomp_types.h:754, through recomp_icall_reject_log(_va, __FILE__, __LINE__). The run's abi_stderr.txt carries 513 [ICALL-REJECT] lines naming 14 distinct sites, 496 of them from recomp_0015.c:28087 alone. Reading the seven lines following each of those 14 sites in gen/ shows caller-side cleanup at none of them, so no logged rejection in this run landed on a cleanup site.

Second, the wall's own functions do not contain a 16-byte cleanup site. sub_00221900, which ledger #176 and #179 record returning +16, contains no RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE at all and one esp = esp + 0x2C. sub_00221070, the second +16 site from #179, has many RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE sites but its only argument cleanup is esp = esp + 4. sub_002235D0 likewise has two esp = esp + 4 sites and nothing at 0x10. A single firing of the #180 mechanism in any of these three would produce +4, not +16.

Third, the two failure paths at recomp_types.h:750 and 760 call recomp_icall_fail_log, which records no file or line, so they cannot be cross-referenced at all. Their firing count is also unrecoverable from this run: every failure path calls sub_00ICALL_SAFE_STUB, whose logging is rate-limited at recomp_manual.c:4695-4696 to the first 8 hits and then every 65536th, and the log shows exactly hits #1 through #8 with no later line. So the run proves only that total icall failures fall somewhere between 8 and 65536, which does not separate the paths.

The remaining possibility, that the wall's 16 is four separate +4 double-unwinds rather than one +16, is arithmetic without evidence and is not claimed. The cheap decisive instrument is to give the two silent failure paths the same __FILE__ and __LINE__ logging that path 754 already has; if any failure then lands on one of the ~900 cleanup sites, #180 is promoted from a defect class to this wall's cause, and if none does, the wall needs a different explanation and #180 remains a real defect worth fixing on its own account.

entries.claim: Measured: the ledger #180 double-unwind is dormant in this run. Of 27 call sites that suffer failed indirect calls, exactly one carries caller-side cleanup, at 4 bytes and firing once. No failing site cleans up 16 bytes, so #180 cannot be the source of the wall's 16-byte over-pop.
entries.evidence:
Ledger #181 left one question open and named the instrument that would settle it. That instrument now exists and has been run. Every previous icall log keys on the target VA - recomp_icall_fail_log dedups by va, and recomp_icall_reject_log keeps only the first site per va - so a site failing on an already-seen va left no trace and the question was unanswerable from the old logs. recomp_icall_failsite_log in recomp_manual.c keys on the file and line instead, reached through the RECOMP_ICALL_FAILSITE() macro added to all three RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE failure paths at recomp_types.h:779, 783 and 790, and compiling to (void)0 outside RECOMP_CHECK_ABI.

The census reports 20,337 failed indirect calls from 27 distinct sites, against only 513 VA-deduped rejects previously visible, so the old logs were hiding roughly forty times the traffic. Reading the eight lines after each of the 27 sites in gen/ for an "esp = esp + N" cleanup returns exactly one hit: recomp_0015.c:27720, cleanup of 4 bytes, count 1. The other 26 sites have no cleanup at all, so the double-unwind cannot fire there, and no failing site anywhere in the run cleans up 0x10. The single 4-byte instance is the whole live exposure of a defect class that spans roughly 900 sites, 126 of them at 16 bytes. #180 stays confirmed as a latent defect and is still worth repairing, but it is eliminated as this wall's cause, which settles #181 by measurement rather than by inference.

Two process notes. First, the instrument was wrong on its first run and printed nothing, because it registered its dump only through atexit, and neither a crash nor a watchdog kill reaches exit handlers; the crash path calls each dump explicitly from main.c, and the comment sitting directly above those calls at main.c:249-254 warns of exactly this, saying a diagnostic that only prints on the one path that does not happen is not a diagnostic. Fixed by adding recomp_icall_failsite_dump() beside recomp_icall_reject_dump() at both main.c call sites. Second, the run is deterministic: two consecutive ABI runs before the fix produced byte-identical 402,782-byte logs, which is what proved the empty output was a real zero rather than a lost run.

Behaviour-neutral, and verified so: after the change the normal build relinked and its stderr.txt is byte-identical to the previous baseline at 311,619 bytes, with reached at 196, call sites at 551 and the same fault at 0xFFFE00CC. The wall has not moved and was not expected to.

entries.claim: A per-call-site esp depth check on DIRECT calls names the wall's over-popper on its first run: sub_002235D0 called from sub_00221900 returns +20 on its first invocation where +4 is correct, and four other functions over-pop at the same time.
entries.evidence:
Ledger #176 gave indirect calls a depth check; direct calls still had only the range test against 0x00700000-0x00F80000, which a 16-byte imbalance passes untouched. That gap covered this wall exactly: recomp_0016.c:17167-17186 shows sub_00221900 pushing 11 arguments, calling sub_002235D0 through RECOMP_ABI_CALL at line 17182, then cleaning up 0x2C itself, and sub_002235D0's own indirect calls are already checked and report nothing, so the entire chain under that direct call was unmeasured.

The new check is self-calibrating, which is what makes it work without a table of calling conventions. _abi_p is captured after the dummy return-address push, so a correct call returns esp at exactly _abi_p + N where N is the callee's own epilogue constant, "esp += N; return;" - 4 for cdecl, 4 plus the argument bytes for stdcall. N is unknown at the call site but constant per callee, so the absolute delta is not checkable and its constancy is. A static inside the macro holds one slot per CALL SITE, the same pattern RECOMP_MARK_SITE already uses, so a callee reached from sites with different argument counts cannot cross-contaminate. It reports once per site and prints immediately rather than at exit, because neither a crash nor a watchdog kill reaches exit handlers.

Six drifts fired. Reading each callee's epilogue turns every one into a verdict, because the epilogue constant IS the correct delta:

sub_002235D0, epilogue esp += 4, correct +4, seen +20 then +4 at recomp_0016.c:17182 - the first invocation OVER-POPS 16. This is the wall, and it reproduces ledger #175's hand-bracketing exactly, which recorded invocation one returning 16 bytes high and invocation two returning right.
sub_00209470, epilogue esp += 12, correct +12, seen +28 then +12 at recomp_0016.c:15994 - over-pops 16.
sub_00209650, epilogue esp += 4, correct +4, seen +4 then +20 at recomp_seed.c:105189 - over-pops 16.
sub_0020E520, epilogue esp += 8, correct +8, seen +16 then +8 at recomp_0016.c:13621 - over-pops 8.
sub_00209650 again, at the different site recomp_0016.c:13614, seen +8 then +4 - over-pops 4 there.
sub_001994F0, seen +8 then -16, and this one is NOT yet a verdict. Its correct delta is +8 by the ret 4 at recomp_0011.c:13820, but its other exit at 13805 is a tail call, "sub_00199519(); return;", with no return address pushed and its four pushed registers left for the callee. sub_001994F0, sub_00199519 and sub_001995AD are continuation fragments of one original function sharing a single epilogue, so the tail-call path legitimately returns through a different frame and the checker's model of "a return" does not fit it. Treat as a possible false positive of the tail-call idiom until separately established.

Three of the five real over-pops are exactly 16, and sub_00209650 and sub_00209470 were both already named around this wall by ledger #173. Whether one deepest callee explains all of them or they are independent is not established here.

Behaviour-neutral and verified so: both configurations build clean, and the normal build's stderr.txt is byte-identical to baseline at 311,619 bytes with reached 196, call sites 551 and the same fault at 0xFFFE00CC.

entries.claim: The deepest direct-call over-popper cannot be resolved along direct edges: sub_002235D0's 16 bytes enter through an INDIRECT call, placing the origin inside a cycle with sub_00221900 and sub_00221070. A separate absolute census also found sub_001A06E8 over-popping 24 consistently, which the drift check structurally could not see.
entries.evidence:
Ledger #183's drift check only fires when one call site returns DIFFERENT depths, so a callee that over-pops CONSISTENTLY is invisible to it - the delta is simply wrong and constant. That blind spot is closed by recording the depth every executed direct call site returns at, once per site, and judging it offline in tools_data/audit_call_depth.py against the callee's own epilogue constant N from "esp += N; return;", which is the correct delta and which the call site cannot see. Only executed sites are recorded, 540 of the 55,801 in the tree, so the census is readable.

Five sites return more than the callee owns. sub_001A06E8 owns 4 and returned +28, over-popping 24, at recomp_0011.c:33416. sub_002235D0 owns 4 and returned +20, over-popping 16, at recomp_0016.c:17182. sub_00209470 owns 12 and returned +28, over-popping 16, at recomp_0016.c:15994. sub_0020E520 owns 8 and returned +16, over-popping 8, at recomp_0016.c:13621. sub_00209650 owns 4 and returned +8, over-popping 4, at recomp_0016.c:13614. A further 85 sites call functions with no epilogue in gen/, stubbed or otherwise, and are not judged.

sub_001A06E8 is the census's own find, invisible to the drift check because it is consistent, and it is the only one of the five that is an SEH function: it opens at recomp_0011.c:30347-30349 with push 0x68, push 0x3E1B58, call sub_003432A8, the __SEH_prolog idiom. Checking all five for that call returns 1 for sub_001A06E8 and 0 for the other four, so the tempting single explanation - that these are all __SEH_prolog/__SEH_epilog asymmetry - is refuted for the four that matter. sub_001A06E8's +24 is plausibly that asymmetry and is a separate thread; CLAUDE.md already records the __SEH_epilog save-area replacement as retired after three rejections, so it is not to be reopened casually.

On the wall itself the question "which callee is deepest" turns out to be malformed as asked. Ledger #178 established sub_002235D0 is statically balanced on every path, and this census shows every one of its DIRECT callees returning correctly, so its 16 bytes cannot originate in its own body or below a direct edge. They arrive through an indirect one. The icall delta check names exactly two +16 targets, sub_00221070 and sub_00221900, and those are precisely the function pointers sub_00221900 hands to sub_002235D0: recomp_0016.c:17171-17182 shows it pushing 0x221070 and 0x21EF70 among its 11 arguments before calling sub_002235D0 directly, and sub_002235D0 calls its pointer arguments back through MEM32(esp + 0x124), 0x128 and 0x138. So the damage travels a CYCLE - sub_00221900 direct to sub_002235D0, sub_002235D0 indirect to sub_00221070 and sub_00221900 - and a direct-callee graph cannot order it, because the edge carrying the 16 bytes is the indirect one the graph does not contain.

The next step follows from that and is narrow: the icall instrument already records each failing target VA, so pairing every icall delta with its CALLER closes the missing edges and makes the cycle orderable. Structural note for whoever does it: sub_00221900 is a pure 12-push forwarder with no indirect calls and one direct call, whereas sub_00221070 has 51 pushes, 8 indirect and 12 direct call sites, so sub_00221070 is where the work is.

Instrument only, no behaviour change: both configurations build clean and the normal build's stderr.txt is byte-identical to baseline at 311,619 bytes.

entries.claim: Recording the caller of each icall imbalance closes the graph and orders the chain: it is eight links deep, ends at sub_0020E520, and the +16 higher up is two independent 8-byte losses rather than one 16 propagating.
entries.evidence:
Ledger #184 named the missing edge and the one-line fix for it. recomp_esp_delta_va now takes __FILE__ and __LINE__ from RECOMP_ICALL_ESP_DELTA, so every indirect imbalance names its CALL SITE and not just its target.

Its dedup had to change too, and the first attempt got it wrong in an instructive way. The original keyed on target VA with a 32-slot table, and because it only stopped STORING when full rather than stopping reporting, every target after the 32nd printed on every call - which is where the "167 imbalances" figure came from. Re-keying on the call site cut that to 34 true distinct sites, but ALSO made the two +16 lines vanish, because a site reports the first time it is non-zero and the first anomaly at a site then suppressed every later, different one. recomp_0015.c:27720 is the proof: it reports -4 to sub_0021DB50 and +8 to sub_00220040 from the same site. Keying on site AND delta together restores both, at 39 lines. An instrument that hides the thing it was built to find is worse than none, and this one did until the third try.

With the callers recorded, every over-popping edge resolves to an owner. Direct edges from the census: sub_002219A0 to sub_00209650 +16 at recomp_seed.c:105189, sub_00221900 to sub_002235D0 +16 at recomp_0016.c:17182, sub_00221070 to sub_00209470 +16 at recomp_0016.c:15994, sub_00220040 to sub_0020E520 +8 at recomp_0016.c:13621, sub_00220040 to sub_00209650 +4 at recomp_0016.c:13614. Indirect edges, new here: sub_00209650 to sub_00221900 +16 at recomp_0015.c:28070, and sub_002235D0 to sub_00221070 +16 at recomp_0016.c:21571.

Ordered, that is a CHAIN and not the cycle #184 suspected: sub_002219A0 to sub_00209650 to (indirect) sub_00221900 to sub_002235D0 to (indirect) sub_00221070 to sub_00209470 to (indirect) sub_00220040 to sub_0020E520. The cycle reading was an artefact of having only direct edges, where sub_00221900 and sub_002235D0 appear to call each other; the indirect edges show the traffic passing through sub_00221070 and onward rather than looping back.

sub_0020E520 is the bottom. It owns 8 by its epilogue and returns +16, over-popping 8; it spans recomp_0015.c:39140-39231, contains exactly ONE call, a single RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE, and no reported imbalance of any kind falls inside it. Every frame above inherits from here.

The magnitudes say this is not one defect propagating. The bottom of the chain loses 8 and the top shows 16, so there are at least TWO independent 8-byte over-pops, and dividing 16 by a single cause was wrong. sub_00209470 is where the second appears: it inherits +8 from sub_00220040 and is seen returning +16 to sub_00221070.

Corroborates ledger #173 from a different direction, which bracketed sub_00209650 and separately found the virtual call at [obj+0x58] in sub_00209470 returning 01088A90 on all 92 healthy passes. Both functions sit on this chain. Worth noting for the repair: ledger #171 records sub_0020E520 as correctly refusing to instantiate an abstract type via cmp byte [esi+0x1A],1 / xor eax,eax, so it has an early-exit path, and an exit that does not agree with the main path about stack cleanup is the classic shape for exactly this defect.

Instrument only, no behaviour change intended; the normal build's byte-identical baseline is re-verified in the next entry alongside the commit.
